ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 11⁄2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
50 g shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and ground (minced)

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 4-6 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded
1 x Y 1 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
To serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as pumpkin, wing beans, round eggplants (aubergines), cucumber, and yard long beans

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the chili paste, pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Gradually add the lemongrass, galangal. fingerroots, and shallot and pound thoroughly until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound to a smooth paste. Set aside. Heat the coconut milk in a wok over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until the oil separates from the coconut milk. Add the chili paste and stir for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and the paste and coconut milk are mixed well Simmer for 1-2 minutes, then add the sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind and mix well until the sugar has dissolved. Add the shrimp (prawns), kaffir lime, and green chiles. Cook for another 2 minutes or until thickened. Serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables and the boiled egg.

recipes.title: Eggplant Dip with Pork
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g long green eggplants, quartered crosswise
2 hard-boiled eggs, coarsely chopped Raw or steamed vegetables, such as Chinese greens, cucumber, carrots, and yard-long beans, to serve
1 tablespoon Fried Garlic (see p. 64), to garnish
1 small handful mint leaves, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Brush a griddle or stove-top grill pan with the oil. Grill the eggplants over medium heat for 10-13 minutes, until softened and their skins are charred. Let cool, peel, and set aside.
Dry-fry the chiles in a wok or pan over medium-high heat for 15 minutes, until softened and charred. Let cool, peel, and set aside.
In the same wok, dry-fry the garlic and shallots for 5-6 minutes, until softened and lightly charred.
Bring 75 ml water to a boil in a small pan. Add the pork and blanch for 1-2 minutes, until cooked, then drain.
Pound the garlic, shallots, and shrimp paste in a mortar. Add the chiles, eggplant, pork, salt, and fish sauce and mix gently with a spoon. Fold in the chopped eggs.
Garnish with fried garlic and mint leaves and serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Spicy Tamarind Dip

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, round eggplants (aubergines), and yard-long beans, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the chili paste, finely pound the chiles, tamarind, garlic, and shallots in a mortar with a pestle. Add the shrimp paste and pound until smooth and thoroughly combined.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chili paste, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add the pork and sugar and cook for about 7 minutes or until the pork is cooked. Serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm head space, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Pork and Tomato Chili Dip
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 21⁄2 tablespoons granulated sugar raw or steamed vegetables, such as carrots, mustard greens, Chinese greens (leaves), and cucumbers, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the dried chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, and half the salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the pork and pound again until well mixed. Add the tomatoes and gently press into the mixture, then coarsely pound until combined. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the pounded tomato mixture and stir-fry for about 4 minutes or until fragrant. Add a small amount of water and season with the fish sauce, sugar, and the remaining salt. Stir until well mixed Cook for another 6-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are cooked and the dip is fully flavored.
Transfer to a bowl and garnish with the cilantro (coriander) and scallions (spring onions). Serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

lines: 8 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and finely chopped
40 g roasted peanuts rice crackers, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Finely pound the cilantro (coriander) root garlic, and peppercorns in a mortar with a pestle, then set aside.

Heat 200 ml coconut milk in a wok over low heat. Add the pounded cilantro root mixture and stir until the coconut oil separates and becomes fragrant. Add the pork and shrimp (prawns) and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until nearly cooked. Add the shallots and remaining coconut milk and stir- fry for 3-4 minutes. Season with the sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind. Add the peanuts and stir thoroughly. Serve in a bowl with rice crackers.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Dip with Rice Crackers Central 1 teaspoon chopped cilantro (coriander) root 1 clove garlic 1 teaspoon white peppercorns 350 ml coconut milk 100 g ground (minced) pork: 8 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and finely chopped 2 shallots, finely sliced 2 tablespoons granulated sugar 1 tablespoon fish sauce 2 tablespoons Tamarind Puree (see p. 63) 40 g roasted peanuts rice crackers, to serve Finely pound the cilantro (coriander) root garlic, and peppercorns in a mortar with a pestle, then set aside. recipes.title: Pickled Bamboo Shoot Dip
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 120 g pickled bamboo shoots (sour and salty version)

ingredientGroups.heading: To serve
lines: 50 g pork cracklings raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, cabbage, and lettuce

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blanch the ground (minced) pork in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute or until cooked. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the bamboo shoots in another pan of boiling water for about 2 minutes to reduce their sourness and saltiness. Drain and set aside.

Dry-fry the garlic and chiles in a wok over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, until softened and slightly burned. Transfer to a mortar and pound thoroughly. Add the bamboo shoots and pound until just before they break into small pieces. Add the blanched pork and pound coarsely until thoroughly combined. Season to taste.
Transfer to a bowl and garnish with the scallions and cilantro. Serve with the pork cracklings and raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.searchText: Pickled Bamboo Shoot Dip North 120 g ground (minced) pork 120 g pickled bamboo shoots (sour and salty version) 2-3 cloves garlic, chopped 5-7 green bird's eye chiles 3 scallions (spring onions), finely sliced 1 teaspoon chopped cilantro (coriander) salt 50 g pork cracklings raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, cabbage, and lettuce Blanch the ground (minced) pork in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute or until cooked. Dry-fry the garlic and chiles in a wok over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, until softened and slightly burned. Transfer to a mortar and pound thoroughly. Add the bamboo shoots and pound until just before they break into small pieces. Add the blanched pork and pound coarsely until thoroughly combined. Season to taste. Transfer to a bowl and garnish with the scallions and cilantro. Serve with the pork cracklings and raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Spicy Frog Dip
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 lemongrass stalks, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
100 g young tamarind leaves or sorrel leaves

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish
lines: To serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as yard-long beans, round eggplants (aubergines), and winged beans

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Dry-fry the chiles in a wok over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant and toasted, then transfer to a plate and set aside.

Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the galangal, lemongrass, fermented fish sauce, and frog meat and cook for 5 minutes or until the meat is cooked. Add the young tamarind leaves stir, and remove from the heat. Remove the frog meat with a slotted spoon and set aside. Reserve the broth (stock).

Pound the chiles in a mortar with a pestle to form fine Flakes, then add the boiled frog meat and pound coarsely. Add 2-3 tablespoons of the frog broth and the fish sauce and mix well. Transfer to a bowl and garnish with the cilantro (coriander), scallion (spring onion), and Vietnamese cilantro leaves. Serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Galangal Chili Dip
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
To serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as mushrooms, cucumber, and napa cabbage

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the broiler (grill) to high.
Crush the galangal and garlic in a mortar with a pestle, then remove and set aside.
Put the dried chiles on the broiler rack and broil for a few minutes until slightly burned. Transfer to the mortar, add the crushed galangal and garlic, and pound until thoroughly combined.
Season with the salt and serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.searchText: Galangal Chili Dip North 4 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped 3 cloves garlic 7 dried red chiles, seeded 1⁄2-1 teaspoon salt To serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as mushrooms, cucumber, and napa cabbage Preheat the broiler (grill) to high. Crush the galangal and garlic in a mortar with a pestle, then remove and set aside. Put the dried chiles on the broiler rack and broil for a few minutes until slightly burned. recipes.title: Spicy Tomato Dip
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3 kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p.378), to serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber and round eggplants (aubergines)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the broiler (grill) to medium-high, Put the tomatoes onto the broiler (grill) rack and grill (broil) for 5-6 minutes until softened and the skins are charred.

Dry-fry the lemongrass, chiles, shallots, galangal, and garlic in a wok over medium heat for 4-5 minutes until fragrant and lightly toasted. Transfer to a mortar and pound with a pestle until smooth. Add the broiled (grilled) tomatoes and gently press with the pestle until combined. Add the fermented fish flesh, tamarind, lime juice, and kaffir lime leaves and stir until well mixed. Serve in a bowl with rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Tomato Dip Northeast 2 tomatoes 2 lemongrass stalks, finely sliced 5 red bird's eye chiles, sliced 2 shallots, finely sliced 2 thin slices galangal, chopped 3 cloves garlic, chopped 1 tablespoon fermented snakehead fish flesh 1 teaspoon Tamarind Puree (see p. 63) 1 teaspoon lime juice 3 kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p.378), to serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber and round eggplants (aubergines) Heat the broiler (grill) to medium-high, Put the tomatoes onto the broiler (grill) rack and grill (broil) for 5-6 minutes until softened and the skins are charred. Dry-fry the lemongrass, chiles, shallots, galangal, and garlic in a wok over medium heat for 4-5 minutes until fragrant and lightly toasted. Transfer to a mortar and pound with a pestle until smooth. Add the broiled (grilled) tomatoes and gently press with the pestle until combined. Add the fermented fish flesh, tamarind, lime juice, and kaffir lime leaves and stir until well mixed. Serve in a bowl with rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Roasted Chili Dip
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 50 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
5 bitter orange leaves, coarsely sliced, to garnish Raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber and round eggplants (aubergines), to serve

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 1 x 10 cm piece red galangal, peeled and finely chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain.
Pound the chiles, garlic, shallots, lemongrass, red galangal, and cardamom leaves in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the dried shrimp and shrimp paste and pound again until combined.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a wok over medium heat and boil for 4-5 minutes, until it develops a grainy texture.
Add the chili paste, sugar, salt, and kaffir lime leaves and simmer for 3-4 minutes. Transfer to a bowl, garnish with the bitter orange leaves, and serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.searchText: Roasted Chili Dip Central 475 ml coconut milk 50 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 2 teaspoons salt 5 kaffir lime leaves, chopped 5 bitter orange leaves, coarsely sliced, to garnish Raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber and round eggplants (aubergines), to serve 50 g dried red chiles, seeded 2 garlic bulbs, cloves separated 5 shallots, chopped 100 g finely chopped lemongrass 1 x 10 cm piece red galangal, peeled and finely chopped 10 g bastard cardamom leaves 100 g dried shrimp 60 g shrimp paste For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain. recipes.title: Spicy Green Mango Dip
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
80 g shredded unripe green (sour) mango or green apple, plus extra to garnish
1 tablespoon lime juice Raw vegetables, such as cauliflower and cucumber, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Add the sugar and shrimp paste and continue to pound until combined.
Add the mango or apple, dried shrimp, fish sauce, lime juice, and 2 tablespoons warm water and gently mix.
Garnish with shredded mango or apple and serve with raw vegetables.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Green Mango Dip Central 5-10 green bird's eye chiles, chopped 3 cloves garlic, chopped 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 2 teaspoons Roasted Shrimp Paste (see p. 38) 80 g shredded unripe green (sour) mango or green apple, plus extra to garnish 2 tablespoons dried shrimp, coarsely pounded 21⁄2 teaspoons fish sauce 1 tablespoon lime juice Raw vegetables, such as cauliflower and cucumber, to serve Pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. recipes.title: Spicy Salacca Dip
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
60 ml fish sauce raw or steamed vegetables, such as carrots and cucumber to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the garlic, shallots, chiles, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle. Add the snake fruit and pound again until combined. Add the sugar, and fish sauce, and mix well. Serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Salacca Dip Central 8 cloves garlic, chopped 3 shallots, chopped 10 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped 2 tablespoons shrimp paste 6 salacca (snake fruit), peeled and pitted 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 60 ml fish sauce raw or steamed vegetables, such as carrots and cucumber to serve Pound the garlic, shallots, chiles, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle. recipes.title: Seafood Dipping Sauce
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 red and green bird's eye chiles
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 tablespoons lime juice Broiled (grilled) or steamed seafood, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the garlic in a mortar with a pestle, add the chiles, and pound into fine pieces.
Add the cilantro and pound until smooth.
Add the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, and 1 tablespoon water and stir with a spoon until the sugar has dissolved. The sauce should be sweet, sour, salty, and hot.
Serve with broiled or steamed seafood. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace, cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.searchText: Seafood Dipping Sauce South 6-7 cloves garlic 10 red and green bird's eye chiles 20 g coarsely chopped cilantro (coriander) 3 tablespoons fish sauce 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 2 tablespoons lime juice Broiled (grilled) or steamed seafood, to serve Pound the garlic in a mortar with a pestle, add the chiles, and pound into fine pieces. recipes.title: Shrimp Paste Dipping Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 x 2 cm piece fingerroot, peeled and julienned
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
4 kaffir lime leaves, torn Raw or steamed vegetables, such as carrots, napa cabbage, cucumbers, and yard-long beans, to serve

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish
lines: 1 red bird's eye chile, seeded and finely sliced lengthwise

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the curry paste with the lemongrass, fingerroot, shallot, shrimp paste, and salted mackerel in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the pounded paste, and stir-fry for about 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and stir continuously until thickened.
Add the sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind to taste and stir until thoroughly combined.
Add the crushed chiles and kaffir lime leaves, stir, and remove from the heat.
Transfer to a bowl, garnish with the green chile, cilantro sprig, and sliced red chile, and serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

120 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumbers, round eggplants (aubergines), and yard-long beans, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the garlic, chiles, and peanuts in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Season with the lemon juice, fish sauce, and sugar. Serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Sweet Chili Dipping Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 tablespoons peanuts, coarsely chopped (optional) Grilled Chicken or Fried Spring Rolls, to serve (see p. 276 and p. 95)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the vinegar, sugar, salt, 4 tablespoons water, and the chile in a pan. Bring to a boil and boil for 2 minutes. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 3-5 minutes, or until syrupy. Remove from the heat and cool.
Garnish with the peanuts, if using, and serve immediately. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace. Cool, cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Thai-Style Satay Sauce
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the curry paste and sauté for 30 seconds, or until it sizzles and becomes fragrant.
Gradually add the coconut milk, stir, and boil for 2-3 minutes. Add the peanuts, sugar, salt, and tamarind and stir for 3-4 minutes. Remove from the heat, transfer to a bowl, and serve.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the garlic and chiles together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Transfer to a bowl, add the fish sauce and lime juice, and mix until thoroughly combined. Serve with grilled meat or fish.

1 scallion (spring onion), finely sliced grilled meat, to serve

steps: Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, tamarind puree, sugar, and chili flakes in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.

Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace. Cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 2-3 weeks.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the pandan leaves and 475 ml water into a food processor and blend. Pour the mixture through a fine strainer (sieve) or cheesecloth (muslin) into a bowl Use the extract immediately. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1⁄2 inch (1 cm) head space, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up 1o 1-2 weeks.

2 hard-boiled eggs, cut into quarters, to garnish raw or steamed vegetables, such as yard long beans, cucumber, and ferns, to serve

Season with the lemon juice and fish sauce, sprinkle with the shallots, and mix well until combined. Transfer to a bowl, season to taste, and garnish with the boiled eggs. recipes.title: Tamarind Puree

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix 475 ml Warm water with the tamarind pods in a large bowl, then knead together by hand. Strain the mixture through cheesecloth (muslin) into a large bowl. Use immediately,. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1⁄2 inch (1 cm) head space, let cool, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the garlic, and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until golden brown. Remove from the heat, drain the garlic, and pat dry on kitchen paper. Use as an ingredient or a garnish.

lines: 5 shallots, peeled and finely sliced lengthwise

steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the shallots, and stir-fry for 10-11 minutes until golden brown. Remove from the heat, drain the shallots, and pat dry on kitchen paper. Use as an ingredient or a garnish.

recipes.searchText: Fried Shallots Central 350 ml vegetable oil 5 shallots, peeled and finely sliced lengthwise Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the shallots, and stir-fry for 10-11 minutes until golden brown. recipes.title: Ground Toasted Rice
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Dry-fry the rice in a wok over medium heat for about 8-10 minutes, stirring continuously, until golden brown and fragrant. Let cool, then pound in a mortar with a pestle until a fine powder: Use immediately. Alternatively, transfer to an airtight container and store for up to 1-2 months.

recipes.title: Deep-Fried Tofu with Dipping Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g tofu, cut into triangles 5 cm long and 1 cm thick

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dipping sauce
lines: 2 red bird's eye chiles, coarsely pounded

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the sauce, put the vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small pan and mix until combined. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then remove from the heat and set aside. Add the chiles and mix well, then add the peanuts and transfer to a small serving bowl.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the tofu for 10 minutes, or until crisp and golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Roasted Fermented Soybean Dip
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3 red and green long chiles, chopped
120 g chopped dill (optional) Glutinous Rice (see p. 378), to serve

steps: Pound the shallots, lemongrass, chiles, and galangal in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Pour in the beaten eggs, add the fermented soybeans with the dill, if using, and stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes until the eggs are cooked. Serve with rice.

Pour in the beaten eggs, add the fermented soybeans with the dill, if using, and stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes until the eggs are cooked. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Old-Style Rice Crust
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put a wok or a pan over medium heat, add the oil, and spread across the pan, making sure that the inside surfaces are fully coated. Gradually move the wok around to let the rice cook evenly for 20-25 minutes until the rice becomes golden brown and crispy. ingredientGroups.heading: For the spicy paste
lines: 200 g fermented fish, rinsed and ground (minced)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak several 12-15 cm bamboo skewers in cold water for 30 minutes. Prepare a charcoal grill with white-hot coals, or heat a gas grill to 190°C.
Whisk the eggs and salt together in a small bowl.
Shape the glutinous rice into oval patties, thread them onto the soaked skewers, and grill for 4-5 minutes on each side, until crisp.
Brush one side with the egg mixture and grill for 1-2 minutes, until the egg dries. Turn and repeat on the other side. Repeat 5-6 times to build a thick, crisp egg coating.
For the spicy paste, cook the garlic, shallots, galangal, lemongrass, chile flakes, and kaffir lime leaves in a pan over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a mortar and pound thoroughly. Add the fermented fish and mix well, then season with the lime juice.
Serve the grilled rice with the spicy paste.

recipes.title: Basic Puff Pastry
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the outer pastry, sift the flour into a large bowl. Dissolve the sugar and salt in 150 ml cold water and add to the flour. Add the vegetable oil and butter and knead until a dough forms. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, to make the inner pastry, sift the flour into another large bowl, add the oil, and knead until a dough forms.
Divide the inner and outer doughs into 20 small pieces.
On a lightly dusted work surface, roll the outer dough balls into rectangles. Put an inner dough ball in the middle of each and cover it with the outer layer.

Lightly dust the work surface again. Roll each dough ball into a 12-15 cm rectangle, working from the middle toward the top and bottom. Roll it into a tube and place it lengthwise on the work surface.
Roll each tube into another rectangle 18-20 cm long, again working from the middle toward the ends. Roll it tightly into a tube and cut it in half.
Place each half vertically on the work surface, press down with a rolling pin, and roll into a thin, flat disk. The pastry is now ready to use.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat add the cilantro (coriander) root, garlic, and white peppercorns, and sauté for 30 seconds. Add the diced chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes. Add the curry powder, onions, potatoes, soy sauce, sugar, salt, and a little water and stir-fry for another 3-4 minutes until the potatoes have softened and are cooked. Let cool.

Place the filling on the pastry disks, brush the edges of the pastry with a little water, and fold the bottom edge of the pastry over to enclose the filling. Press down to seal, then crimp the edge. Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the pastry packages in batches for 8-10 minutes or until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve.

steps: Prepare the banana-leaf cups. For each cup, place 2 banana leaf circles back to back with the shiny surface face outward on both sides. steps: Break the eggs into a bowl and add half the salt. Beat with a fork and set aside.
For the stuffing, heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the ground pork and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.

Add the onions, carrot, tomato, and chiles and stir-fry for another minute. Add 2-3 tablespoons water, then season with the sugar, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and remaining salt. Stir for 1-2 minutes, add the pineapple, and stir-fry for 1 minute. Set aside.

For the omelet, heat another wok over medium heat, add the remaining 11⁄2 tablespoons oil, and roll the oil around the wok. Reduce the heat to low, then add the beaten eggs. Spoon the stuffing into the center of the omelet. Fold the bottom edge up, fold the left and right sides into the middle, and finish by folding the top side down to create a square package.

Place a serving plate upside down over the package, press firmly, and carefully turn the wok upside down to transfer the omelet to the plate. Cut across the middle of the omelet and serve with cucumber slices.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the sauce, mix the chili sauce, sugar, salt, vinegar, and 1-2 tablespoons water together in a pan over low heat. Heat for 1 minute or until the mixture starts to boil, then remove from the heat and let cool.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the fish into a food processor and process until it is a fine, smooth texture, then transfer to a large bowl. Add the black pepper, salt, and flour and knead with your hands for 5-10 minutes. While kneading, slowly add the ice cubes until the texture is sticky and firm.

Using a spoon, shape the fish mixture into sma 1 cm-diameter balls and soak in a bowl of warm water (about 110-120°F/45-50°C) for 30 minutes. To harden the fish balls, maintain the water temperature by refreshing it with warm water as needed.
Fill a large bowl with ice-cold water. Set aside.

Bring a medium pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the fish balls and cook for 5 minutes until they float to the surface. Remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to the bowl of ice-cold water. Transfer to an airtight container and store in the refrigerator for up to 1-2 weeks or freeze for a up to a month.

recipes.title: Taro Pyramids
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dough
lines: 50 g wheat starch, plus extra for dusting

ingredientGroups.heading: For the batter
lines: 50 g wheat starch, plus extra for dusting
120 ml limewater (see p. 509) or club soda (soda water)

ingredientGroups.heading: For the filling
lines: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus extra for deep-frying

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the dough, steam the taro for about 30 minutes or until cooked. Drain and grind or pound in a mortar with a pestle until smooth, then let cool. When cool, put the taro in a large bowl, add the wheat starch and coconut cream, and mix until thoroughly combined.

For the batter, mix the wheat starch, rice flour, salt, sugar, and egg in a bowl. Gradually add the limewater or club soda (soda water) and 175 ml water, a small amount at a time. Mix until no lumps are left. Set aside. For the filling, pound the garlic, cilantro (coriander) root, and pepper in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the pounded paste, and stir- fry for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the pork, shrimp, and mushrooms and stir-fry for another 3-4 minutes until well cooked. Add the sugar and soy sauce and stir until combined, then remove from the heat.

Scoop out a tablespoon of the taro mixture and flatten it with your hand. Put a teaspoon of the filling in the center and fold and pinch the edges together to enclose the filling into a pyramid shape. Repeat until all the dough and filling are used.

Heat enough oil for deep-frying in a large wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the taro pyramids in batches for 5-7 minutes or until crispy and golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve with cucumber relish.

recipes.title: Pork Roll

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 tablespoons pork liver, cut into small pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the sauce, pound the chiles, garlic and pineapple in a mortar with a pestle. Heat a pan over medium heat, add the chile and pineapple mixture, sugar, vinegar, and salt and simmer, stirring, until thick and sticky. Put the pork, pork liver, crabmeat, soy sauce, onion, sesame oil, and sugar into a large bowl and mix with your hands until combined.

Place the tofu sheet on a work surface and put the filling at one end, leaving a 2 cm border. Brush the borders with a little water then roll up, tucking in the ends as you go, to form a roll Brush the end with more water and press to seal. Set aside covered in a damp dish towel to prevent it from drying out. Pour 350 ml water into a large bowl, add the tempura flour, and stir until the flour has dissolved.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Dip the tofu roll into the tempura batter and deep-fry for 7-10 minutes until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve, cut into slices, with the dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Thai Summer Rolls

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 15 g crispy pork rind, coarsely chopped

ingredientGroups.heading: For the sauce
lines: 100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat add the jicama and oyster sauce, and saute for 30 seconds. Remove from the heat and set aside.

To make the sauce, pound all the ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Heat the sauce in a wok over medium heat. bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until thickened.

Lay a spring roll wrapper out on a work surface so that one of the corners faces you. Put a little of the lettuce, bean sprouts, pork skin, fried shallots, and jicama in the center of the wrapper and add a little sauce. Fold the bottom corner of the wrapper up and over the filling. Fold the left and right corners in to create a package. Roll the package up toward the top corner and brush a little water on the top edges of the wrapper to stick the package together. Repeat until you have used up the filling. Cut the rolls in half and serve with the remaining sauce.

recipes.title: Pork and Shrimp Golden Packages
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 scallion (spring onion) or baby leek, 20-30 cm long
150 g shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and ground (minced)
30 spring-roll wrapper sheets, about 13 cm in diameter
950 ml vegetable oil, for deep-frying Sweet Chili Dipping Sauce (see p. 60), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare one bowl of boiling water and another of cold water.
Cut the scallion or leek lengthwise into 5-7 mm-wide strips, making one strip for each wrapper.
Blanch the strips in the boiling water for 30 seconds, transfer to the cold water, then drain and pat dry.
For the filling, combine the shrimp, pork, saam-gler, soy sauce, sugar, and water chestnuts in a large bowl.
Cover and chili for at least 10 minutes.
Place a wrapper on the work surface and put 1 teaspoon filling in the center. Lift the edges to form a package and tie securely with a blanched scallion strip. Repeat with the remaining filling.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C. Deep-fry the packages in batches for 5-7 minutes, until golden brown and crisp.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve with sweet chili dipping sauce.

steps: Break the crackers into small pieces and put them in a deep bowl.
Add the fish paste, pork crackling, garlic, shallot, carrot, and yard-long bean and gently mix until combined.
Season with the lime juice, oil, and fish sauce and serve.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 150 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
100 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and ground
1 pineapple, peeled, cored, and cut into 3 x 1 cm pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Finely pound the garlic, cilantro root, and pepper in a mortar with a pestle.

Shape the cooled mixture into 2 cm balls and place each ball on a piece of pineapple. Top with a cilantro leaf and a slice of chile, then serve.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g tenderloin steak (beef sirloin), thinly sliced
1⁄2 head green or white cabbage, cut into chunks
120 ml Barbecue Sauce (see p. 63), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, or prepare according to package directions. Drain, cut, and set aside.
Put the beef in a bowl, add the oyster sauce, sugar, and soy sauce, and mix well. Cover and marinate for 10-15 minutes.
Put the beef and shrimp in a shallow serving dish and pour the beaten egg over them. Set aside.
Put the drained noodles on a serving plate with the cabbage, water spinach, and basil leaves.
For the soup, combine the chicken broth, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, shallots, cilantro, and galangal in a large bowl. Pour into a hot pot and bring to a boil.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 kg pork sirloin, rinsed and sliced into 2.5 cm strips
200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Finely pound the garlic, cilantro (coriander) roots, and peppercorns in a mortar with a pestle. Transfer to a large bowl and add the pork, salt, soy sauce, and sugar and mix well. Cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let marinate in the refrigerator for 2-4 hours.
Meanwhile, soak 10-15 bamboo skewers in a bowl of cold water for 30 minutes, This prevents the skewers from burning during cooking.
Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot, or your gas grill (barbecue) is preheated to 400°F/200°C.

Using your hands, mold some of the pork mixture onto a soaked wooden skewer, making sure that the mixture is firmly attached to the skewer and molds into an oval shape. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Brush the oil over the pork skewers, then grill for 10-12 minutes until cooked. Serve.

lines: 1 teaspoon coriander seeds, ground and toasted

steps: Slice the pork into pieces about 2.5 cm wide, 7.5 cm long, and 8 mm thick.

To serve Glutinous Rice (see p. 378) selection of condiments, such as sliced ginger, shallots, peanuts, bird's eye chiles, and scallions (spring onions)

steps: Put the ground (minced) meat, garlic, rice, and salt in a large bowl and mix together with clean, damp hands until the mixture is sticky and can be molded. Divide the mixture into portions, place the meat in the center of a banana leaf, and top with a chile. Cover the meat with the sides of the leaf, fold over the ends, and tightly seal with string. Alternatively, and the whole chiles to the meat, then pack the meat mixture into a large plastic food bag and seal. Let ferment for 7-10 days at room temperature The meat will taste sour when ready. Serve as patties with rice and a selection of condiments. Alternatively, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Steamed Spring Rolls
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 30 rice crepes or rice paper spring roll wrappers plum sauce, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the vermicelli in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes, then drain. Put all the ingredients except the rice crepes in a large bowl and mix together until thoroughly combined.

Lay a rice crepe on a work surface. Put 1-2 tablespoons of the filling in the center of the crepe and spread out thinly. Don't overfill because it might tear. Fold the bottom of the crepe up and over the filling. Fold the left and right sides in to create a package. Roll the package up toward the top of the crepe and brush a little water on the top edges of the crepe to stick the package together. Repeat until all the filling is used Steam the rolls in a steamer for about 5 minutes or until cooked. Serve with plum sauce.

recipes.title: Stuffed Roti
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: For the roti pastry
lines: 120 ml ghee or vegetable oil, plus extra for greasing

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Grease a baking sheet with vegetable oil and set aside.

To make the roti pastry, put the flour in a large bowl. Whisk half the beaten egg, the milk, salt, sugar, and 120 ml water in another bowl until the sugar and salt dissolve. Pour into the flour and mix and knead until the ingredients start to combine. Add 1 tablespoon ghee or vegetable oil and continue kneading until smooth.

Divide the dough into small equal portions. Coat your fingers with ghee or oil and shape the portions into small balls. Place them on the greased baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap or cheesecloth, and let stand for 2-10 hours before cooking.

Meanwhile, prepare the stuffing. Heat the butter and 1 tablespoon oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the saam-gler and curry powder and cook for 1 minute, or until fragrant. Add the onions and sauté for 1 minute, then add the chicken and stir-fry for 2 minutes, or until cooked. Season with the salt and sugar, stir-fry until fully flavored, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Place a dough ball on an oiled work surface. Dip your hand in ghee or oil, then press and flatten the dough into a very thin, wide, almost translucent sheet.

Put 3-4 tablespoons stuffing in the center, pour about 11⁄2 teaspoons beaten egg over it, and sprinkle with a little scallion. Fold in the sides, then the ends, to form a square package. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

Heat 1⁄2 tablespoon oil or ghee in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Cook the roti one at a time for about 2 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and crisp. Transfer to a serving plate and repeat with the remaining roti. Serve with cucumber relish.

recipes.title: Fried Crickets with Herbs
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3 garlic bulbs, cloves separated and finely sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the crickets in an airtight container and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, then remove and transfer to the freezer for 30 minutes.
Blanch the crickets in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then rinse under cold running water, drain, and set aside.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the ginger, galangal, lemongrass, and garlic for 1 minute or until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Deep-fry the peanuts, if using, in the oil for about 1 minute or until toasted. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Deep-fry the kaffir lime leaves in the oil for 20-30 seconds. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Make sure the oil is at the correct temperature, then deep-fry the crickets for about 5 minutes or until golden brown and crispy, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Mix the crickets, ginger mixture, garlic, and peanuts together and season with the salt Garnish with the kaffir lime leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Roasted Crickets
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the crickets in an airtight container and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, then remove and transfer to the freezer for 30 minutes. Remove the crickets from the freezer and wash 3 or 4 times in water.
Heat a wok over medium heat, add the crickets, and roast for 6-7 minutes. Add the lemongrass and pandan leaves and season with salt. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Serve.

recipes.title: Omelet with Red Ant Eggs
recipes.subtitle: North

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Break the eggs into a bowl, add the shallots, red ant eggs, and fish sauce, and beat thoroughly with a fork.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the garlic, and sauté for 1 minute. Pour in the egg mixture and roll it around the wok to form an omelet. Continue moving and rolling the wok for 2-3 minutes, until the omelet is yellow and begins to come away from the wok. Carefully flip and cook for another 1-2 minutes to color the other side. Serve.

recipes.title: Pickled Cabbage
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g choy sum (flowering Chinese cabbage), cut into 5 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix 950 ml water and the rice together in a large bowl. Stir until the water turns milky white. Strain through cheesecloth (muslin) and reserve 250 ml of the rice water. Strain the rice water again and set aside.
Put the choy sum and salt in a large bowl and rub the salt all over the cabbage. Squeeze and knead for 2-3 minutes until softened. Add the cooled glutinous rice and massage until well mixed.
Transfer to a large sterilized jar and add the reserved rice water, leaving 5 cm headspace. Add the ginger, if using, cover, and stand overnight at room temperature. Drain the next day and serve.

recipes.title: Dried Mango
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 kg ripe mangoes, peeled, pitted, and thinly sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the mango and salt in a food processor and blend until smooth. Transfer to a wok and heat over medium heat for about 20 minutes until sticky. Remove from the heat and let cool slightly, then shape the mango mixture into small balls. Flatten the balls into disks 5 cm in diameter. Put the mango disks on a tray and sun-dry for 24 hours. Turn over and let dry for another 48 hours. Store the dried mango in sterilized airtight jars. They must be stored away from moisture, so when filling the jars, make sure your hands are dry.

lines: 65 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 sour green mangoes, peeled and thinly sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the sugar and fish sauce together in a wok, then heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 5-8 minutes until thick. Add the shallot, chiles, and dried shrimp and mix well. Transfer to a small serving bowl and serve with the sliced green mango.

recipes.title: Preserved Mango
recipes.subtitle: Central
recipes.prepTime: 15 minutes, plus soaking and drying time

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg sour green mango, peeled, seeded, and sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pour 1.2 liters water into a large bowl, add the rock salt, and stir until the salt has dissolved. Add the mango slices to the salted water, cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm), and let soak for 24 hours The next day, remove the mango from the salted water with a slotted spoon and soak in the limewater for 1 hour. Rinse under cold running water and let dry. Bring 800 ml water and 700 g sugar to a boil in a large pan and keep boiling for 3-4 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool.

Put the sliced mango in a large bowl, pour the sugar syrup over the fruit, and cover with plastic wrap. Let soak overnight in the refrigerator. The next day, remove the mango with a slotted spoon and set aside. Bring the sugar syrup to a boil over medium heat and gradually add the remaining 100 g sugar. Boil until thick and sticky. Remove from the heat and let cool. When cool pour into an airtight container and add the mango. Cover and set aside for 2-3 days. Store in the refrigerator for up to I month.

recipes.title: Dried Bananas
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 small ripe bananas, peeled and sliced into circles

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Line a baking sheet with cheesecloth (muslin). Arrange the bananas on the lined baking sheet, cover with more cheesecloth to prevent any bugs from settling on the bananas, and let dry in the sun for 3-5 days. Turn the baking sheet once a day so the bananas dry evenly. Preheat the oven to 325°F/160°C/Gas Mark 3 and line a large baking sheet with wax (greaseproof) paper.

Mix the dried bananas with the honey in a large bowl. Transfer to the lined baking sheet and bake in the oven for about 20 minutes. Let cool, then transfer to a sterilized airtight jar and store for up to 3-4 weeks.

recipes.title: Thai-Style Chinese Cruller
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 120 g all-purpose (plain) flour, plus 50 g flour, for dusting
2 teaspoons superfine (caster) sugar a pinch of salt
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus extra for deep-frying
To serve coffee, hot chocolate, congee, or sweetened condensed milk

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar, and salt into a large bowl and mix well. Add 5 tablespoons water and knead for 10 minutes or until the dough is mixed well. Add the 1 tablespoon oil and knead for another 2-3 minutes. Cover the dough with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let rest for 2-10 hours. Knead the dough on a floured work surface. Roll into a tube shape and gently press with a rolling pin to create a 5 mm thick rectangle sheet. Cut the rectangle in half Lengthwise, then cut crosswise to create 2 x 8 cm strips. Take 2 dough strips. Moisten the middle of one strip with some water, then press the other strip on top where the water is. Stretch them out slightly. Repeat until all the dough strips are used.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the dough for 1-2 minutes on each side or until the dough has puffed up and turned golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve with coffee, hot chocolate, congee, or sweetened condensed milk.

recipes.title: Grilled Yuca Root with Coconut Syrup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 700 g-1 kg yuca root (cassava), peeled and cut crosswise into 10 cm pieces
200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the yuca root in cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and set aside.

For the coconut syrup, heat the coconut milk in a pan over medium heat. When it starts to boil, add the sugar and salt and stir until dissolved. Reduce the heat slightly and boil gently for 4-5 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Heat a charcoal grill until white hot, preheat a gas grill to 350°F/180°C, or heat an indoor broiler to medium-high. Steam the yuca over high heat for about 10 minutes, or until it just starts to cook; do not overcook it.
Grill the yuca over medium heat for about 10 minutes on each side, or until brown. If broiling, place the rack about 10 cm from the heat and broil for about 10 minutes on each side.
Put the grilled yuca on a cutting board and flatten each piece by pressing it with another board or a plate.

Dip the yuca in the coconut syrup for 2-3 minutes. Return it to the grill or broiler and cook each side for 3-5 minutes, or until the coating dries. Transfer to a plate, pour over the remaining syrup, and serve.

lines: 3 tablespoons lemon juice Ice cubes, to serve

steps: Bring 3 liters water to a boil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the butterfly pea flowers and boil for about 5 minutes.
Add the sugar, salt, and lemon juice and stir for about 5 minutes, until the sugar and salt dissolve.
Remove from the heat and let cool slightly. Strain through cheesecloth into a heatproof pitcher and cool completely.
Serve over ice.

recipes.title: Dragon Fruit Frappé

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the dragon fruits into a blender, add the ice cubes, honey, and lime juice and blend until smooth. Serve.

recipes.title: Water Chestnut Rubies and Emeralds in Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 250 ml cream soda syrup or green
250 ml grenadine or red sugar syrup
400 g peeled and diced water chestnuts
1 pandan leaf, tied in a knot
250 ml coconut milk ice cubes, crushed to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the cream soda syrup, grenadine, and tapioca flour in separate bowls. Divide the water chestnuts between the bowls of red and green sugar syrup and let soak for about 10 minutes or until the chestnuts absorbs the color. Remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to the bowl of tapioca flour. Shake the bowl until the water chestnuts are well coated with starch.

Have a bowl of ice water ready. Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil in a pan, add the coated water chestnuts, and let sit for 3-4 minutes until the water chestnuts float to the surface and the flour has become transparent (jellylike). Transfer to the bowl of ice water and set aside.

Bring 250 ml water and the sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Boil until the mixture turns syrupy, then remove from the heat, let cool, and set aside. Heat the pandan leaf and coconut milk in a pan over low-medium heat for 3-4 minutes or until it reaches a boil. Remove from the heat, let cool, and set aside.
Drain the water chestnuts and spoon into a serving bowl. Add the sugar syrup, and infused coconut milk, and crushed ice cubes and serve.

lines: 20 g Asiatic pennywort leaves, washed thoroughly
2 tablespoons sugar syrup (see left) ice cubes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the leaves in a blender, add 250 ml recently boiled water, and process until smooth. Strain through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a large heatproof pitcher (jug) to remove the residue.

Carefully pour 250 ml boiling water over the residue into the pitcher and squeeze the cheesecloth to extract the liquid Discard the residue. Add the sugar syrup to the juice, stir well, and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes.

Strain through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a large heatproof pitcher (jug) to remove the residue. Serve cold with ice cubes.

recipes.title: Kumquat Juice
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 tablespoon salt ice cubes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Wash the kumquats and squeeze the juice into a large pan. Pour in 2 liters water and stir until mixed. Add the sugar and salt, then bring to a boil over medium heat. Remove from the heat, strain through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a large heatproof pitcher (jug), and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes.

recipes.searchText: Kumquat Juice Central 1 kg kumquats 1 kg superfine (caster) sugar 1 tablespoon salt ice cubes, to serve Wash the kumquats and squeeze the juice into a large pan. Pour in 2 liters water and stir until mixed. Add the sugar and salt, then bring to a boil over medium heat. Remove from the heat, strain through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a large heatproof pitcher (jug), and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes.

recipes.title: Lemongrass Juice
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1⁄2 teaspoon salt ice cubes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 2 liters water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, and simmer for 8-10 minutes. Remove from the heat and strain the lemongrass juice through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a large heatproof pitcher (jug). Add the sugar and salt and stir until dissolved. Pour the lemongrass juice into a clean pan and bring to a boil over medium heat, then remove from the heat and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes:.

recipes.searchText: Lemongrass Juice Central 500 g chopped lemongrass stalks 300 g superfine (caster) sugar 1⁄2 teaspoon salt ice cubes, to serve Bring 2 liters water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, and simmer for 8-10 minutes. Remove from the heat and strain the lemongrass juice through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a large heatproof pitcher (jug). Add the sugar and salt and stir until dissolved. Pour the lemongrass juice into a clean pan and bring to a boil over medium heat, then remove from the heat and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes:.

recipes.title: Passion Fruit Juice
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 teaspoon salt Ice cubes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 350 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add the sugar and stir until dissolved and syrupy, then remove from the heat.
Strain the passion fruit pulp through cheesecloth into a large heatproof pitcher and discard the residue.
Add the salt and 120 ml of the sugar syrup and stir well.
Serve cold over ice.

recipes.searchText: Passion Fruit Juice Northeast 200 g superfine (caster) sugar 1 kg passion fruit, halved 1 teaspoon salt Ice cubes, to serve Bring 350 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the salt and 120 ml of the sugar syrup and stir well. Serve cold over ice.

recipes.title: Pandan Juice
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 5 x 30 g pandan leaves, washed and cut crosswise into 5-7.5 cm strips
50 g granulated sugar A pinch of salt Ice cubes, to serve (optional)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1.4 liters water to a boil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add the pandan leaves, reduce the heat to medium-low, and boil for 5 minutes.
Add the sugar and salt and boil for another 2-3 minutes, until dissolved.
Remove from the heat and adjust the sweetness to taste.
Strain through a fine sieve into a heatproof pitcher. Serve hot, or cold over ice.

recipes.searchText: Pandan Juice Northeast 5 x 30 g pandan leaves, washed and cut crosswise into 5-7.5 cm strips 50 g granulated sugar A pinch of salt Ice cubes, to serve (optional) Bring 1.4 liters water to a boil in a large pan over medium-high heat. recipes.title: Roselle Juice
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g fresh roselle (or 20 g dried roselle). cleaned
4 teaspoons salt ice cubes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 2 liters of water to a boil in a large pan. Add the roselle, reduce the heat, and simmer gently until the water turns dark red. Remove the roselle with a slotted spoon, add the sugar and salt, and bring back to a boil. Boil for 10 minutes, then remove from the heat and flavor to taste. Pour into a heatproof pitcher (jug) and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes.

recipes.searchText: Roselle Juice North 200 g fresh roselle (or 20 g dried roselle). cleaned 200 g granulated sugar 4 teaspoons salt ice cubes, to serve Bring 2 liters of water to a boil in a large pan. recipes.title: Sweetened Soy Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Rinse the soybeans until the water becomes clear, then soak in 750 ml water for at least 6 hours. Drain and discard the soaking water.

Finely pound the soybeans in a mortar with a pestle, then transfer to a large bowl, pour in 1.7 liters water, and stir well. Strain through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a pan, discarding the residue left in the cheesecloth.

Bring the soy milk to a boil over medium heat, stirring continuously for 5 minutes. Add the sugar, reduce the heat to low, and stir for 5-10 minutes or until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat and serve hot or cold.

recipes.searchText: Sweetened Soy Milk Central 160 g soybeans, peeled 100 g superfine (caster) sugar Rinse the soybeans until the water becomes clear, then soak in 750 ml water for at least 6 hours. Add the sugar, reduce the heat to low, and stir for 5-10 minutes or until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat and serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Tamarind Juice
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 80 g peeled and seeded sour tamarind pods
250 g granulated sugar ice cubes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the tamarind puree, soak the tamarind pods in 350 ml warm water for 15-20 minutes. Use your hand to squeeze the tamarind and water to mix and remove the tamarind flesh until you have quite a thick puree. Strain the tamarind mixture through a fine strainer (sieve) into a cup. Set aside. Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the tamarind puree, salt, and sugar and stir until the sugar has dissolved, then boil for 4-5 minutes. Remove from the heat. Serve hot or cold with ice cubes.

recipes.searchText: Tamarind Juice Northeast 80 g peeled and seeded sour tamarind pods 1⁄2 teaspoons salt 250 g granulated sugar ice cubes, to serve To make the tamarind puree, soak the tamarind pods in 350 ml warm water for 15-20 minutes. Serve hot or cold with ice cubes.

recipes.title: Spicy Egg Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 hard-boiled eggs, peeled and quartered lengthwise
5 red and green bird's-eye chiles, finely chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Arrange the eggs on a serving plate.
Stir the shallots, chiles, fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the dressing over the eggs, garnish with the cilantro leaves, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Egg Salad Central 4 hard-boiled eggs, peeled and quartered lengthwise 2 shallots, sliced lengthwise 5 red and green bird's-eye chiles, finely chopped 21⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce 2 tablespoons lime juice 11⁄2 tablespoons superfine (caster) sugar 1 handful cilantro (coriander) leaves Arrange the eggs on a serving plate. Stir the shallots, chiles, fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves. Pour the dressing over the eggs, garnish with the cilantro leaves, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Salted Egg Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 yard-long bean, cut into 8 cm pieces
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 salted duck eggs, cut into quarters lengthwise

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Coarsely pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle.
Add the yard-long bean, tomatoes, papaya, and dried shrimp and mix together.
Season with the lime juice, sugar, and fish sauce and mix well.
Add the eggs and gently stir with a spoon.
Transfer to a serving dish, sprinkle with the peanuts, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Salted Egg Salad Central 5-6 red bird's eye chiles 3-4 cloves garlic 1 yard-long bean, cut into 8 cm pieces 3 small tomatoes 175 g julienned green papaya 2 tablespoons dried shrimp 1-2 tablespoons lime juice 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 1 tablespoon fish sauce 2 salted duck eggs, cut into quarters lengthwise 2 tablespoons roasted peanuts, to garnish Coarsely pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle. Add the yard-long bean, tomatoes, papaya, and dried shrimp and mix together. Season with the lime juice, sugar, and fish sauce and mix well. Add the eggs and gently stir with a spoon. Transfer to a serving dish, sprinkle with the peanuts, and serve.

recipes.title: Thai Rice Salad
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g jasmine rice, rinsed and drained
200 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dressing
lines: 50 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the dressing, bring the fish sauce and 250 ml water to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the sugar, lemongrass, lime leaves, and galangal and return to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.

Remove from the heat and strain through cheesecloth (muslin) into a clean pan. Discard the solids. Return the liquid to the heat, bring to a boil, then simmer for another 5-7 minutes until thickened and reduced by half. Set aside.

For the rice salad, process the morinda leaves in a blender. Strain through cheesecloth into a bowl or pitcher, add 600 ml water, and stir. Put the rice in a pan, add enough morinda water to cover, bring to a boil over medium heat, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the shrimp in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until pink. Drain, pound to a smooth paste, then toast the paste in a wok for 5-7 minutes until dry. Set aside.
Dry-fry the grated coconut in a clean wok for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden brown. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Soak the vermicelli in water for 10 minutes, or according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the salt, sugar, and noodles and stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until dry.
Mix all the rice-salad ingredients together and serve with the dressing and side dishes.

Add the salt, sugar, and noodles and stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until dry. Mix all the rice-salad ingredients together and serve with the dressing and side dishes.

recipes.title: Spicy Fish Salad
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg sea bass or sea bream, cleaned and filleted
65 g pea eggplants, grilled and pounded

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Finely chop the fish, then cook in a large skillet or frying pan for 2-3 minutes. Set aside. Mix the chili flakes, ground rice, shallots, scallion (spring onion), cilantro (coriander), and sawtooth cilantro (coriander) together in a bowl. Add the fish sauce, fermented fish sauce, galangal, and eggplant (aubergine), and mix well. Sprinkle with the mint leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Seaweed Salad
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
100 g red and green bird's-eye chiles
350 g sliced shallots Betel leaves, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the seaweed in a bow of water for 1 hour then drain and set aside.

Mix the coconut cream, tamarind, sugar, salt, and shrimp paste together in a large pan. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then remove from the heat and let stand until warm. Add the soaked seaweed, the peanuts, dried shrimp, coconut chiles, and shallot and mix together. Put a tablespoon of the salad into the center of a betel leaf. Repeat until all the salad s used. Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Mackerel Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 x 150 g steamed salted horse mackerel, or 150 g smoked mackerel
7 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
1 x 5⁄8-inch/11⁄2 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the horse mackerel and fry for 2-3 minutes on each side. Remove and let cool.
Remove the skin and bones and put the flesh in a large bowl. Gently crumble it into small pieces.
Add the shallots, chiles, lemongrass, ginger, lime juice, and fish sauce and mix well. Transfer to a serving plate, garnish with the peppermint leaves, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Squid and Heart of Palm Salad
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g squid, cleaned and cut into 4 cm pieces
100 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails still intact

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dressing
lines: 10 red bird's eye chiles, finely chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blanch the squid in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes or until cooked. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the shrimp in another pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes or until pink. Drain and set aside.
For the dressing, mix the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and chiles in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Add the squid, shrimp, heart of palm, mango, carrot, onion, cilantro, and scallions. Mix well and serve.

recipes.title: Deep Fried Squid Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g squid, cut into 1 cm-thick rings
2 lemongrass stalks, finely sliced Peppermint leaves, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Whisk the flour and cold water together until thoroughly combined.

Heat the oil in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C. Dip the squid in the batter, carefully add it to the oil, and deep-fry for 4-5 minutes, until golden and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Mix the chili jam, lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, shallot, kaffir lime leaves, chiles, and lemongrass in a bowl.
Add the squid and mix well. Transfer to a serving plate, garnish with peppermint leaves, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Wing Bean Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 12 uncooked jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled and deveined, with tails still intact
40 g cashew nuts Peppermint leaves, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Cook the shrimp in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, or until they turn pink, then drain and set aside.
Fill a bowl with ice-cold water and set aside.
Blanch the wing beans in a pan of boiling water for 30 seconds, then drain and transfer to the ice water for 1 minute.
Drain the beans, slice them into 5 mm-thick slices, and set aside.
To make the sauce, mix all the sauce ingredients together in a large bowl until thoroughly combined.
Add the shrimp, squid, cashew nuts, and wing beans and mix well.
Transfer to a serving plate, garnish with peppermint leaves, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Giant Freshwater Shrimp Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3-8 red bird's eye chiles, finely chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the broiler (grill) to high. Put the shrimp on the broiler rack and broil for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until cooked. Let cool slightly, remove the shells, and press the juices from the heads.
Put the shrimp in a bowl, add the remaining ingredients, and mix until thoroughly combined. Serve.

lines: 100 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined
10 red bird's eye chiles, finely chopped
1 teaspoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar lettuce leaves, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blanch the pork in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes or until cooked. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the squid in another pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the shrimp in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes or until pink. Drain and set aside.

Mix the pork, squid, shrimp, carrots, chiles, shallots, celery, and heart of palm in a large bowl. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar and mix until the sugar dissolves. Serve on lettuce leaves.

recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 150 g squid, sliced into 2 cm-thick rings
180 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined
1 tablespoon sliced red and green bird's eye chiles
1 handful cilantro (coriander), chopped, plus extra sprigs to garnish
20 g Chinese celery stalk, chopped into 3 cm lengths
5 kaffir lime leaves, chopped (optional) lettuce leaves, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blanch the squid in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the shrimp in another pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
For the dressing, combine the lime juice, fish sauce, and sugar in a small bowl. Add the chicken broth or water and stir until the sugar dissolves.

Put the shrimp, squid, onion, mango, carrot, chiles, tomatoes, cilantro, celery, scallions, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, if using, and dressing in a large bowl. Stir 3-4 times until coated. Serve on lettuce leaves and garnish with cilantro sprigs.

recipes.title: Spicy Salad with Shrimp and Pork
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact
500 g vegetable hummingbird flowers, stamens removed

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dressing
lines: 10 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring a pan of water to a boil, add the shrimp, and blanch for 1-2 minutes, or until pink and cooked. Drain and set aside.

Return the water to a boil, add the pork, and blanch for 2-3 minutes, or until cooked. Drain and set aside. Return the water to a boil once more, add the vegetable hummingbird flowers, and blanch for 1 minute. Drain and set aside.

For the dressing, pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar and stir until the sugar dissolves. Transfer the dressing to a large serving bowl, add the shrimp, pork, and flowers, and mix well. Stir in the shallots and serve.

Drain and set aside. Return the water to a boil, add the pork, and blanch for 2-3 minutes, or until cooked. Drain and set aside. Return the water to a boil once more, add the vegetable hummingbird flowers, and blanch for 1 minute. Drain and set aside. For the dressing, pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar and stir until the sugar dissolves. Transfer the dressing to a large serving bowl, add the shrimp, pork, and flowers, and mix well. Stir in the shallots and serve.

recipes.title: Glass Noodle Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 50 g squid, sliced into 2 cm-thick rings
10 red bird's-eye chiles, very finely chopped
30 g Chinese celery stalks, sliced into 2.5 cm pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes. Drain, then blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, or cook according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the sliced pork in boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Blanch the fish balls in boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Blanch the squid in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then drain and set aside. Blanch the ground pork in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then drain and set aside.

Put the noodles in a large bowl. Add the sliced pork, fish balls, squid, ground pork, fried fish balls, Chinese fish cake, onion, chiles, sugar, lime juice, fish sauce, cilantro, and Chinese celery. Mix well and serve.

recipes.searchText: Glass Noodle Salad Central 500 g glass noodles 50 g pork tenderloin, sliced 50 g squid, sliced into 2 cm-thick rings 50 g fish balls 50 g ground pork 4 fried fish balls 7 slices Chinese fish cake 100 g sliced onion 10 red bird's-eye chiles, very finely chopped 1 tablespoon granulated sugar 2 tablespoons lime juice 11⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce 1 tablespoon chopped cilantro 30 g Chinese celery stalks, sliced into 2.5 cm pieces Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes. Blanch the ground pork in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then drain and set aside. Put the noodles in a large bowl. Add the sliced pork, fish balls, squid, ground pork, fried fish balls, Chinese fish cake, onion, chiles, sugar, lime juice, fish sauce, cilantro, and Chinese celery. Mix well and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Shrimp and Mango Salad
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 tablespoons julienned sour green mango or shredded carrot

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the dressing, mix all the ingredients together in a bowl and set aside For the salad, mix all the ingredients together in a large bowl, add the dressing, and mix until combined. Garnish with the dried chiles and fried shallot and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Shrimp and Mango Salad South 5 red bird's eye chiles 4 shallots, sliced 1 tablespoon sliced lemongrass 4 teaspoons chopped cilantro (coriander) leaves 2 teaspoons chopped scallion (spring onions) 4 kaffir lime leaves, thinly sliced 2 tablespoons julienned sour green mango or shredded carrot 2 tablespoon roasted cashew nuts 100 g dried shrimp 2 tablespoons lime juice 2 teaspoons fish sauce 2 teaspoons sugar 5 dried red chiles, fried 2 tablespoons Fried Shallot (see p. 64) To make the dressing, mix all the ingredients together in a bowl and set aside For the salad, mix all the ingredients together in a large bowl, add the dressing, and mix until combined. Garnish with the dried chiles and fried shallot and serve.

recipes.title: Cilantro Salad
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 90 g pork crackling, cut into small pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, garlic, ginger, shallots, galangal, lemongrass, cilantro roots, and shrimp paste thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chili paste, and stir-fry for 2 minutes, or until fragrant, then remove from the heat.
Put the cilantro and pork crackling in a bowl and mix well. Add the chili paste and a pinch of salt and mix well. Sprinkle with the fried garlic and shallots and serve.

recipes.searchText: Cilantro Salad North 80 g finely sliced cilantro (coriander) 90 g pork crackling, cut into small pieces 3 tablespoons Fried Garlic (see p. 64) 3 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 64) Salt 7 dried red chiles 7 cloves garlic 4 slices ginger 5 shallots, chopped 2 slices galangal 2 lemongrass stalks 3 cilantro (coriander) roots 1 teaspoon shrimp paste 2 tablespoons vegetable oil For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. recipes.title: Spicy Yard-Long Bean and Pork Salad
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish
lines: 2 tablespoons chopped scallions (spring onions) white sesame seeds (optional)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, salt, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside.

Bring a pan of water to a boil. Add the water spinach and blanch for 30 seconds, then transfer to cold water and drain. Add the yard-long beans to the boiling water and blanch for 1 minute, then transfer to cold water and drain. Boil the eggplants and lablab beans separately for 2-3 minutes, then drain. Coarsely chop all the vegetables.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the pork and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add the vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Transfer to a serving dish and garnish with the neem tree tips, shallots, cilantro, scallions, and sesame seeds, if using.

Transfer to a serving dish and garnish with the neem tree tips, shallots, cilantro, scallions, and sesame seeds, if using.

recipes.title: Spicy Dried Buffalo Skin Salad
recipes.subtitle: North

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the boiler (grill) to medium. Put the buffalo skin on the broiler (grill) rack and char to remove the hairs. Soak the skin in a bowl of water for 3 hours, then drain, transfer to a pan of boiling water, and boil for 20 minutes or until tender. Drain and set aside.

For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallot, garlic, and salt in a mortar win a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix until combined. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the garlic and 11⁄2 teaspoons chili paste and cook for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the tomatoes, buffalo skin, and 2 tablespoons water and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Transfer to a serving plate, sprinkle with the sesame seeds, and scallion (spring onion) and garnish with the cilantro (coriander) sprig. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Dried Buffalo Skin Salad North 200 g dried buffalo skin, shredded 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 6 cloves garlic, chopped 10 cherry tomatoes, halved 2 tablespoons white sesame seeds 1 tablespoon chopped scallion (spring onion) 1 cilantro (coriander) sprig, to garnish 5 dried red chiles, seeded 3 shallots, coarsely chopped 8 cloves garlic 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon shrimp paste Heat the boiler (grill) to medium.
