recipes.title: Spicy Pork Liver Salad
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g pork liver, rinsed, drained, and cut into bite-size pieces
1 tablespoon Ground Toasted Rice (see p. 64) Glutinous Rice (see p. 378), to serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as Chinese greens, cucumber, and napa (Chinese) cabbage, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the pork liver and blanch for 1-2 minutes, or until medium cooked.
Remove from the heat and add the chili flakes, lime juice, fish sauce, shallot, scallions, sawtooth cilantro, mint leaves, and ground toasted rice and mix well.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with glutinous rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Pork Liver Salad Northeast 75 ml chicken broth (stock) 100 g pork liver, rinsed, drained, and cut into bite-size pieces 2 teaspoons dried chili flakes 1 tablespoon lime juice 1 tablespoon fish sauce 1 shallot, sliced lengthwise 3 scallions (spring onions), finely sliced 2 sawtooth cilantro (coriander) leaves, finely sliced 1 handful mint leaves 1 tablespoon Ground Toasted Rice (see p. 64) Glutinous Rice (see p. 378), to serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as Chinese greens, cucumber, and napa (Chinese) cabbage, to serve Bring the broth to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Remove from the heat and add the chili flakes, lime juice, fish sauce, shallot, scallions, sawtooth cilantro, mint leaves, and ground toasted rice and mix well. Transfer to a serving plate and serve with glutinous rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Peanut Curd in Spicy Salad
recipes.subtitle: North
recipes.prepTime: 10 minutes, plus soaking and cooling time

ingredientGroups.heading: For the spicy salad
lines: 1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and finely sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the peanuts in water overnight, then drain. Grind them thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle until fine.

Bring 2 liters water and the ground peanuts to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Stir in the rice flour, then strain through cheesecloth (muslin) into a large, shallow rectangular container. Spread out the curd mixture and leave to cool until solid.

For the salad, cut the peanut curd into 2.5 cm pieces about 3-4 mm thick and place in a large bowl. Add the chili jam, salt, shallot, garlic, and pork and mix together. Add the lime juice, lemon juice, and cilantro and mix well. Sprinkle with the fried garlic and shallots and serve.

recipes.searchText: Peanut Curd in Spicy Salad North 1 kg peanuts, peeled 500 g rice flour 2 tablespoons Chili Jam (see p. 35) 1 teaspoon salt 1 shallot, sliced 1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and finely sliced 150 g shredded pork, fried 1 tablespoon lime juice 11⁄2 teaspoons lemon juice 30 g finely chopped cilantro (coriander) 6 tablespoons Fried Garlic (see p. 64) 6 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 64) Soak the peanuts in water overnight, then drain. recipes.title: Spicy Beef Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g thin beef sirloin, tenderloin, or rump steak
1 cucumber, halved lengthwise and sliced into 1 cm-thick pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat a charcoal or gas grill to 400°F/200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium. Put the beef in a shallow dish, add the soy sauce, turn to coat, and marinate for about 10 minutes.
Grill or broil the beef for 4-5 minutes on each side. Remove, slice into strips, and set aside.
For the dressing, stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and chiles together until the sugar dissolves.
Put the beef, cucumber, tomatoes, shallots, and cilantro in a large bowl. Pour in the dressing, toss lightly, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Beef Salad Central 300 g thin beef sirloin, tenderloin, or rump steak 2 teaspoons soy sauce 1 cucumber, halved lengthwise and sliced into 1 cm-thick pieces 2 tomatoes, quartered 3 shallots, sliced 1 handful sawtooth cilantro (coriander), coarsely chopped 3 tablespoons fish sauce 3 tablespoons lime juice 1 tablespoon granulated sugar 5 red bird's eye chiles, chopped Heat a charcoal or gas grill to 400°F/200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium. Put the beef in a shallow dish, add the soy sauce, turn to coat, and marinate for about 10 minutes. Grill or broil the beef for 4-5 minutes on each side. Remove, slice into strips, and set aside. For the dressing, stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and chiles together until the sugar dissolves. Put the beef, cucumber, tomatoes, shallots, and cilantro in a large bowl. Pour in the dressing, toss lightly, and serve.

recipes.title: Chinese Mustard Green Salad
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 60 g chopped Chinese mustard greens (with yellow flowers)
70 g white and black sesame seeds, roasted

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blanch the mustard greens in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and plunge into ice-cold water.
Mix the remaining ingredients in a large bowl. Drain the mustard greens, add them to the bowl, and mix well. Sprinkle with the fried garlic and shallots and serve.

recipes.searchText: Chinese Mustard Green Salad North 60 g chopped Chinese mustard greens (with yellow flowers) 1 tomato, sliced 3 tablespoons chili powder 150 g peanuts, roasted 70 g white and black sesame seeds, roasted 1 teaspoon turmeric 1 teaspoon salt 3 tablespoons Fried Garlic (see p. 64) 2 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 64) Blanch the mustard greens in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and plunge into ice-cold water. Mix the remaining ingredients in a large bowl. Drain the mustard greens, add them to the bowl, and mix well. Sprinkle with the fried garlic and shallots and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Round Eggplant and Pork Salad
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 8 dried red bird's eye chiles, chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Boil the pork for 3-4 minutes, or until cooked. Drain and pat dry, then pound thoroughly in a mortar. Tear the pork into small pieces and set aside.
Mix 475 ml water with the salt until dissolved. Halve the eggplants lengthwise, slice them lengthwise into 3 mm pieces, and soak in the salt water for 5 minutes.

For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, galangal, and salt until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix thoroughly.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chopped garlic and chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute, or until golden and fragrant. Add the pork and 1 tablespoon water and stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Drain the eggplants and mix them with the pork and chili paste. Sprinkle with the cilantro, scallion, peppermint, and Vietnamese cilantro and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Round Eggplant and Pork Salad North 100 g pork loin 1 teaspoon salt 3-7 young round eggplants (aubergines), stems discarded 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 7 cloves garlic, chopped 1 tablespoon chopped cilantro (coriander) 1 tablespoon chopped scallion (spring onion) 1 tablespoon chopped peppermint leaves 1 tablespoon chopped Vietnamese cilantro (coriander) 8 dried red bird's eye chiles, chopped 2 shallots, chopped 4 cloves garlic, sliced 2 thin slices galangal 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon shrimp paste Boil the pork for 3-4 minutes, or until cooked. Add the pork and 1 tablespoon water and stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes. Remove from the heat. Drain the eggplants and mix them with the pork and chili paste. Sprinkle with the cilantro, scallion, peppermint, and Vietnamese cilantro and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Red Ant Salad
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 9 cm piece galangal, peeled and sliced
5 red and green bird's eye chiles, finely chopped

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dressing
lines: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
To serve wild betel leaves, sliced star gooseberry leaves, sliced young jackfruit, peeled and seeded while wearing gloves, and cut into chunks

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the ants in an airtight container and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, then transfer to the freezer for 30 minutes.
Roast the ants in a wok over medium heat for 6-8 minutes, or until dry. Set aside.

For the dressing, mix the tamarind, sugar, fermented fish sauce, fish sauce, shrimp paste, lime juice, and salt in a bowl. Transfer to a wok and warm over low heat for 2-3 minutes, or until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat and cool.
Add the ants, galangal, lemongrass, chiles, dried shrimp, and peanuts to the cooled dressing and stir until combined. Serve with the wild betel leaves, star gooseberry leaves, and young jackfruit.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Red Ant Salad Northeast 80 g red ants 9 cm piece galangal, peeled and sliced 30 g sliced lemongrass stalk 5 red and green bird's eye chiles, finely chopped 30 g dried shrimp 75 g roasted peanuts 1 tablespoon Tamarind Puree (see p. 83) 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 2 tablespoons boiled fermented fish sauce 1 teaspoon fish sauce 1 teaspoon shrimp paste 1 teaspoon lime juice 1 teaspoon salt To serve wild betel leaves, sliced star gooseberry leaves, sliced young jackfruit, peeled and seeded while wearing gloves, and cut into chunks Put the ants in an airtight container and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, then transfer to the freezer for 30 minutes. recipes.title: Thai Spicy Salad with Giant Water Bug Eggs
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 5-7 red and green bird's eye chiles, finely chopped
2 scallions (spring onions), snipped into small lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying to 350°F/180°C. Deep-fry the squid and fish bladder for 5 minutes, or until crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar in a large bowl. Add the crispy fish bladder and squid, cashew nuts, onions, tomato, chiles, sweet shrimp if using, scallions, carrots, mango, celery, and giant water bug eggs. Mix well and serve.

recipes.searchText: Thai Spicy Salad with Giant Water Bug Eggs South 475 ml vegetable oil, for deep-frying 25 g finely sliced dried squid 50 g dried fish bladder 2 tablespoons fish sauce 2 tablespoons lime juice 1 tablespoon granulated sugar 40 g roasted cashew nuts 40 g sliced onions 1⁄2 small tomato, sliced 5-7 red and green bird's eye chiles, finely chopped 30 g sweet shrimp (optional) 2 scallions (spring onions), snipped into small lengths 100 g julienned carrots 165 g julienned sour green mango 1 Chinese celery stalk, chopped 2 tablespoons giant water bug eggs Heat the oil for deep-frying to 350°F/180°C. Deep-fry the squid and fish bladder for 5 minutes, or until crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar in a large bowl. Add the crispy fish bladder and squid, cashew nuts, onions, tomato, chiles, sweet shrimp if using, scallions, carrots, mango, celery, and giant water bug eggs. Mix well and serve.

recipes.title: Snail and Noodle Salad
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g snakehead fish or catfish, cleaned
1 handful young pink mempat leaves or tamarind leaves, sliced
1 handful chayote shoots or young spinach, sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the snails in tepid water for 1-2 hours, then drain. Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, then drain and blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, or according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.

Fill a large bowl with water and add the vinegar. Remove and discard the outer red petals and small white flowers from the banana blossom. Cut off the tip and base, quarter the blossom lengthwise, and place it in the vinegar water. Separate and clean the layers, discard the flowers within, finely slice the leaves to 5 mm thick, and return them to the vinegar water.
Bring 750 ml water to a boil. Add the snails, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain, discard the shells, and set aside.
Bring 350 ml water to a boil in another pan. Add the fish and cook for 7-10 minutes. Drain, discard the bones and skin, and tear the flesh into small pieces.

Pound the chili flakes and shallots to a smooth paste. Transfer to a large bowl and add the snails and fish. Drain and rinse the banana blossom, add it with the remaining ingredients, and mix thoroughly. Garnish with the chiles and fried shallots and serve.

Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, then drain and blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, or according to the package directions. Drain and set aside. Separate and clean the layers, discard the flowers within, finely slice the leaves to 5 mm thick, and return them to the vinegar water. Bring 750 ml water to a boil. Add the snails, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain, discard the shells, and set aside. Bring 350 ml water to a boil in another pan. Add the fish and cook for 7-10 minutes. Drain, discard the bones and skin, and tear the flesh into small pieces. Pound the chili flakes and shallots to a smooth paste. Transfer to a large bowl and add the snails and fish. Drain and rinse the banana blossom, add it with the remaining ingredients, and mix thoroughly. Garnish with the chiles and fried shallots and serve.

recipes.title: Pickled Vegetable Salad
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 x 1-inch/3.5-om piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Leave 3 chiles whole and finely chop the rest, then set aside.
Mix the pickled mustard greens, eggplant (aubergine), and ginger together in a large bowl. Sprinkle with the whole and finely chopped chiles. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Pickled Vegetable Salad Northeast 5 red bird's-eye chiles 120 g sliced pickled mustard greens 2 yellow round eggplants (aubergines), sliced 1 x 1-inch/3.5-om piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced Leave 3 chiles whole and finely chop the rest, then set aside. Mix the pickled mustard greens, eggplant (aubergine), and ginger together in a large bowl. Sprinkle with the whole and finely chopped chiles. Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Shiitake Mushroom Salad
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 230 g fresh shiitake mushrooms, stems discarded
3-5 red and green bird's eye chiles, finely chopped
1 tablespoon mint leaves, to garnish raw vegetables, such as tomatoes, cucumber, lettuce, and cabbage, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blanch the shiitake mushrooms in boiling water for 1 minute, or until cooked. Drain and pat dry, then slice into 5 mm strips and put in a large bowl.
Add the cilantro, shallots, kaffir lime leaves, scallions, garlic, sawtooth cilantro, ground toasted rice, chili flakes, lime juice, lemongrass, chiles, fish sauce, and chicken broth and mix well.
Garnish with the mint leaves and serve with raw vegetables.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Shiitake Mushroom Salad Northeast 230 g fresh shiitake mushrooms, stems discarded 1 tablespoon sliced cilantro (coriander) 2-3 small shallots, finely sliced lengthwise 3 kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced 2 scallions (spring onions), finely sliced 4 cloves garlic, thinly sliced 2 sawtooth cilantro (coriander) leaves, finely sliced 1 tablespoon Ground Toasted Rice (see p. 64) 1-2 teaspoons dried chili flakes 1 tablespoon lime juice 1 lemongrass stalk, finely sliced 3-5 red and green bird's eye chiles, finely chopped 11⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce 2 tablespoons chicken broth (stock) 1 tablespoon mint leaves, to garnish raw vegetables, such as tomatoes, cucumber, lettuce, and cabbage, to serve Blanch the shiitake mushrooms in boiling water for 1 minute, or until cooked. Drain and pat dry, then slice into 5 mm strips and put in a large bowl. Add the cilantro, shallots, kaffir lime leaves, scallions, garlic, sawtooth cilantro, ground toasted rice, chili flakes, lime juice, lemongrass, chiles, fish sauce, and chicken broth and mix well. Garnish with the mint leaves and serve with raw vegetables.

recipes.title: Spicy Mushroom Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 8-10 jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled and deveined
300 g mixed mushrooms, such as straw, king oyster, and shimeji mushrooms
11⁄2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 handful cilantro (coriander), coarsely chopped, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blanch the pork in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes or until cooked. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the shrimp in another pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the mushrooms in another pan of boiling water for about 30 seconds. Drain and set aside.
For the dressing, stir the fish sauce, lime juice, chiles, and sugar together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Put the pork, shrimp, mushrooms, scallions, shallots, and dressing in a large bowl and mix well. Transfer to a serving plate, sprinkle with cilantro, and serve.

methodGroups.heading: Method

Add the beans and pound coarsely.

recipes.title: Spicy Pomelo Salad

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 11⁄2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Cook the shrimp in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, or until pink, then drain and set aside.
Cook the pork in another pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Dry-fry the coconut in a skillet or frying pan over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 1-2 minutes, or until light brown. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside.
To make the dressing, put the sugar, salt, chili flakes, and coconut milk in a bowl and mix until the sugar has dissolved. Set aside.

Peel the pomelo and cut the flesh into segments. Remove and discard the pith and membrane, then break the flesh into small pieces and transfer to a large bowl. Add the dried shrimp, cooked shrimp, coconut, peanuts, garlic, and dressing and gently toss until well mixed.
Transfer to a serving plate, sprinkle with the cashew nuts, fried shallots, and chopped cilantro, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Blue Crab and Papaya Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 live blue crabs, about 300 g each, cleaned
1 yard-long bean, cut into 5-7.5 cm pieces
11⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
25 g cashew nuts, roasted raw vegetables, such as yard-long beans and napa (Chinese) cabbage, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the crabs in the freezer for 20 minutes, then remove and put them in a large bowl.

Take one crab and place it on a cutting board. Turn the crab onto its back with its legs facing upward. Raise the tail flap and push a small screwdriver or skewer through the hole underneath. Press firmly down on the screwdriver handle until it reaches the other side of the shell. Remove the screwdriver and repeat with the remaining crab.
Remove the crab apron and carapace and rinse until clean. Cut each crab in half vertically, then cut each piece horizontally. Remove the claws, crush them, and set aside.
Blanch the crab pieces and claws in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes, or until cooked, then drain and set aside.

Finely pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle. Add the papaya, tomatoes, and yard-long bean and pound again. Add the crab and lightly pound and stir at the same time with the pestle and a spoon.
Add the fish sauce, sugar, and lime juice and mix well. Transfer to a serving plate and sprinkle with the cashew nuts. Serve with raw vegetables.

recipes.title: Chicken and Banana Blossom Salad

lines: 2 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, chopped into bite-size pieces
10 kaffir lime leaves, torn, to garnish
3 lemongrass stalks, finely chopped, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Fill a large bowl with water and add the vinegar. Peel away and discard the outer red petals and the small white banana flowers. Trim the tip and base of the blossom, quarter it lengthwise, and place the pieces in the vinegar water.
Peel and clean each layer, discarding the flowers inside. Slice the layers 5 mm thick and return them to the vinegar water. Repeat until the whole blossom is prepared.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add 750 ml water and bring to a boil.
Add the shallots and chicken, return to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes.

Drain and rinse the banana blossom, then add it to the wok and cook for 5 minutes. Add the sawtooth cilantro, scallions, cilantro, Vietnamese cilantro, galangal, and peppermint and cook for 3 minutes.
Garnish with the kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass and serve.

recipes.searchText: Chicken and Banana Blossom Salad North 2 teaspoons white vinegar 1 banana blossom 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 3 cloves garlic, chopped 75 ml Larb Chili Paste (see p. 41) 5 shallots, chopped 2 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, chopped into bite-size pieces 3 tablespoons chopped sawtooth cilantro (coriander) 3 tablespoons chopped scallions (spring onions) 3 tablespoons chopped cilantro (coriander) 1 tablespoon chopped Vietnamese cilantro (coriander) 10 slices galangal 10 peppermint leaves, tom 10 kaffir lime leaves, torn, to garnish 3 lemongrass stalks, finely chopped, to garnish Fill a large bowl with water and add the vinegar. Peel away and discard the outer red petals and the small white banana flowers. Trim the tip and base of the blossom, quarter it lengthwise, and place the pieces in the vinegar water. Peel and clean each layer, discarding the flowers inside. Slice the layers 5 mm thick and return them to the vinegar water. Repeat until the whole blossom is prepared. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add 750 ml water and bring to a boil. Add the shallots and chicken, return to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse the banana blossom, then add it to the wok and cook for 5 minutes. Add the sawtooth cilantro, scallions, cilantro, Vietnamese cilantro, galangal, and peppermint and cook for 3 minutes. Garnish with the kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass and serve.

recipes.title: Indian Trumpet Flower Pod Spicy Salad
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 teaspoon chili powder peppermint leaves, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Dry-fry the flower pod in a wok over medium heat for about 5 minutes, until toasted. Let cool slightly, remove the outer layer, and rinse under cold running water.
Slice the pod into 5 mm pieces. Put it in a bowl with the salt, lime juice, fish sauce, ground toasted rice, scallion, sawtooth cilantro, kaffir lime leaves, and chili powder and toss gently.
Garnish with peppermint leaves and serve.

recipes.searchText: Indian Trumpet Flower Pod Spicy Salad North 1 Indian trumpet flower pod 1 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon lime juice 1 teaspoon fish sauce 1 teaspoon Ground Toasted Rice (see p. 64) 1 tablespoon sliced scallion (spring onion) 1 tablespoon chopped sawtooth cilantro (coriander) 1 teaspoon sliced kaffir lime leaves 1 teaspoon chili powder peppermint leaves, to garnish Dry-fry the flower pod in a wok over medium heat for about 5 minutes, until toasted. Let cool slightly, remove the outer layer, and rinse under cold running water. Slice the pod into 5 mm pieces. Put it in a bowl with the salt, lime juice, fish sauce, ground toasted rice, scallion, sawtooth cilantro, kaffir lime leaves, and chili powder and toss gently. Garnish with peppermint leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Egg Tofu and Ground Pork Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 bunch cilantro (coriander) leaves, coarsely chopped, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the egg tofu, combine the soy milk and salt in a bowl. Add the eggs and whisk gently, avoiding bubbles. Pour into a shallow dish to a depth of about 4 cm. Steam over very low heat for 12-15 minutes, or until firm, then cut into 3 x 3 x 1.5 cm pieces. The egg tofu can be refrigerated for 2-3 days.
Combine the pork and Saam-Gler in a bowl. Add 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and mix well, then shape into small balls.

Bring the broth and 475 ml water to a boil in a pan. Add the pork balls and simmer for 2-3 minutes, or until they float. Add the salt and remaining soy sauce, then add the egg tofu and celery and cook for 2 minutes. Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.searchText: Egg Tofu and Ground Pork Soup Central 200 g ground (minced) pork 11⁄2 teaspoons Saam-Gler (see p. 41) 3 tablespoons soy sauce 475 ml chicken or pork broth (stock) 11⁄2 teaspoons salt 2 celery stalks, chopped 1 bunch cilantro (coriander) leaves, coarsely chopped, to garnish 300 ml soy milk 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 3 eggs For the egg tofu, combine the soy milk and salt in a bowl. Add the eggs and whisk gently, avoiding bubbles. Pour into a shallow dish to a depth of about 4 cm. Steam over very low heat for 12-15 minutes, or until firm, then cut into 3 x 3 x 1.5 cm pieces. The egg tofu can be refrigerated for 2-3 days. Combine the pork and Saam-Gler in a bowl. Add 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and mix well, then shape into small balls. Bring the broth and 475 ml water to a boil in a pan. Add the pork balls and simmer for 2-3 minutes, or until they float. Add the salt and remaining soy sauce, then add the egg tofu and celery and cook for 2 minutes. Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.title: Fermented Fish and Jackfruit Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 broiled (grilled) sea bass or sea bream, cut into bite-size pieces
1 kg young jackfruit, peeled and seeded wearing gloves, and cut into 2.5 cm slices
100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the shallots, garlic, fingerroot, and lemongrass thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the broiled (grilled) fish and pound until combined. Bring the coconut milk to a boil in another pan over medium heat, add the pounded fish paste and the fermented fish, return to a boil, and add the pork Return to a boil and add the jackfruit then continue to boil for 5 minutes until cooked. Add the salt, fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, and kaffir lime leaves and stir. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.searchText: Fermented Fish and Jackfruit Soup Central 1 shallot, chopped 2 cloves garlic, chopped 40 g chopped fingerroot 1 lemongrass stalk, chopped 1 broiled (grilled) sea bass or sea bream, cut into bite-size pieces 1 liter coconut milk 100 g fermented fish, bones removed 300 g pork side (belly), diced 1 kg young jackfruit, peeled and seeded wearing gloves, and cut into 2.5 cm slices 1 teaspoon salt 3 tablespoons fish sauce 100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 4 teaspoons Tamarind Puree (see p. 63) 10 kaffir lime leaves Pound the shallots, garlic, fingerroot, and lemongrass thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the broiled (grilled) fish and pound until combined. Bring the coconut milk to a boil in another pan over medium heat, add the pounded fish paste and the fermented fish, return to a boil, and add the pork Return to a boil and add the jackfruit then continue to boil for 5 minutes until cooked. Add the salt, fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, and kaffir lime leaves and stir. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Mullet Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 piece fresh ginger, about 7 cm, peeled and sliced
1 piece galangal, about 7.5 cm, peeled and sliced
1 gray mullet or red snapper, about 500 g, cleaned, descaled, and cut into 5 cm pieces
75 ml mangrove palm vinegar, white wine vinegar, or Tamarind Puree (see p. 63)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 960 ml water to a boil in a large pan. Add the ginger, galangal, lemongrass, chiles, and shallots, return to a boil, and cook for 5 minutes. Carefully add the fish and cook for another 5 minutes. Season with the vinegar and salt. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.searchText: Mullet Soup Central 1 piece fresh ginger, about 7 cm, peeled and sliced 1 piece galangal, about 7.5 cm, peeled and sliced 11⁄2 lemongrass stalks, sliced 2 shallots, thinly sliced 1 gray mullet or red snapper, about 500 g, cleaned, descaled, and cut into 5 cm pieces 4-5 red bird's-eye chiles, finely chopped 75 ml mangrove palm vinegar, white wine vinegar, or Tamarind Puree (see p. 63) 1⁄2 teaspoon salt Bring 960 ml water to a boil in a large pan. Add the ginger, galangal, lemongrass, chiles, and shallots, return to a boil, and cook for 5 minutes. Carefully add the fish and cook for another 5 minutes. Season with the vinegar and salt. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy-and-Sour Mackerel Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400-500 g horse mackerel, cleaned and descaled
10 green and red bird's-eye chiles, sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the salt, lemongrass, garlic, and kaffir lime leaves and boil for 2-3 minutes.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice, stir, and increase the heat to high. Add the mackerel and return to a boil without stirring.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Add the chiles and cilantro and stir. Ladle into soup bowls and serve hot.

recipes.searchText: Spicy-and-Sour Mackerel Soup Central 1.2 liters chicken broth (stock) 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 1 lemongrass stalk, crushed and sliced 3 cloves garlic, coarsely pounded 4 kaffir lime leaves, torn 3 tablespoons fish sauce 3 tablespoons lime juice 400-500 g horse mackerel, cleaned and descaled 10 green and red bird's-eye chiles, sliced 2 tablespoons chopped cilantro (coriander) Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the salt, lemongrass, garlic, and kaffir lime leaves and boil for 2-3 minutes. Add the fish sauce and lime juice, stir, and increase the heat to high. Add the mackerel and return to a boil without stirring. Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Add the chiles and cilantro and stir. Ladle into soup bowls and serve hot.

recipes.title: Sweet-and-Sour Mackerel Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 5 small whole mackerel, cleaned and descaled
1 x 2.5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the cilantro roots, salt, shrimp paste, and shallots together in a mortar with a pestle.
Bring the broth or water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the pounded mixture, stir, and return to a boil.
Add the tamarind, sugar, and fish sauce and return to a boil. Add the mackerel and cook for about 10 minutes.
Add the ginger and scallions and stir. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the dried chiles, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Sweet-and-Sour Mackerel Soup Central 3 cilantro (coriander) roots, chopped 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon shrimp paste 4 shallots, chopped 800 ml fish broth (stock) or water 4 tablespoons Tamarind Puree (see p. 63) 1 tablespoon granulated sugar 1 tablespoon fish sauce 5 small whole mackerel, cleaned and descaled 1 x 2.5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned 25 g chopped scallions (spring onions) 5 dried red chiles, seeded Pound the cilantro roots, salt, shrimp paste, and shallots together in a mortar with a pestle. Bring the broth or water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the pounded mixture, stir, and return to a boil. Add the tamarind, sugar, and fish sauce and return to a boil. Add the mackerel and cook for about 10 minutes. Add the ginger and scallions and stir. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the dried chiles, and serve.

recipes.title: Sea Bass Soup with Cardamom Shoots
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g sea bass fillet, cut into 4 cm pieces
200 g Siam cardamom shoots, cut into 4 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Add the sea bass, cardamom shoots, and salacca (snake fruit).
Return to a boil and add the kaffir lime leaves, fish sauce, lime juice, chiles, and cilantro. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.searchText: Sea Bass Soup with Cardamom Shoots Central 500 g sea bass fillet, cut into 4 cm pieces 200 g Siam cardamom shoots, cut into 4 cm lengths 200 g salacca (snake fruit), peeled 2-3 kaffir lime leaves, torn 1 tablespoon fish sauce 1 teaspoon lime juice 3-8 green bird's-eye chiles, chopped 1 small handful cilantro (coriander), chopped Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Add the sea bass, cardamom shoots, and salacca (snake fruit). Return to a boil and add the kaffir lime leaves, fish sauce, lime juice, chiles, and cilantro. Cook for 3-4 minutes. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Sea Bass in Herb Soup
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 teaspoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
500 g sea bass fillets, cut into bite-size chunks

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan. Add the fish sauce, shrimp paste, shallots, and garlic and return to a boil.
Add the tamarind sauce and sugar and return to a boil. Add the sea bass and cook for 3-5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and add the sweet basil, star gooseberry, and hairy basil leaves. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.searchText: Sea Bass in Herb Soup South 2 tablespoons fish sauce 1⁄2 tablespoon shrimp paste 4 shallots, chopped 3 cloves garlic, chopped 2 tablespoons tamarind sauce 1 teaspoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 500 g sea bass fillets, cut into bite-size chunks 20 sweet basil leaves 20 star gooseberry leaves 20 hairy basil leaves Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan. recipes.title: Sea Bass and Rice Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 x 300 g sea bass, cleaned, filleted, and cut into 3-4 cm slices, bones reserved

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish
lines: 5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the shiitake mushrooms in warm water for 15 minutes. Squeeze dry, cut into quarters, and set aside.
Bring the chicken broth and 350 ml water to a boil in a large pan over high heat. Add the galangal, garlic, black pepper, and fish bones and boil for 4-5 minutes without stirring.
Strain through a fine strainer into a clean pan. Return to a boil over medium heat, add the soy sauce, fish sauce, and shiitake mushrooms, and stir.
Return to a boil, add the sea bass, and cook for 2 minutes without stirring, or until the fish is cooked. Add the rice and celery and boil for another 1-2 minutes.
Ladle into soup bowls, garnish with fried garlic, scallions, cilantro, and ginger, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Sea Bass and Rice Soup Central 5 dried shiitake mushrooms 475 ml chicken broth (stock) 2 thin slices galangal, pounded 2 cloves garlic 1 teaspoon ground black pepper 1 x 300 g sea bass, cleaned, filleted, and cut into 3-4 cm slices, bones reserved 1 tablespoon soy sauce 1 teaspoon fish sauce 260 g cooked long-grain rice 30 g chopped Chinese celery 3 tablespoons Fried Garlic (see p. 64) 2-3 scallions (spring onions), chopped 1 handful cilantro (coriander), chopped 5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned Soak the shiitake mushrooms in warm water for 15 minutes. Squeeze dry, cut into quarters, and set aside. Bring the chicken broth and 350 ml water to a boil in a large pan over high heat. Add the galangal, garlic, black pepper, and fish bones and boil for 4-5 minutes without stirring. Strain through a fine strainer into a clean pan. Return to a boil over medium heat, add the soy sauce, fish sauce, and shiitake mushrooms, and stir. Return to a boil, add the sea bass, and cook for 2 minutes without stirring, or until the fish is cooked. Add the rice and celery and boil for another 1-2 minutes. Ladle into soup bowls, garnish with fried garlic, scallions, cilantro, and ginger, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy-and-Sour Soup with Egg Noodles
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g squid, halved and tentacles removed
4 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Rinse the sea bass and pat dry. Put it in a pan with enough water to cover by about 1 inch (2.5 cm) and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 2-3 minutes, until cooked, then drain.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, or according to the package directions. Drain, transfer to a serving bowl, and set aside.

Put the galangal, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, shallots, mushrooms, tomatoes, squid, shrimp, and cooked fish in a large pan. Add the Chili Jam, salt, lime juice, fish sauce, and milk. Pour in the chicken broth, bring to a simmer, and cook for about 3 minutes, until hot. Pour over the noodles, garnish with cilantro, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy-and-Sour Soup with Egg Noodles South 120 g sea bass fillets, skinned 100 g egg noodles 3 slices galangal 4 kaffir lime leaves, torn 2 lemongrass stalks, chopped 3 shallots, halved 4 straw mushrooms, halved 2 tomatoes, quartered 100 g squid, halved and tentacles removed 4 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact 2 tablespoons Chili Jam (see p. 35) 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 2 tablespoons lime juice 2 tablespoons fish sauce 3 tablespoons milk 750 ml chicken broth (stock) 3 sprigs cilantro (coriander) Rinse the sea bass and pat dry. recipes.title: Spicy Snakehead Fish and Lotus Stem Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3 lemongrass stalks, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
800 g snakehead fish or catfish, cleaned, descaled, and cut into 2.5 cm pieces
200 g peeled and sliced lotus stem
4-6 dried red chiles, seeded and chopped
2 sawtooth cilantro (coriander) sprigs, chopped, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, shallots, tamarind, and salt and return to a boil.
Add the fish and lotus stem and cook for about 8 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Add the fish sauce, lemon juice, and chiles. Ladle into soup bowls, garnish with sawtooth cilantro, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Snakehead Fish and Lotus Stem Soup Central 950 ml water 3 lemongrass stalks, cut into 2.5 cm pieces 4-5 slices galangal 6 kaffir lime leaves 2-3 shallots, sliced 2 tablespoons Tamarind Puree (see p. 63) 1 teaspoon salt 800 g snakehead fish or catfish, cleaned, descaled, and cut into 2.5 cm pieces 200 g peeled and sliced lotus stem 2 tablespoons fish sauce 2 tablespoons lemon juice 4-6 dried red chiles, seeded and chopped 2 sawtooth cilantro (coriander) sprigs, chopped, to garnish Bring the water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the fish sauce, lemon juice, and chiles. Ladle into soup bowls, garnish with sawtooth cilantro, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Vegetable Soup
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g chayote shoots or young spinach

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, garlic, shallots, and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix to combine.
Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat, add the chili paste, and stir until dissolved. Add the dried fish and return to a boil.

Reduce the heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the fish softens. Add the chayote shoots or spinach and the tomatoes and simmer, stirring occasionally, for another 3-4 minutes. Ladle into bowls and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Vegetable Soup North 350 ml vegetable broth (stock) 50 g chopped dried snakehead fish 100 g chayote shoots or young spinach 5 cherry tomatoes 5 dried red chiles 5 cloves garlic, sliced 3 shallots, chopped 1 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon shrimp paste For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, garlic, shallots, and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix to combine. recipes.title: Salmon Sour Soup
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 x 40 g salmon fillets, cut into 1 cm-thick slices
1 x 5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 scallions (spring onions), cut into 2 cm lengths
4 dried red chiles, seeded, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the paste, pound the black peppercorns, shallots, and cilantro roots in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix until thoroughly combined.
Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the paste and crushed shallots and boil for 1-2 minutes.
Add the salmon and ginger, return to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Add the tamarind, sugar, and fish sauce, followed by the scallions. Ladle into a soup bowl, garnish with the dried chiles, and serve.

Ladle into a soup bowl, garnish with the dried chiles, and serve.

recipes.title: Very Spicy Papaya and Young Coconut Soup
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 liters water Juice of 2 limes, strained
600 g mixed fruit, such as young papaya, young coconut meat, ripe banana, pineapple, and pickled bamboo
1 kg sea bass, mullet, or king mackerel fillets, cut into 2.5-5 cm pieces
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the dried and fresh chiles, turmeric, garlic, and shallots in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix until thoroughly combined.
Bring the water to a boil in a large pan. Add the chili paste and lime juice and return to a boil, then add all the fruit.
Return to a boil, add the fish, and cook for 5 minutes. Season with the salt and sugar, ladle into soup bowls, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Vegetable and Fish Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g whole snakehead fish, cleaned, skinned, head and bones removed, and cut into 5 cm pieces
100 g pumpkin, cut into 2.5 cm slices
200 g angled gourd, peeled, halved, and cut into 2 cm-thick slices
10-15 young Ceylon spinach or ordinary spinach leaves

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, pound the chiles, salt, peppercorns, fingerroot, shallots, and shrimp paste together thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish and pound again until smooth. Set aside.

Bring the chicken broth (stock) to a boil in a pan over high heat. Add the chili paste and fish sauce and return to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium, add the pumpkin and baby corn, and return to a boil for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms, angled gourd, Ceylon spinach, ivy gourd leaves, if using, and basil. Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy-and-Sour Tilapia Soup
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 lemongrass stalks, coarsely crushed and cut into 5 cm lengths
600 g tilapia, cleaned, filleted, and cut into bite-size pieces
10-15 red and green bird's-eye chiles, pounded

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the broth and salt to a boil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Add the galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, shallots, and garlic and boil for about 2 minutes.
Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and tomatoes and return to a boil.
Add the tilapia and cook for 3-4 minutes without stirring, until cooked.
Stir in the chiles and cilantro, ladle into bowls, and serve.

Add the tilapia and cook for 3-4 minutes without stirring, until cooked. Stir in the chiles and cilantro, ladle into bowls, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Eel Soup
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3 lemongrass stalks, diagonally sliced into 4 cm lengths
300 g eel, cleaned and cut into 5 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the broth and 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan.
Add the fingerroot, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, lemongrass, garlic, shallots, and chile powder and return to a boil.
Add the eel and return to a boil. Add the fish sauce and tamarind puree and boil for 7-10 minutes, until the eel is tender.
Stir in the basil, if using. Ladle into bowls and serve.

3 scallions, cut into 4 cm lengths, to garnish

Add the onion and tomatoes and return to a boil. Add the mushrooms and shrimp and boil for about 1 minute, until the shrimp are cooked.
Add the lime juice, chiles, sugar, fish sauce, and shallots and stir. Ladle into bowls, garnish with cilantro and scallions, and serve.

lines: 1 handful melinjo leaves or young spinach
4-5 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan. Add the shrimp paste, sugar, and salt, stir, and return to a boil.
Add the melinjo leaves and shrimp and return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2 minutes, or until the shrimp are cooked. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, fingerroot, peppercorns, and shallots in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and dried shrimp and mix until combined.
Bring 475 ml water and the chili paste to a simmer in a pan over low heat. Add the fish sauce, salt, and sugar and stir well.
Add the shrimp, pumpkin, angled loofah, watermelons, waxy corn, bottle gourd, and dried shrimp. Stir well and cook for 7-10 minutes. Add the lemon basil leaves and serve.

recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 × 30 g dried squid, sliced crosswise into 2 cm-wide pieces
400 g soft-bone pork ribs, cleaned and chopped into 4 cm pieces
400 g daikon (mooli) radish, peeled, halved lengthwise, and cut crosswise into 2 cm-thick pieces
3 scallions (spring onions), chopped into 4 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the dried squid in water for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Bring 950 ml water, the salt, peppercorns, and cilantro roots to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs and boil for 4-5 minutes, then add the daikon and boil for another 4-5 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and soaked squid. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the cilantro and scallions, and serve.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200-250 g small squid, cleaned, with tentacles removed and reserved

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the garlic and peppercorns to a smooth paste. Transfer to a large bowl, add the pork and 1 teaspoon soy sauce, and mix well. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes.
Stuff the pork mixture into the squid cavities, then lightly score each squid once or twice.
Pour the broth and 350 ml water into a large pan. Add the cilantro root and salt and bring to a boil over medium heat. Add the stuffed squid and tentacles and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until cooked.
Add the remaining soy sauce and Chinese celery and stir a few times. Remove from the heat, ladle into soup bowls, and serve.

recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, then drain and blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, or prepare according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the fish balls in boiling water for 2 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
For the soup, combine the broth, cilantro roots, garlic, peppercorns, salt, soy sauce, and sugar in a pan. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Divide the noodles and bean sprouts among serving bowls. Pour about 300 ml soup into each bowl and top with the fish balls, fish cake, scallions, cilantro, and Fried Garlic. Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Buffalo Meat Soup

lines: 11⁄4 kg buffalo meat or beef brisket, diced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the cilantro, scallions, and sawtooth cilantro, and serve.

recipes.title: Oxtail Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 kg oxtail, cut into 2.5-5 cm pieces
7 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the cardamom pods, bay leaves, cilantro roots, garlic, and peppercorns into a herb infuser and set aside.

Bring 3 liters water to a boil over high heat. Add the oxtail and boil for 20-30 minutes, skimming away any scum. Add the herb infuser and cinnamon, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 2 hours, or until the oxtail is tender.
Remove the oxtail and set aside. Strain the soup through cheesecloth into a clean pan and bring it back to a boil over medium heat, adding more water if necessary.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the onion and ginger and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until softened. Transfer to the soup, add the tomatoes, and cook for another 30 minutes.
Ladle into serving bowls and season with the fish sauce and lime juice. Garnish with the chiles, fried shallots, celery, scallions, cilantro, and lime wedges and serve.

recipes.title: Clear Soup with Pork Balls and Noodles
recipes.subtitle: Central
recipes.prepTime: 10 minutes, plus soaking and marrating times

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in a bowl of water for 5 minutes, or according to package directions. Drain, cut into short lengths, and set aside.
Mix the pork, 1 tablespoon sugar, and the soy sauce in a large bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes. Add the noodles, mix together, shape into small balls, and set aside.
Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the fish sauce and remaining sugar, then add the pork balls.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 4-5 minutes, or until the pork balls float to the surface. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the cilantro leaves, and serve.

lines: 700 g pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
4 pieces rock sugar or 1⁄2 tablespoon granulated sugar

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish
lines: 40 g chopped scallions (spring onions) and cilantro (coriander)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the broth (stock) put the cinnamon stick, star anise, garlic, peppercorns and Cilantro (coriander) roots into an herb infuser.

Soak the vermicelli in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, then drain and blanch in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute or prepare according to package directions, until cooked. Drain.

Divide the vermicelli, fried garlic oil, cooked pork, and bean sprouts among serving bowls. Pour 350 ml of the broth into each bowl and garnish with the radish, scallions (spring onions), and cilantro (coriander). Serve.

recipes.title: Red Sauce Noodle Soup

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 daikon (mooli) radish, cut diagonally into 1 cm-thick slices

ingredientGroups.heading: For the soup
lines: 100 g water spinach, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
8 pieces cooked squid, cut into 2.5 cm pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the pork stock to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the cilantro roots, daikon, and salt and return to a boil. Boil for 5 minutes, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for another 5 minutes.
For the red sauce, put all its ingredients in a food processor with 75 ml water and process until smooth. Set aside.

Divide the water spinach, noodles, squid, pig's blood curd, fish balls, tofu, red sauce, and pickled chiles among serving bowls. Pour 250 ml pork stock into each bowl, place a fried wonton on top, and serve.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 Chinese fish cakes, cut into 2 cm pieces
2 tablespoons chopped salted dried cabbage leaves
4 tablespoons chopped salted radish fish sauce, to taste granulated sugar, to taste
50 g finely chopped scallions (spring onions) and cilantro (coriander), to garnish

ingredientGroups.heading: For the wontons
lines: 100 g wonton wrappers vegetable oil, for drizzling

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the roasted pork, combine the pork, Saam-Gler, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, five-spice powder, and food coloring in a bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator overnight, or for at least 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 325°F/160°C. Put the pork in a roasting pan and roast for 45-55 minutes, or until cooked through. Let cool, then slice.

For the wontons, combine the pork, Saam-Gler, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sugar in a bowl. Put 1 teaspoon of filling in the center of each wrapper, dampen the edges, and fold into a triangle. Cook the wontons in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, or until they float. Drain and drizzle with a little oil.
For the soup, bring the broth to a boil with the cilantro roots, garlic, peppercorns, salt, soy sauce, and daikon. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Soak the rice noodles in water for 10 minutes, then blanch for about 1 minute, or cook according to the package directions. Drain. Blanch the ground pork for 2-3 minutes and drain.

Divide the noodles, roasted pork, wontons, blanched pork, Fried Garlic, fish cakes, peanuts, cabbage, and radish among six bowls. Add about 250 ml hot soup to each bowl. Season with fish sauce and sugar to taste, garnish with the scallion and cilantro mixture, and serve.

lines: 200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

steps: Soak the dried noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, until soft. Drain and set aside.

Pour a little sauce and 350 ml soup into each bowl. Add the pork liver, sliced pork, eggs, yard-long beans, lettuce, scallion, and cilantro, then serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Pork Soup with Straw Mushrooms
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 800 g pork short ribs, cut into bite-size pieces
15 red and green bird's eye chiles pounded

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water and the pork ribs to a boil in a large pan over medium heat, then reduce the heat and simmer for 40 minutes. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Drain and set aside.

Heat the broth (stock) in a pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, mushrooms, boiled meat, chiles, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and cilantro (coriander). Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the fried shallots and chili flakes, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Pork Soup with Straw Mushrooms Central 800 g pork short ribs, cut into bite-size pieces 1.2 liters vegetable or chicken broth 2 lemongrass stalks, sliced 100 g straw mushrooms, halved 15 red and green bird's eye chiles pounded 2 tablespoons fish sauce 3 tablespoons lime juice 1 tablespoon granulated sugar 1 sawtooth cilantro (coriander) sprig, chopped 3 tablespoons Fried Shallots (Bee p. 64) 1⁄2 tablespoon dried chili flakes Bring 1.2 liters water and the pork ribs to a boil in a large pan over medium heat, then reduce the heat and simmer for 40 minutes. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Drain and set aside. Heat the broth (stock) in a pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, mushrooms, boiled meat, chiles, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and cilantro (coriander). Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the fried shallots and chili flakes, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Pork and Madan Leaf Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg boneless pork leg, cut into bite-size pieces
120 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1.5 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chile paste, dry-fry the galangal, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, and cilantro root in a wok over medium heat for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Transfer to a mortar and pound with the dried chiles, salt, and shrimp paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chile paste and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the pork, fish sauce, and sugar and mix well. Transfer to a pan, add the coconut milk, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the pork softens. Add the madan leaves and return to a boil. Ladle into bowls and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Pork and Madan Leaf Soup Central 1 tablespoon vegetable oil 1 kg boneless pork leg, cut into bite-size pieces 120 ml fish sauce 120 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 250 ml coconut milk 200 g young madan leaves 1.5 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped 2 shallots, sliced 1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped 2 lemongrass stalks, sliced 1 teaspoon chopped cilantro root 15 dried red chiles 1 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon Roasted Shrimp Paste (see p. 36) For the chile paste, dry-fry the galangal, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, and cilantro root in a wok over medium heat for 1 minute, until fragrant. Transfer to a mortar and pound with the dried chiles, salt, and shrimp paste. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chile paste and sauté for 1 minute. Add the pork, fish sauce, and sugar and mix well. Transfer to a pan, add the coconut milk, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the pork softens. Add the madan leaves and return to a boil. Ladle into bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Roasted Duck Noodle Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: For the roasted duck
lines: 1 kg whole duck, cleaned and without giblets
11⁄4 tablespoons black salted soybeans, finely pounded

ingredientGroups.heading: For the soup
lines: 1 small cinnamon stick, broken into small pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F/150°C/Gas Mark 2.
Rinse the duck in cold water and pat dry. Rub it all over with the salt flakes and leave for 30 minutes. Rinse off the salt, pat dry, and set aside.

Pound the ginger, garlic, and cilantro roots until smooth. Mix with the five-spice powder, salted soybeans, salt, liquor or brandy, and sugar. Put the mixture inside the duck and place the duck on a roasting tray.

For the honey sauce, mix the honey, thick soy sauce, and 75 ml water. Brush the duck all over 2-3 times, then roast for about 13⁄4 hours, or until cooked, brushing with more sauce every 30 minutes. Cover with foil and rest for at least 15 minutes. Remove the drumsticks, carve the meat, and slice it into strips.

For the soup, heat the broth over medium heat. Put the star anise, cinnamon, garlic, cilantro roots, and black pepper in a spice bag and add it to the broth. Boil for 5 minutes. Season with soy sauce, salt, sugar, and dark soy sauce. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.

Divide the noodles, bean sprouts, scallions, fried garlic, and duck among bowls. Pour about 250 ml soup into each bowl. Season to taste with vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, and chili flakes, if using, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Roasted Duck Noodle Soup Central 1 kg whole duck, cleaned and without giblets 70 g salt flakes 5 slices fresh ginger 4 cloves garlic, chopped 3-4 cilantro (coriander) roots, chopped 1 teaspoon five-spice powder 11⁄4 tablespoons black salted soybeans, finely pounded 1 teaspoon salt 1 tablespoon 53-proof liquor or brandy 1 tablespoon sugar 2 tablespoons honey 1 tablespoon thick soy sauce 1.75 liters chicken broth (stock) 2 star anise 1 small cinnamon stick, broken into small pieces 2 cloves garlic, coarsely crushed 2 cilantro (coriander) roots, coarsely crushed 1⁄2 teaspoon ground black pepper 2 tablespoons soy sauce 1 teaspoon salt 11⁄2 teaspoons granulated sugar 1 teaspoon dark soy sauce 300 g fresh green egg noodles (ramen) 100 g bean sprouts 20 g finely sliced scallions (spring onions) 4 tablespoons Fried Garlic (see p. 64) 60 ml white rice vinegar (optional) 60 ml soy sauce (optional) 50 g superfine (caster) sugar (optional) 2 tablespoons dried chili flakes (optional) Preheat the oven to 300°F/150°C/Gas Mark 2. Rinse the duck in cold water and pat dry. Rub it all over with the salt flakes and leave for 30 minutes. Rinse off the salt, pat dry, and set aside. Pound the ginger, garlic, and cilantro roots until smooth. Mix with the five-spice powder, salted soybeans, salt, liquor or brandy, and sugar. Put the mixture inside the duck and place the duck on a roasting tray. For the honey sauce, mix the honey, thick soy sauce, and 75 ml water. Brush the duck all over 2-3 times, then roast for about 13⁄4 hours, or until cooked, brushing with more sauce every 30 minutes. Cover with foil and rest for at least 15 minutes. Remove the drumsticks, carve the meat, and slice it into strips. For the soup, heat the broth over medium heat. Put the star anise, cinnamon, garlic, cilantro roots, and black pepper in a spice bag and add it to the broth. Boil for 5 minutes. Season with soy sauce, salt, sugar, and dark soy sauce. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes. Divide the noodles, bean sprouts, scallions, fried garlic, and duck among bowls. Pour about 250 ml soup into each bowl. Season to taste with vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, and chili flakes, if using, and serve.

recipes.title: Chicken and Coconut Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g black-skinned chicken breast or boneless chicken thigh, cut into 3 × 4 cm pieces
2 whole young coconuts, opened at the top and drained, with tops reserved as lids
4 dried red bird's-eye chiles, seeded, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the chicken broth and salt to a boil over medium heat.
Pound the cilantro root, shallot, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves to a paste. Add it to the pan and boil for 1-2 minutes.
Add the chicken and boil for 3-4 minutes, or until cooked. Add the young coconut flesh, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and coconut milk and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add the chopped chiles and cilantro. Ladle the soup into the whole young coconuts, garnish with Chili Jam oil and the dried chiles, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Chicken and Coconut Soup Central 800 ml chicken broth (stock) 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 1 cilantro (coriander) root 1 shallot, halved 2 lemongrass stalks, diagonally sliced 6 thin slices galangal 4 kaffir lime leaves, torn 300 g black-skinned chicken breast or boneless chicken thigh, cut into 3 × 4 cm pieces 100 g young coconut flesh 11⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce 21⁄2 teaspoons lime juice 1⁄2 teaspoon granulated sugar 200 ml coconut milk 1-2 red bird's-eye chiles, chopped 10 g chopped cilantro (coriander) 1 teaspoon Chili Jam oil (see p. 35) 2 whole young coconuts, opened at the top and drained, with tops reserved as lids 4 dried red bird's-eye chiles, seeded, to garnish Bring the chicken broth and salt to a boil over medium heat. Ladle the soup into the whole young coconuts, garnish with Chili Jam oil and the dried chiles, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Chicken and Taro Soup
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g chicken, either half a whole chicken or boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
200 g taro, peeled and cut into 3 cm dice
20 g chopped scallions (spring onions), to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, peppercorns, garlic, shallots, and lemongrass to a smooth paste. Add the shrimp paste and mix to combine.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and cook for 1 minute, or until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil. Add the taro and salt, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 4-5 minutes, or until the taro is tender.
Remove from the heat, ladle into soup bowls, garnish with the scallions and cilantro, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Chicken and Taro Soup North 3 tablespoons vegetable oil 300 g chicken, either half a whole chicken or boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces 475 ml chicken broth (stock) 200 g taro, peeled and cut into 3 cm dice 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 20 g chopped scallions (spring onions), to garnish 10 g chopped cilantro (coriander), to garnish 5 dried red bird's-eye chiles, chopped 1⁄2 teaspoon Sichuan peppercorns 5 cloves garlic, chopped 2 small shallots, chopped 1 lemongrass stalk, finely sliced 1 teaspoon shrimp paste For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, peppercorns, garlic, shallots, and lemongrass to a smooth paste. Add the shrimp paste and mix to combine. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and cook for 1 minute, or until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes. Pour in the broth and bring to a boil. Add the taro and salt, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 4-5 minutes, or until the taro is tender. Remove from the heat, ladle into soup bowls, garnish with the scallions and cilantro, and serve.

recipes.title: Pickled Lime
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 winter melon, peeled, seeded, and cut into 7 x 3 cm pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak: the shiitake mushrooms in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes, then squeeze to drain, slice into bite-size pieces, and set aside. Bring the broth (stock) and 750 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, cilantro (coriander) root, and salt and return to a boil. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes. Add the pickled lime juice, pickled limes. and shiitake mushrooms, then simmer again for 10 minutes. Add the winter melon and soy sauce and continue to simmer for another 20 minutes or until the chicken and winter melon are tender. Stir gently. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with white pepper, and serve.

recipes.title: Sour-and-spicy Chicken Soup with Tamarind Leaves
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 lemongrass stalks, cut into 4 cm diagonal slices
1 whole 400 g chicken, chopped with the bone into small pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the broth (stock) and salt to a boil over high heat in a large pan. Add the galangal lemongrass, and shallots and boil for 1 minute. Had the chicken and return to a boil. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until cooked and tender. Add the fish sauce, kaffir lime leaves young tamarind leaves, tomatoes, and chiles Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.searchText: Sour-and-spicy Chicken Soup with Tamarind Leaves Northeast 950 ml chicken broth (stock) 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 3 thin slices galangal 2 lemongrass stalks, cut into 4 cm diagonal slices 3 small shallots, coarsely crushed 1 whole 400 g chicken, chopped with the bone into small pieces 2 tablespoons fish sauce 4 kaffir lime leaves, torn 1 handful young tamarind leaves 2 tomatoes, cut into wedges 5 red bird's-eye chiles, lightly pounded Bring the broth (stock) and salt to a boil over high heat in a large pan. Add the galangal lemongrass, and shallots and boil for 1 minute. Had the chicken and return to a boil. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until cooked and tender. Add the fish sauce, kaffir lime leaves young tamarind leaves, tomatoes, and chiles Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Daylily and Shiitake Mushroom Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 250 g pork short ribs, cut into bite-size pieces
2 tablespoons goji berries salt, to taste

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs, white pepper, garlic, and cilantro roots and return to a boil. Skim, reduce the heat, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender.
Meanwhile, soak the daylily in water for 15-20 minutes. Rinse it 4-5 times under cold running water and squeeze dry. Discard the coarse stems and tie each daylily into a knot.
Add the daylily, shiitake mushrooms, and goji berries to the pan and simmer for about 10 minutes, or until the daylily has softened. Season to taste, ladle into bowls, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Daylily and Shiitake Mushroom Soup Central 250 g pork short ribs, cut into bite-size pieces 1 teaspoon ground white pepper 6-7 cloves garlic, pounded 3 cilantro (coriander) roots 30 g dried daylily 8 shiitake mushrooms, rinsed 2 tablespoons goji berries salt, to taste Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs, white pepper, garlic, and cilantro roots and return to a boil. Skim, reduce the heat, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender. Meanwhile, soak the daylily in water for 15-20 minutes. Rinse it 4-5 times under cold running water and squeeze dry. Discard the coarse stems and tie each daylily into a knot. Add the daylily, shiitake mushrooms, and goji berries to the pan and simmer for about 10 minutes, or until the daylily has softened. Season to taste, ladle into bowls, and serve.

recipes.title: Shiitake and Stinkhorn Mushroom Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1 liter water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs and return to a boil. Skim, reduce the heat, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender.

Meanwhile, soak the shiitake and stinkhorn mushrooms separately in hot water for about 15 minutes. Squeeze the softened shiitakes dry and cut into bite-size pieces. Rinse the stinkhorns to remove any dirt, squeeze dry, and cut into bite-size pieces.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and sauté for 1-2 minutes, or until dry. Season with some of the soy sauce, then remove from the heat.
When the pork-rib broth is clear, add the goji berries, red dates, salt, black pepper, and remaining soy sauce. When the ribs are tender, add the mushrooms. Ladle into bowls and serve.

recipes.searchText: Shiitake and Stinkhorn Mushroom Soup Central 500 g pork short ribs, chopped 25 g dried shiitake mushrooms, rinsed 30 g dried stinkhorn mushrooms, sliced 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 80 ml soy sauce 1 tablespoon goji berries 1 tablespoon red dates, chopped 1 teaspoon salt 2 teaspoons ground black pepper Bring 1 liter water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs and return to a boil. Skim, reduce the heat, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender. Season with some of the soy sauce, then remove from the heat. When the pork-rib broth is clear, add the goji berries, red dates, salt, black pepper, and remaining soy sauce. When the ribs are tender, add the mushrooms. Ladle into bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Bitter Gourd and Pork Rib Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Trim the ends from the bitter gourd. Halve it lengthwise and scrape out the seeds and white fiber, then halve each piece lengthwise again and cut crosswise into 5 cm lengths.
Dissolve 1 tablespoon salt in 475 ml water. Add the bitter gourd and soak for 15-30 minutes, then drain and rinse.

Pour 950 ml water into a large pan. Add the garlic, cilantro roots, peppercorns, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Add the pork ribs and soy sauce and boil for 4-5 minutes.

Add the bitter gourd and boil for another 10 minutes without stirring, skimming any scum. Reduce the heat, cover, and cook for another 50-60 minutes, or until the pork is tender. Garnish with cilantro and serve.

Halve it lengthwise and scrape out the seeds and white fiber, then halve each piece lengthwise again and cut crosswise into 5 cm lengths. Dissolve 1 tablespoon salt in 475 ml water. Add the bitter gourd and soak for 15-30 minutes, then drain and rinse. Pour 950 ml water into a large pan. Add the bitter gourd and boil for another 10 minutes without stirring, skimming any scum. Reduce the heat, cover, and cook for another 50-60 minutes, or until the pork is tender. Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.title: Pork and Bottle Gourd Soup
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g pork tenderloin or short ribs, sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add the pork, bottle gourd, sugar, and salt and cook for about 30 minutes.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the scallions and cilantro, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Pork and Bottle Gourd Soup North 2 liters water 400 g pork tenderloin or short ribs, sliced 115 g mature bottle gourd, cubed 1 tablespoon granulated sugar 11⁄2 teaspoons salt 3 scallions (spring onions), chopped 4 cilantro (coriander) stalks, chopped Bring the water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the pork, bottle gourd, sugar, and salt and cook for about 30 minutes. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the scallions and cilantro, and serve.

recipes.title: Chinese Cabbage Soup
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g pork side (belly), cut into 2 cm-thick slices
250 g choy sum (Chinese flowering cabbage), cut into 6 cm strips

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the broiler (grill) to medium.
Pound the shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle to a fine paste.
Place the soybean sheet on a broiler pan and broil for about 2 minutes, until fragrant and dark brown. Let cool, then add it to the mortar and pound until ground.
Bring the water to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the pork and salt and boil for 20-30 minutes, until softened, skimming away any scum.
Add the paste, ground soybean sheet, tamarind, fish sauce, sugar, and cabbage and continue boiling for 4-5 minutes, until the cabbage is soft.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the fried garlic and roasted chiles, and serve.

Add the pork and salt and boil for 20-30 minutes, until softened, skimming away any scum. Add the paste, ground soybean sheet, tamarind, fish sauce, sugar, and cabbage and continue boiling for 4-5 minutes, until the cabbage is soft. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the fried garlic and roasted chiles, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Soup with Chinese Mustard Greens
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g Chinese mustard greens scallions (spring onions), chopped to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, and salt together in a mortar with a pestle. Place the soybean sheet on the broiler (grill) pan and broil (grill) for about 2 minutes until fragrant and garlic brown. Let cool, then add to the mortar and pound with the pestle until ground. Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a pan over medium heat, add the Chinese mustard greens, and cook for 3-4 minutes And the chile and shallot mixture, stir, and simmer for 2-3 minutes Ladle into in soup bowls, sprinkle with the scallions spring onions), and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Catfish and Snake Gourd Curry
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g catfish, cleaned, head removed, and cut into 2.5 cm-thick pieces
230 g snake gourd or zucchini (courgette), cut into 2.5 cm-thick slices
a handful of wild bitter gourd leaves or other bitter green leaves
a handful of sweet basil leaves

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: To serve Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378) or Glutinous Rice (see p. 378)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallots, lemongrass, and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside.

Bring the broth to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and boil for 1 minute. Add the fish and ground toasted rice and return to a boil, then season with the fermented fish sauce and fish sauce.

Add the snake gourd or zucchini, both kinds of eggplant, wild bitter gourd leaves, and scallions. Stir gently and boil for 3-5 minutes, or until the vegetables soften. Add the basil, stir again, and remove from the heat. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Spicy Catfish and Jackfruit Curry
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g young jackfruit, peeled and seeded wearing gloves, and cut into 2.5 cm slices

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles and the remaining chili paste ingredients in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside.

Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan, add the chili paste and jackfruit, and cook for 3-4 minutes or until the jackfruit has softened. Add the catfish and cook for another 3-4 minutes, then add the tomatoes, tamarind, fermented fish sauce, and sugar and stir gently. Remove from the heat and sprinkle with the chopped cilantro (coriander) and scallions (spring onions). Serve.

Remove from the heat and sprinkle with the chopped cilantro (coriander) and scallions (spring onions). Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Catfish and Tree Basil Curry
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g catfish, head removed and cut into 2 cm-thick pieces
2 handfuls of tree basil or holy basil leaves, chopped salt

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chili paste, and cook for 1-2 minutes or until fragrant. Add the coconut milk and bring to a boil. Add the fish, cook for 4 minutes, then add the chiles, fish sauce, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Stir and cook for another 1-2 minutes or until the fish is fully flavored. Add the tree basil, stir a couple times, then serve.

recipes.title: Fried Sheatfish Curry

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 x 300 g small white sheatfish, cleaned, gutted
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2-3 orange spur chiles, finely sliced diagonally

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the fish for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Set aside. Bring the coconut milk to boil in a clean wok over medium heat and add the chili paste. Stir for 2 minutes or until thoroughly combined and the coconut milk has thickened. Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and evaporated milk if using. Stir until the sugar has dissolved. Add the fish and cook for 1-2 minutes or until full-favored. Add the chiles and most of the basil leaves. Stir 3-4 times and remove from the heat. Garnish with the remaining basil leaves and serve.
