Season with lime juice and serve with the cucumber, scallions, lime wedges, and extra fish sauce.

recipes.title: Mackerel Fried Rice
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 150 g salted horse mackerel or smoked mackerel fillet
4 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped, plus extra to garnish
1 small cucumber, peeled and sliced, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat 60 ml oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the mackerel and cook for 3 minutes on each side, until beginning to brown. Let cool, then break into smaller pieces.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over medium heat. Add half the shallots and sauté for 1 minute, until softened and fragrant.
Add the rice and stir-fry for about 1 minute. Add the mackerel and soy sauce and stir-fry for another minute.
Add the remaining shallots and the chiles and stir until combined. Transfer to a plate, garnish with chopped chiles, and serve with cucumber and lime wedges.

recipes.searchText: Mackerel Fried Rice Central 60 ml vegetable oil, plus 2 tablespoons 150 g salted horse mackerel or smoked mackerel fillet 2 shallots, sliced 525 g Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378) 1 tablespoon soy sauce 4 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped, plus extra to garnish 1 small cucumber, peeled and sliced, to serve 2 lime wedges, to serve Heat 60 ml oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the remaining shallots and the chiles and stir until combined. Transfer to a plate, garnish with chopped chiles, and serve with cucumber and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Shrimp Paste Fried Rice with Sweet Pork
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 small Chinese pork sausage, diagonally sliced
2 yard-long beans, sliced into 5 mm pieces
120 g pork, cut into small pieces, for the sweet pork
1 tablespoon fish sauce, for the sweet pork
3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar, for the sweet pork
2 teaspoons dark soy sauce, for the sweet pork
2 teaspoons sliced shallot, for the sweet pork

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the roasted shrimp paste in a bowl and add 1 tablespoon boiled water. Stir until the shrimp paste becomes liquid, then add the steamed rice and stir until thoroughly combined. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over medium heat, add the rice, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, then remove from the heat and let cool.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over low heat, add the dried shrimp, and saute for 2 minutes until crispy. Remove the shrimp with a slotted spoon and set aside. Add the sliced Chinese sausage to the wok and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, until cooked, then remove from the heat.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a clean wok over low heat. Roll the oil around the wok so it coats the whole surface of the wok, then pour in the beaten egg and roll around the wok to create a thin omelet. Remove, let cool, then roll up and slice into strips. Set aside.

For the sweet pork, heat 2 tablespoons water in a wok over medium heat, add the pork, fish sauce, and sugar, and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Add the soy sauce and shallot, and stir-fry for 1 minute or until cooked, then remove from the heat.

Place the rice on a serving plate, then arrange the sweet pork, shallots, fried dried shrimp sliced chiles, mango, yard-long beans, and fried dried chiles on the side. Sprinkle with the sliced omelet and serve with the lime.

Add the sliced Chinese sausage to the wok and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, until cooked, then remove from the heat. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a clean wok over low heat. Roll the oil around the wok so it coats the whole surface of the wok, then pour in the beaten egg and roll around the wok to create a thin omelet. Remove, let cool, then roll up and slice into strips. Set aside. Place the rice on a serving plate, then arrange the sweet pork, shallots, fried dried shrimp sliced chiles, mango, yard-long beans, and fried dried chiles on the side. Sprinkle with the sliced omelet and serve with the lime.

recipes.title: Shrimp Paste Fried Rice
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: For the omelet vegetable oil, for frying
For the rice
lines: 500 g Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 318), warm

ingredientGroups.heading: To serve
lines: 5 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped Sweet. Stir-Fried Pork (see p. 346)
1 sour green mango or sour green apple, shredded

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the crispy shrimp, heat the oil in a wok over low-medium heat. Add the dried shrimp and fry for 2-3 minutes until golden brown. Remove from the wok with a slotted spoon and sel aside on paper towels.

In a clean wok, make the omelet. Add 1 teaspoon of oil, and roll around the wok. Add 75 ml of the beaten egg and roll around the wok to create a thin crepe Cook for about 2 minutes until set. Put the omelet on a plate and set aside. Repeat this process with another teaspoon of oil and the remaining egg until all the egg is used, adding a teaspoon of oil at a time. Stack the omelets, then cut them into quarters and slice them into Ys 1 cm-thick strips. Set aside.

Put the cooked rice in a large bowl. Mix 1⁄2 tablespoon water with the shrimp paste until combined, then add to the rice. Using your hands, gently mix until the rice is well coated with shrimp paste. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the garlic and shallot, and saute until fragrant. Add the rice, stir, and toes the mixture for 2-3 minutes until the rice is hot and a slightly darker color.

To serve, fill a small bowl to the rim with the rice and turn upside down in the middle of a serving plate. Top the rice with the chiles, then place the omelet strips, crispy shrimp, pork, mango, sliced shallots, and lime wedges to the side of the rice.

Stir-Fried Pork (see p. 346) 1 sour green mango or sour green apple, shredded 2 shallots, sliced lime wedges To make the crispy shrimp, heat the oil in a wok over low-medium heat. Repeat this process with another teaspoon of oil and the remaining egg until all the egg is used, adding a teaspoon of oil at a time. Stack the omelets, then cut them into quarters and slice them into Ys 1 cm-thick strips. Set aside. Put the cooked rice in a large bowl. Mix 1⁄2 tablespoon water with the shrimp paste until combined, then add to the rice. Using your hands, gently mix until the rice is well coated with shrimp paste. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the garlic and shallot, and saute until fragrant. Add the rice, stir, and toes the mixture for 2-3 minutes until the rice is hot and a slightly darker color. To serve, fill a small bowl to the rim with the rice and turn upside down in the middle of a serving plate. Top the rice with the chiles, then place the omelet strips, crispy shrimp, pork, mango, sliced shallots, and lime wedges to the side of the rice.

recipes.title: Fried Brown Rice with Shrimp
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and tails intact

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the shrimp (prawns) and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until they turn pink. Add the eggs and cook for 1 minute until cooked. Add the rice and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the tofu, sugar, and soy sauce and stir-fry for another 1 minute until fragrant. Add the peas, carrot, and onion and stir-fry for another 1 minute Garnish with the cucumber, tomato, cilantro (coriander), scallion (spring onion), and corn kernels and serve.

recipes.searchText: Fried Brown Rice with Shrimp Central 4 tablespoons vegetable oil 6 cloves garlic, finely chopped 300 g shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and tails intact 2 eggs, beaten 350 g steamed brown rice 2 tablespoons diced fried tofu 4 teaspoons granulated sugar 2 tablespoons soy sauce 2 tablespoons peas 2 tablespoons diced carrot 2 tablespoons diced onion 1⁄2 Lebanese cucumber, peeled and sliced 1 tomato, sliced 2 teaspoons chopped cilantro (coriander) 1 scallion (spring onion), chopped 2 tablespoons corn kernels Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the shrimp (prawns) and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until they turn pink. Add the eggs and cook for 1 minute until cooked. Add the rice and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the tofu, sugar, and soy sauce and stir-fry for another 1 minute until fragrant. Add the peas, carrot, and onion and stir-fry for another 1 minute Garnish with the cucumber, tomato, cilantro (coriander), scallion (spring onion), and corn kernels and serve.

recipes.title: Rice with Black Sesame Seeds
recipes.subtitle: North

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Toast the black sesame seeds in a pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes or until fragrant. Remove from the heat and pound in a mortar with a pestle until a fine powder. Add the rice and pound together. Add the salt and sugar and continue to pound until combined. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Rice with Black Sesame Seeds North 4 tablespoons black sesame seeds 300 g cooked Glutinous Rice (see p. 378) 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 50 g superfine (caster) sugar (optional) Toast the black sesame seeds in a pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes or until fragrant. Remove from the heat and pound in a mortar with a pestle until a fine powder. Add the rice and pound together. Add the salt and sugar and continue to pound until combined. Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Shrimp Fried Rice
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined with tails intact
10 red and green bird's-eye chiles, finely chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the shrimp and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rice, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Add the chiles and stir-fry for another 30 seconds, until thoroughly combined.
Serve with the scallions and cucumber.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Shrimp Fried Rice Central 3 tablespoons vegetable oil 3 cloves garlic, finely chopped 10 shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined with tails intact 260 g Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378) 2 tablespoons soy sauce 2 teaspoons oyster sauce 1⁄2 teaspoon granulated sugar 10 red and green bird's-eye chiles, finely chopped 2 scallions (spring onions), chopped 1 small cucumber, peeled and sliced Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and sauté for 30 seconds. Add the shrimp and cook for 1 minute. Add the rice, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Add the chiles and stir-fry for another 30 seconds, until thoroughly combined. Serve with the scallions and cucumber.

recipes.title: Thai Chicken with Seasoned Fried Rice
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 x 2.5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
250 ml oil from Fried Shallots (see p. 64)
200 g evaporated milk Juice of 2 limes
6 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 64), to garnish

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dipping sauce
lines: 1 small scallion (spring onion), about 7.5 cm long
100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 tablespoons Tamarind Puree (see p. 63) Raw vegetables, such as lettuce and cucumber, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the dipping sauce, pound the cilantro root, pickled garlic, and garlic cloves together in a mortar until smooth; remove and set aside.
Pound the peppermint leaves, scallion, and chiles together in the same mortar and set aside.

Pour 250 ml water into a large wok or pan. Add the salt, sugar, and tamarind and cook over medium heat, stirring. Stir in both pounded mixtures and cook for another 5 minutes, stirring continuously. Transfer to a serving bowl and set aside.
For the rice, pound the cilantro root, garlic, and peppercorns together until smooth, then set aside. Separately pound the ginger and shallots.
Heat the fried-shallot oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the cilantro-root mixture and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the pounded ginger and shallots and sauté for another 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the chicken, evaporated milk, lime juice, tomatoes, cilantro stem, pandan leaves, sugar, and salt and stir to combine.
Transfer to a large pan and add 1 liter water. Bring to a boil, then add the rice, masala powder, and saffron and stir well.
Cover and cook over medium heat for about 30 minutes. Add the butter and stir until thoroughly combined.
Garnish with the fried shallots and serve with the dipping sauce, raw vegetables, and cilantro.

recipes.title: Crispy Curry Rice with Fermented Pork
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and very finely sliced
75 g roasted peanuts green lettuce, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring a pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork skin and cook for 20-25 minutes. Drain and trim off the extra fat underneath the skin. The skin should be 7 mm thick. Slice into thin strips about 2.5 mm thick and 5 cm long. Set aside.
Put the steamed rice and curry paste into a large bowl and mix well. Break in the egg, add the salt, and knead by hand until combined, then mold into egg-size balls.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the rice balls for 7-9 minutes until brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and set aside.
Deep-fry the dried chiles for 10 seconds, then remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and set aside.
Put the crispy rice balls into a large bowl and break them into small pieces. Add the fermented pork, shallots, ginger, and three-quarters of the scallions and mix until combined.
Season to taste with the lime juice and fish sauce. Add the peanuts and fried chiles and mix again. Garnish with the remaining scallions and serve with lettuce.

recipes.title: Rice with Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Wash the rice and drain through a strainer (sieve). Heat the coconut milk, 230 ml waler, sugar, and salt in a large nonstick pan over medium heat and stir until the sugar and salt have dissolved. Reduce the heat to low and add the rice. Cover with a lid and cook for 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice is soft. Serve.

recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g shredded young coconut meat, plus extra to garnish salt, to taste granulated sugar, to taste (optional)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the cooked rice into a large bowl and pour over the coconut water. Add the coconut meat and salt to taste and mix well. Add sugar if you prefer a sweeter taste. Serve garnished with coconut flesh.

recipes.title: Thai Pork Fried Rice with Fried Eggs
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 150 g pork loin or shoulder, cut into thin slices

ingredientGroups.heading: To serve
lines: 1 cucumber, peeled and sliced lime wedges

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, add 2 of the eggs, one at a time, and fry for 2 minutes. Remove, cover to keep warm, and set aside.

Drain all but 2 tablespoons oil from the wok and reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the pork and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until cooked. Add the remaining egg, gently beat, and cook for 40-50 seconds until the egg is lightly cooked. Add the rice and stir- fry for another 1 minute or until well mixed then season with the soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar and stir-fry for another 2 minutes until well combined. Add the kale, onions, and tomato wedges and stir fry for 1-2 minutes.
To serve, place the rice on serving plates, top with a fried egg, and arrange the cucumber and lime wedges on the side.

recipes.title: Glutinous Coconut Rice in Palm Leaves
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 teaspoon salt Palm leaves, 25-50 cm long

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium.
Mix the flours, sugars, coconut, and salt in a large bowl.

Lay out a palm leaf and place 1 tablespoon of the rice mixture lengthwise on it. Cover with another palm leaf and pin the top, middle, and bottom with small bamboo pins or toothpicks. Repeat with the remaining mixture.
Grill or broil over medium-low heat for 10 minutes on each side. Serve.

recipes.title: Glutinous Rice in a Banana Leaf
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 475 ml coconut cream banana leaves, cut into 6 x 7-inch/15 x 18 cm rectangles

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the beans and glutinous (sticky) rice in separate bowls of cold water overnight. The next day, drain the rice and beans.
Bring 1 liter water to a boil in a large pan, add the beans, and cook for 25 minutes, then drain.
Meanwhile, pound the cilantro (coriander) roots and pepper in a mortar with a pestle. Set aside.
Put the beans and the cilantro root mixture in a wok and stir-fry over medium heat for about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Combine the coconut milk, sugar, and salt in another wok and cook over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sugar and salt have dissolved. Add the drained rice and cook for another 7 minutes, stirring continuously. Stir until the rice absorbs all the liquid, then slowly add the coconut cream. Mix well and cook for another 20 minutes. Let cool.

Lay a banana leaf on a work surface. Put 1 tablespoons of the rice mixture in the center of the leaf and flatten. Place one-quarter of a banana and 1 tablespoon of beans on top. Fold the banana leaf over the filling, tucking in the side to form a package and secure with string. Steam the packages in a steamer for 45-60 minutes or until the rice has softened. Serve.

recipes.title: Baked Pineapple and Rice
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 70 g chicken breast, cut into 1.5 cm cubes

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To prepare the pineapple, cut off the stem, then cut across the top about 3 cm from the crown and set it aside as a lid. Use a long, thin knife to cut along the inside of the pineapple and loosen the flesh, then scoop it out to leave a hollow pineapple bowl. Set 80 g of the flesh aside, cut the remaining flesh into small chunks, and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F/Gas Mark 4).
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chicken, and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the shrimp and cook for another minute, or until the chicken and shrimp are cooked.
Add the rice, pineapple chunks, and red bell pepper and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the curry powder, soy sauce, sugar, and salt and stir-fry for another minute, or until thoroughly combined.
Spoon the mixture into the pineapple bowl and bake for 10 minutes. Remove from the oven and top with the pork floss and cashew nuts. Cover with the pineapple lid and serve.

recipes.title: Fried Rice with Pineapple
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 120 g shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact
250 g pineapple, cut into 2 cm dice
2 scallions (spring onions), thinly sliced, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the garlic, and stir-fry for about 1 minute, or until fragrant. Add the shrimp and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until pink. Remove the shrimp from the wok and set aside.
Add the steamed rice to the wok and stir for about 1 minute, or until the rice is well coated with the oil. Add the soy sauce, sugar, and shrimp and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Add the pineapple and cashew nuts and cook for another minute, stirring gently. Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with the scallions. Serve with the lime wedges.

recipes.title: Glass Noodle and Fried Pork Spicy Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails still intact
2 scallions (spring onions), cut into 2.5 cm slices

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes. Drain and cook in boiling water for 1 minute, or according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
Boil the shrimp for 2-3 minutes, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain. Return the water to a boil and cook the ground pork for 2-3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Mix the chili jam, lime juice, fish sauce, and sugar in a bowl to make the dressing.
Put the noodles, shrimp, chicken, pork, dried shrimp, and fried garlic in a serving bowl. Add the dressing and mix well.
Add the scallions, Chinese celery, and crispy pork skin, mix again, and serve.

recipes.title: Phuket-Style Stir-Fried Hokkien Noodles
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 50 g fresh squid, cleaned, with tentacles set aside
50 g sea bass, cut into pieces
200 g napa (Chinese) cabbage, cut into 5 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, add the shallots, and stir-fry for 2 minutes, or until soft and beginning to brown.
Add the pork and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the squid tubes and tentacles, shrimp, fish, and oysters and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, until cooked.
Add the noodles and stir-fry for 1 minute, or until softened. Season with both soy sauces and stir until thoroughly combined.
Add the napa cabbage and broth and stir-fry for 1 minute more.
Remove the wok from the heat and serve with the poached eggs on top.

recipes.title: Crispy Rice Noodles with Herbs
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, then drain and set aside.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Fry the rice noodles in batches for 1 minute, then remove and drain on paper towels Deep-fry the kaffir lime leaves, dried chiles, and sliced lemongrass in the same oil for 30 seconds until crispy. Remove from the wok and drain on paper towels.

Bring the tamarind, chili flakes, salt, sugar, and glucose syrup to a boil in a clean wok. Stir continuously. Keep boiling for 5 minutes. Slowly pour the tamarind sauce over the fried rice noodles and stir until thoroughly combined. Serve.
Alternatively, let cool, transfer to in an airtight container, and store in the refrigerator for up to 15 days.

recipes.subtitle: Central

lines: 50 g chopped Chinese celery, cut into 4 cm length pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or prepare according to package directions. Drain, cut, and set aside.
Cook the pork in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes until cooked, then drain and set aside.

Cook the squid in another pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes until cooked, then drain and set aside. Cook the shrimp (prawns) in another pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes until the shrimp change color, then drain and set aside. recipes.title: Phat Thai Wrapped in Eggs

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 11⁄2 tablespoons finely chopped sweet fermented radish
50 g fresh extra-firm tofu, cut into 1 cm cubes
80 g uncooked jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled and deveined, tails still intact
100 g bean sprouts, plus extra to serve
20 g chopped Chinese chives, cut into 4 cm lengths
30 g unsalted peanuts, roasted and crushed
1 handful cilantro (coriander) sprigs, to garnish lime wedges, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the dried noodles in water for 10 minutes, or according to the package directions, until soft. Drain and set aside.
Mix the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, and tamarind in a small bowl. Set aside.

Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add 3 tablespoons oil, the shallots, garlic, and fermented radish and sauté for 1 minute. Add the dried shrimp and fry for 1 minute. Add the tofu and cook for 1 minute. Add the shrimp and sauté for 1-2 minutes, until pink and cooked. Push everything to one side of the pan.

Add the noodles and broth to the pan and stir-fry for 1 minute without mixing them with the other ingredients. Add the sauce and continue to stir-fry the noodles for 2 minutes, or until cooked and the sauce starts to dry. Mix everything together, then add the bean sprouts, chives, and peanuts. Stir well, remove from the heat, divide into three portions, and set aside.
Heat 11⁄2 teaspoons oil in a wok over medium heat and roll the oil around the wok. When hot, add 75 ml beaten egg and roll it in a circular motion to make a thin, 25 cm omelet.
When cooked, place the omelet in a 16 cm bowl. Put one portion of noodles in the omelet and fold it over the noodles. Invert the bowl onto a serving plate. Repeat with the remaining egg and noodles.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with lime wedges and raw bean sprouts.

Put one portion of noodles in the omelet and fold it over the noodles. Invert the bowl onto a serving plate. Repeat with the remaining egg and noodles. Garnish with cilantro and serve with lime wedges and raw bean sprouts.

recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 7 red and green bird's-eye chiles, pounded
150 g Chinese broccoli, cut into 4 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Separate the noodle strips. If refrigerated, wrap them in cheesecloth and steam for 2-3 minutes, microwave for 1 minute, or prepare according to package directions. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and chiles and stir-fry for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the broccoli and baby corn and stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes.
Add the noodles, mushrooms, soy sauce, and sugar and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until the noodles are soft and fully flavored.
Add the basil leaves, stir a few times, and serve.

recipes.title: Fried Noodles in Coconut Milk with Shrimp
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 15 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
10 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined black pepper
To serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber. bean sprouts, and yard-long beans

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes or according to package directions, until soft. Drain and set aside.
Pound the shallots and chiles together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth, then add the shrimp paste and pound until combined.

Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste, stir, and boil for about 2 minutes. Add the sugar, tamarind salt, and a pinch of black pepper, and stir until combined and beginning to boil. Add the shrimp (prawns) and cook for 1-2 minutes until the shrimp turn pink and are cooked. Add the noodles and stir for 3-4 minutes until thoroughly combined and the noodles are soft, and the sauce has dried out. Add a little water if the sauce has dried out but the noodles are still not soft enough to serve. Serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Fried Noodles with Chicken and Gravy
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g chicken breast, cut into 1⁄2 cm strips
80 ml vegetable oil, plus extra for drizzling
250 g bamboo shoots in brine, drained and cut into 1 cm batons
150 g canned champignon or white button mushrooms

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish
lines: 2 scallions (spring onions), cut into 1 cm batons
To serve a selection of condiments, such as granulated sugar, dried chili flakes, fish sauce, and white vinegar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the soy sauce and 1 tablespoon tapioca flour in a shallow bowl, add the chicken, and mix to coat. Cover and leave for at least 10 minutes.

Bring a half-full pan of water to a boil. Cook the noodles in batches for 2-3 minutes at a time, or according to the package directions. Remove with a slotted spoon, arrange on a serving plate, drizzle with oil to prevent sticking, and set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute, or until golden and fragrant. Add the chicken, increase the heat slightly, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, or until it starts to cook.

To make the gravy, pour in the broth and bring to a boil. Add the salted soybeans, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and black pepper. Reduce the heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked.

Put the remaining tapioca flour in a bowl, add 75 ml water, and stir until smooth. Increase the heat under the wok to medium and add the tapioca mixture in small amounts to thicken the gravy; it should be thick but not gloopy.
Add the bamboo shoots and mushrooms, return to a boil, and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Spoon the chicken and gravy over the noodles and garnish with the scallions and chiles. Serve with the condiments.

recipes.title: Korat-Style Fried Noodles
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 Chinese chives, cut into 4 cm pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the shallots and garlic and stir-fry for about 1 minute, until golden.
Add the broth, fish sauce, sugar, tamarind puree, chile powder, and salted soybeans and bring to a boil.

Quickly rinse the noodles under cold running water, add them to the wok, and stir-fry for 5-7 minutes, or according to package directions, until soft and almost dry. Add a little water if the broth evaporates before the noodles cook.
Reduce the heat and add the scallions, bean sprouts, and chives. Mix well and stir-fry for another 30 seconds. Serve.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g pork shoulder or tenderloin, thinly sliced
200 g Chinese broccoli, cut into 4 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Separate the noodle strips. If refrigerated, wrap them in cheesecloth and steam for 3-5 minutes to warm through, or microwave for 1 minute. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and quickly stir-fry for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Add the rice noodles and stir-fry for another 1 minute, until softened. Season with the soy sauce and sugar, then add the broccoli and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Move the noodle mixture to one side of the wok. Break in the egg, beat it, and let it begin to set before moving the noodles back into the center.
Stir-fry for another minute, until thoroughly combined, and serve.

recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and coarsely chopped

ingredientGroups.heading: For the sauce
lines: 1 tablespoon calamansi (Chinese orange) or white passion fruit juice
11⁄2 tablespoons julienned calamansi or passion fruit zest
100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar pinch of salt

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish
lines: 1 red spur chile, seeded and sliced
To serve raw or steamed vegetables, such as yard-long beans, bean sprouts, and cucumbers

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the vermicelli in a bowl of water for 5 minutes, or according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.

Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Spread 30 g portions of vermicelli around the wok and deep-fry for 1 minute at a time, or until golden and crisp on both sides. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and repeat with the remaining vermicelli.
In the same wok, pour the beaten egg through a fine strainer and drizzle it around the wok from about 20 cm above to create an egg mesh. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Deep-fry the tofu for 2 minutes, or until golden brown, then remove and drain. Deep-fry the shrimp for 1-2 minutes, then remove and drain.
Pound all the paste ingredients in a mortar with a pestle.

For the sauce, heat the oil in a clean wok over medium heat. Add the paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, or until fragrant. Add the tamarind, calamansi or passion fruit juice and zest, lime juice, both sugars, salt, vinegar, ketchup, and fish sauce and stir for 4-5 minutes, or until thickened.
Add the fried shrimp and tofu and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Add the crispy noodles and stir until completely coated in the sauce.
Transfer to a serving plate and garnish with the egg mesh, scallions, bean sprouts, chile, cilantro, and fried shallots. Serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g snakehead fish, sea bass, or sea bream, filleted and cut into bite-size pieces
1 kg cooked rice noodles, to serve
270 g chopped yard-long beans, to serve
2 handfuls water mimosa, coarsely chopped, to serve
20 g dried chile flakes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 250 ml water and the broth to a boil in a large pan.
Add the chiles, garlic, shallots, galangal, lemongrass, fingerroots, and fermented fish sauce and boil for about 7 minutes.

Return the broth to the pan and bring to a boil over medium heat. Add the pounded paste, fish sauce, sugar, and fish balls and boil for 2-3 minutes.
Add the scallions and cook for about 2 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Divide the noodles and fish balls among serving bowls and pour over the broth. Top with the bean sprouts, basil, yard-long beans, water mimosa, chile flakes, and eggs.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, until soft, then drain, rinse, and set aside. To make the beef broth (stock), bring 2 liters water to a boil in a large pan. Add all the ingredients and return to a boil. Use a slotted spoon to remove any scum. Cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 1-2 hours until the beef is tender. Remove the beef from the pan and set aside Blanch the rice noodles and bean sprouts in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and divide among serving bowls. Add the lettuce, Chinese celery, scallions (spring onions), cilantro (coriander), and 50 g stewed beef. Add 1 ladleful of beef broth to each bowl and serve.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 250 g pork tenderloin or shoulder, thinly sliced
200 g Chinese broccoli, cut into 2-inch 5 cm-long pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the rice noodles and dark soy sauce and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until the noodles have softened. Remove from the wok and set aside.

Dissolve the tapioca flour in 50 ml water and slowly add to the wok, stirring continuously, until the mixture has thickened into a gravy. Add the broccoli and cook for about 2 minutes or until the broccoli is tender.
Transfer the noodles to a deep serving plate or bowl and pour the gravy, pork, and vegetables over the noodles. Serve.

steps: Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chicken and salt, reduce the heat to low-medium, and simmer for 10 minutes. Serve with the cilantro (coriander), cucumber slices, and lettuce leaves.

recipes.title: Fried Rice Noodles with Chicken
recipes.subtitle: Central

lines: 200 g skinless, boneless chicken breast, sliced
1 tablespoon finely chopped sweet preserved turnip

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the chicken, ground white pepper, sesame oil, and 1 teaspoon soy sauce in a bowl, mix well, and let stand for 10~15 minutes.

Separate the strips of noodles from each other. If the noodles have been kept in the refrigerator, wrap them in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 2-3 minutes until warmed through. Alternatively, heat in a microwave for 1 minute. Set aside.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over low- medium heat, add the garlic and preserved turnip, and stir-fry for 10 seconds or until fragrant. Add the chicken, increase the heat to medium, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until cooked. Add the noodles and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, then season with 2 teaspoons soy sauce, the oyster sauce, and sugar. Stir until combined, then move to one side of the wok.

Add 1 tablespoon oil, break in the eggs, and let the egg whites become lightly cooked before scrambling. When the eggs are cooked halfway, mix with the noodles and stir-fry for about 1 minute or until the eggs are fully cooked. Add the bean sprouts and stir-fry for 20 seconds. Remove from the heat Let cool for 1 minute, then add the lettuce and scallions (spring onions) and stir. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Fried Rice Noodles with Chicken Central 200 g skinless, boneless chicken breast, sliced 1 teaspoon ground white pepper 1⁄2 teaspoon sesame oil 11⁄2 tablespoons soy sauce 400 g large fresh rice noodles 3 tablespoons vegetable oil 3 cloves garlic, crushed 1 tablespoon finely chopped sweet preserved turnip 1 tablespoon oyster sauce 1 tablespoon granulated sugar 2 eggs 100 g bean sprouts 4-6 leaves round or curly lettuce 2 scallions (spring onions), finely chopped Put the chicken, ground white pepper, sesame oil, and 1 teaspoon soy sauce in a bowl, mix well, and let stand for 10~15 minutes. Separate the strips of noodles from each other. If the noodles have been kept in the refrigerator, wrap them in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 2-3 minutes until warmed through. Alternatively, heat in a microwave for 1 minute. Set aside. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over low- medium heat, add the garlic and preserved turnip, and stir-fry for 10 seconds or until fragrant. Add the chicken, increase the heat to medium, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until cooked. Add the noodles and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, then season with 2 teaspoons soy sauce, the oyster sauce, and sugar. Stir until combined, then move to one side of the wok. Add 1 tablespoon oil, break in the eggs, and let the egg whites become lightly cooked before scrambling. When the eggs are cooked halfway, mix with the noodles and stir-fry for about 1 minute or until the eggs are fully cooked. Add the bean sprouts and stir-fry for 20 seconds. Remove from the heat Let cool for 1 minute, then add the lettuce and scallions (spring onions) and stir. Serve.

recipes.title: Rice Vermicelli with Pineapple and Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg fresh rice vermicelli or 400 g dried rice vermicelli

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili sauce
lines: 10 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
25 g chopped fresh ginger, to serve
10 cloves garlic, thinly sliced, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Cook the vermicelli according to the package directions. If using dried vermicelli, first soak it in water for 10 minutes, until soft. Drain, rinse under cold water, and leave in a strainer to drain completely.
Process the dried shrimp in a food processor into fine flakes and set aside.
For the chili sauce, combine the chiles, fish sauce, and lime slices in a small serving bowl and set aside.
Simmer the coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a pan over low-medium heat for 2-3 minutes, until the sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from the heat.
Divide the vermicelli among serving bowls and pour over the coconut milk mixture.
Top with the ginger, garlic, dried-shrimp flakes, diced pineapple, and chili sauce.

recipes.title: Corn in Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the sugar and salt and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the corn, stir gently, and return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Serve hot or cold.

recipes.searchText: Corn in Coconut Milk Central 400 ml coconut milk 100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 400 g sweetcorn kernels Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the sugar and salt and stir until the sugar dissolves. Add the corn, stir gently, and return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Corn with Young Coconut
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 80 g shredded fresh coconut, or 40 g dry unsweetened desiccated coconut

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: If using dried coconut, wrap it in cheesecloth and steam for 10 minutes, until hydrated and softened. Let cool.
Boil the corn for 10-12 minutes, then drain and slice the kernels from the cobs.
Mix the corn and coconut, reserving some coconut for decoration. Add the sugar and salt and stir together. Decorate with the reserved coconut and serve.

recipes.searchText: Corn with Young Coconut Northeast 80 g shredded fresh coconut, or 40 g dry unsweetened desiccated coconut 2 corn cobs, husks removed 11⁄2 tablespoons granulated sugar 1⁄4 teaspoon salt If using dried coconut, wrap it in cheesecloth and steam for 10 minutes, until hydrated and softened. Let cool. Boil the corn for 10-12 minutes, then drain and slice the kernels from the cobs. Mix the corn and coconut, reserving some coconut for decoration. Add the sugar and salt and stir together. Decorate with the reserved coconut and serve.

recipes.title: Corn and Pandan Pudding
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg banana leaves, cut into 15 cm circles

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare 15-20 banana-leaf cups. For each cup, place 2 banana-leaf circles back to back with the shiny sides facing outward. Fold up about 3 cm of leaf at the edge and fold it inward on itself to form a corner. Secure with a toothpick or staple and repeat to make four corners.
For the filling, combine the mung bean flour, sugar, corn, pandan extract, and 250 ml water in a pan.
Cook over low-medium heat, stirring continuously for 7-8 minutes, until thick and transparent.
Fill each banana-leaf cup with about 1 tablespoon filling, leaving about 5 mm headspace. Set aside.
For the topping, combine the coconut milk, rice flour, salt, and sugar in a pan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly for 6-7 minutes, until thickened.
Top each filled cup with about 1⁄2 tablespoon topping, let cool, and serve.

recipes.title: Steamed Rice Flour Topped with Coconut Flesh
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g rice flour meat of 2 coconuts, cut into thin strips
50 g salt jasmine flowers, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 475 ml water and the sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Stir until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is syrupy, then remove from the heat and let cool. Sprinkle 120 ml water onto the rice flour to dampen it, then sift this wet rice flour through a strainer (sieve) into a bowl. Wrap the powdered rice flour in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 10 minutes, then transfer to a large bowl and let cool.

Gradually add the cold sugar syrup to the cold steamed rice flour and mix well with a spatula. Mix the coconut flesh and salt together in a bowl, then stir into the rice flour mixture until combined. Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with jasmine Flowers. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Steamed Rice Flour Topped with Coconut Flesh Central 500 g superfine (caster) sugar 500 g rice flour meat of 2 coconuts, cut into thin strips 50 g salt jasmine flowers, to garnish Bring 475 ml water and the sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Stir until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is syrupy, then remove from the heat and let cool. recipes.title: Golden Egg Teardrops
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10-12 jasmine flowers or 11⁄4 teaspoons jasmine essence

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the jasmine water, bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Let cool and transfer to a large bowl. Add the jasmine flowers, cover, and let steep overnight. The next day, remove and discard the flowers.
For the syrup, mix the sugar with the jasmine water, or jasmine essence, and pandan leaf in a pan over medium-low heat, then bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, strain the egg yolks through cheesecloth into a bowl. Whisk until thick, smooth, and pale yellow, taking care not to overwhisk. Add the flour and gently fold until well mixed.
When the syrup starts boiling, remove and discard the pandan leaf.

Use the narrow grooved handle of a noodle spoon or a teaspoon to scrape 1⁄2 teaspoon egg mixture onto another spoon, then use your thumb to push the mixture into the boiling syrup. Repeat, keeping the syrup boiling, until all the mixture is used or there is no room on the surface. The egg mixture should form teardrops.
Cook the teardrops in the syrup for 4-5 minutes, then remove them with a slotted spoon and transfer to a bowl.
Pour about 120 ml syrup over the egg teardrops. Let cool, then remove the teardrops from the syrup with a slotted spoon and serve.

recipes.title: Coconut Custard with Fried Shallots
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1.5 kg jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
13 duck eggs or 15 hen eggs, beaten

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F/180°C/Gas Mark 4. Grease a 30 cm square baking pan. Mix the coconut milk, flour, sugar, and eggs together in a bowl until thoroughly combined. Pour the mixture into a pan and cook over medium heat for 7 minutes, stirring frequently. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and bake for 15 minutes or until golden brown. Sprinkle with the fried shallots, cut into squares, and serve.

recipes.title: Job's Tears and Young Coconut Porridge
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 215 g Job's tear seeds (Chinese pearl barley)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Rinse and soak the Job's tear seeds in a bowl of water overnight. The next day, drain and rinse. Transfer to a large pan, add 950 ml water, cover with a lid, and cook over low heat for about 1 hour or until cooked. Drain and rinse the Job's tears again and return to the pan. Add the coconut water and bring to a boil over medium heat. Add the sliced coconut, sugar, and half the salt, and stir until the sugar and salt have dissolved Dissolve the cornstarch (cornflour) and the arrowroot starch in 60 ml water. Stir half of the mixture into the pan and cook until thick. Remove from the heat.

Bring the coconut cream to a boil in another pan over medium heat. Add the remaining salt and stir for about 2 minutes or until the salt has dissolved. Add the rest of the cornstarch mixture and stir until thickened. Remove from the heat.
Put the Job's tears into small serving bowls and pour over the coconut cream. Serve.

recipes.title: Sweet Glutinous Rice with Dried Shrimp
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg banana leaves, cut into 15 cm circles

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the turmeric in a large mortar. Add 2 liters water, mix, then strain through cheesecloth into a large bowl and discard the residue.
Add the rice to the turmeric water, cover, and soak overnight or for at least 3 hours.
Wrap the soaked rice in cheesecloth and steam for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until cooked and translucent.
Prepare banana-leaf cups by placing two leaf circles back to back, shiny sides outward. Fold and secure four corners with toothpicks or staples.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil over low-medium heat. Add the salt and sugar and stir until dissolved.
Add the rice and cook for 3-4 minutes, until thoroughly combined. Remove from the heat, cover, and rest for 10 minutes.
For the topping, dry-fry the coconut in a wok over medium heat for 1-2 minutes, stirring continuously, until it begins to color.
Add the dried shrimp, sugar, and fried shallots and stir until combined.
Spoon the rice into the banana-leaf cups, sprinkle with the topping, and serve.

recipes.title: Caramel
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice in a large bowl of water overnight or for at least 3 hours. Wash and drain. Wrap the rice in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 30-35 minutes, stirring the rice every 10 minutes until cooked through. The rice will look transparent when cooked. Mix the rice flour with the steamed rice in another pan, then add the coconut milk and sugar and cook over low heat for 2-3 hours or until sticky. Let cool in a casserole dish, then cut into 4 cm squares and serve.

recipes.title: Sweet Coconut Balls
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1⁄2 teaspoon salt, plus extra for rolling
300 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
880 g shredded fresh coconut, plus 40 g for rolling

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the flour, coconut milk, and salt in a bowl, then knead by hand until the dough is sticky. Cover with plastic wrap and set aside.
Bring the sugar to a simmer in a wok over low heat for 2-3 minutes, until softened. Add 80 g shredded coconut and stir-fry until dry. Remove from the heat.

Spread the remaining coconut and a little salt on a plate. Roll out the dough and cut small circles with a cookie cutter. Put a teaspoon of filling in the center of each circle and mold the dough around it to form a ball.
Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Carefully add the balls and cook for 4-5 minutes, until they float. Drain, roll in the salted shredded coconut, and serve.

recipes.title: Black Beans in Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 15 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain, rinse, and put into a pan. Pour in enough water to cover and bring to a boil over medium heat. Boil for 50-60 minutes or until softened. Drain and transfer to a clean pan. Add the coconut milk and 75 ml water and bring to a boil over medium heat. When the mixture is boiling, add both sugars and the salt and stir until the sugars have dissolved. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes or until the beans are fully flavored. Remove from the heat and serve.

recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the cooked rice, three-quarters of the coconut, the sugar, and salt together in a large bowl.
Scoop out a teaspoon of the mixture, roll it into a ball, and place on a plate. Repeat with the remaining mixture.
Sprinkle with the remaining coconut and serve.

recipes.title: Sweet Glutinous Rice with Black Beans
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 75 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the rice, soak the rice in water overnight, or for at least 3 hours. Drain and rinse, then wrap in cheesecloth and steam for 20 minutes.
Pour the coconut milk into a pan, add the salt and granulated sugar, and gradually bring to a boil. Remove from the heat and reserve three-quarters of the sweet coconut milk for topping.
Put the rice and remaining sweet coconut milk into another pan, mix well, cover, and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes. Pour the reserved sweet coconut milk over the rice.
For the beans, rinse them under cold running water, put them in a pan, and cover with 950 ml water. Bring to a boil and cook for about 20 minutes, until soft.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in another pan over low heat. Add the salt and both sugars and stir, then add the black beans and stir until mixed.
Pour the beans over the rice and serve.

recipes.title: Glutinous Rice Roasted in Bamboo
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 teaspoon salt bamboo stalks, about 2 inches/S om in diameter, and cut into 30 cm long pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice in a bowl of water for about 2 hours, then drain and set aside Soak the beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain, rinse, and put into a pan. Pour in enough water to cover and bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce the heat and simmer for about 30 minutes. Remove from the heat and mix with the rice. Spoon the mixture into the bamboo stalks until three-quarters full.

Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot. Bring the coconut milk, sugar, and salt to a boil over medium heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat and carefully pour into the bamboo stalks. Cover with the banana leaf and cook over the charcoal fire for 21⁄2-3 hours. Remove from the heat, carefully split the bamboo stalks open, and serve.

recipes.title: Glutinous Rice in Coconut Shell
recipes.subtitle: South
recipes.prepTime: 10 minutes plus soaking time and resting time

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 50 g cooled black beans or red beans
50 g arrowroot starch or tapioca flour

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice in a large bowl of cold water overnight or for at least 3 hours. Wash and drain. Wrap the rice in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 30-35 minutes. stirring the rice every 10 minutes until cooked through. The rice will look transparent when cooked. Set aside.
Heat the coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a pan over medium heat and simmer, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved.

Put the steamed rice into a bowl and add the black or red beans. Sprinkle with half the sweetened coconut milk and stir until thoroughly combined. Let rest for 10 minutes. Open the young coconuts, remove the flesh with a spoon, keeping the shells intact. Set the shells aside. Shred the coconut flesh, add to the rice and bean mixture, and stir until well mixed. Set aside. Preheat the oven to 425°F/220°C/Gas Mark 7.

Mix the starch or flour with the remaining sweetened coconut milk in a pan and simmer over low heat for a few minutes or until thickened. Add the mixture to the rice and coconut mixture, then pour into the coconut shells and bake for 10-15 minutes. Serve.

recipes.title: Glutinous Rice in Tiger Grass Leaf
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 teaspoon salt tiger grass leaves, for wrapping

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice in a bowl of water overnight or for at least 3 hours, then drain, rinse under cold running water, and drain again. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

Soak the beans in another bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain, rinse, and put into a pan. Pour in enough water to cover and bring to a boil over medium heat. Boil for 50-60 minutes or until softened.

recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 small ripe bananas Banana leaves, cut into 18-20 cm-wide strips

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice in water overnight or for at least 3 hours. Drain, rinse under cold running water, and drain again.
Soak the beans in a separate bowl of water for 2 hours. Drain, rinse, and place in a pan with enough water to cover.
Bring the beans to a boil over medium heat and boil for 50-60 minutes, until softened.

Combine the rice and sweetened coconut milk in a wok over medium heat. Stir continuously for about 10 minutes, until the rice begins to cook. Remove from the heat.

Lay a banana leaf on a flat work surface. Put 1 tablespoon rice and 10 black beans in the center. Cover with 2 banana halves and top with another spoonful of rice.
Fold the leaf around the filling and secure with string to form a package. Repeat until all the filling is used.
Steam the packages for 40-45 minutes, then serve.

recipes.title: Crispy Stuffed Buns
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

ingredientGroups.heading: For the filling
lines: 150 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the filling, soak the mung beans in water for 2 hours.
For the dough, mix the flours together. Gradually add 120-175 ml water and knead until a dough forms. Add the coconut and sugar and knead until sticky enough to shape.

Drain the mung beans, wrap them in cheesecloth, and steam for 25 minutes, or until cooked. Melt the sugar in a wok over low heat for 2-3 minutes. Add the coconut and mung beans and cook until dry enough to shape into 2.5 cm balls.
Roll the dough to 2 mm thick and cut into 6 cm circles. Put a ball of filling in the center of each circle and enclose it with the dough.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 350°F/180°C. Fry the buns in batches for 7-8 minutes, or until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towels and serve.

recipes.title: Sugar-Coated Stuffed Dough Balls
recipes.subtitle: Central
recipes.prepTime: 10–15 minutes, plus soaking and resting time

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 tablespoons coconut milk vegetable oil, for deep-frying

ingredientGroups.heading: For the filling
lines: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the filling, soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 30 minutes. Drain, rinse, and drain again. Wrap the mung beans in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam over medium heat for 20 minutes, or until cooked. Remove from the cheesecloth and let cool. Process the mung beans in a food processor and set aside.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the shallot and stir-fry for 1 minute, or until softened. Add the mung beans, sugar, salt, and white pepper, reduce the heat to medium-low, then stir until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is thoroughly combined. Remove from the heat and set aside.

To make the dough, mix the rice flour, glutinous rice flour, and salt together in a large bowl. Add the sugar and crumble it into the flour mixture. Gradually pour in the coconut milk and 120 ml water, a little at a time, crumbling and mixing the flour mixture into the liquid with your other hand. Keep kneading until a smooth dough forms, adding a little more water if it is too dry. Cover with plastic wrap and rest for 20 minutes.
When the filling is cool, roll portions just under a tablespoon each into balls. Divide the dough into small portions and roll these into balls as well.

Working with one dough ball at a time, flatten it with your thumb from the center outward to form a circle about 3 mm thick and 6 cm in diameter. Put a ball of filling in the middle, wrap the dough around it, and squeeze and tap the seam closed. Gently roll into a ball and repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the dough balls in batches for about 8 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Bring the superfine sugar and 120 ml water to a boil in a clean wok over medium heat. Boil for about 21⁄2 minutes, or until thickened. Remove from the heat, immediately add the fried dough balls, and stir until coated in the sugar syrup. Remove with a slotted spoon, let cool slightly, and serve.

recipes.title: Mung Bean Porridge with Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1⁄2 teaspoon rice flour a pinch of salt

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain and rinse. Put the beans in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 25 minutes or until cooked. Set aside.
Mix the coconut cream, rice flour, and salt together in a pan and cook over low heat for 3-4 minutes or until thickened. Set aside.

Bring 750 ml water to a boil in another pan. Add the sugar and stir until dissolved. Mix the tapioca flour, arrowroot flour, and 0 ml water together in a bowl. Continue to stir the sugar mixture in the pan and gradually pour in the flour mixture. Stir and cook for 1-2 minutes or until thickened. Add the mung beans, then stir and cook for another 3-4 minutes or until the mung beans are fully flavored. Transfer to serving bowls, pour over the coconut cream mixture, and serve.

recipes.title: Sweet Mung Bean Packages
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 45 g shredded fresh or dry unsweetened (desiccated) coconut

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain and rinse. Wrap the beans and coconut in separate pieces of cheesecloth and steam for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix the sugar, salt, and sesame seeds together in a small bowl and set aside.
Mix the flour and 250 ml water in a bowl until a dough forms. Knead until soft and smooth. Pinch off pieces and shape into small balls.

Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Add the dough balls one by one and boil for 5 minutes, or until cooked and floating. Remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to a large bowl. Add a small amount of water to prevent them sticking together.

Spread the steamed mung beans and coconut on separate plates. Flatten each dough ball into a 1 cm-thick patty. Place 1-2 teaspoons mung beans in the center and wrap the edges over the filling to form an oval package.

Squeeze the edges to seal, roll in the steamed mung beans, and place on a serving plate. Repeat with the remaining patties. Cover with the steamed coconut, sprinkle with the sugar and sesame mixture, and serve.

recipes.title: Colorful Mung Bean Noodles in Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 195 g mung bean starch (mung bean flour)
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
475 ml coconut milk Thai scented dessert candle, for smoking ice cubes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Divide the mung bean starch (flour) into 3 equal portions to make sa-lim noodles in different colors. For the green noodles, mix 65 g starch, the pandan juice, and 250 ml water together until thoroughly combined. For red noodles, mix 65 g starch, the red food coloring, and 600 ml water together until thoroughly combined. For white noodles, mix 85 g starch and 600 ml water together until thoroughly combined Fill a large pan with cold water and set aside. Heat the first portion of starch in a separate pan over low heat for 7-9 minutes, stirring until translucent and shiny. When cooked pour the mixture into a sa-lim mold or a potato ricer and slowly press the mixture through the mold, letting it drop into the pan of cold water The mixture should resemble noodles. Let soak in the cold water for at least 10 minutes then drain and wrap in cheesecloth (muslin). Transfer to a plate and set aside. Repeat with the second and third starch portions. Heat the sugars, salt, and coconut milk in another pan over low heat, stirring, for about 5 minutes or until the sugars have dissolved.

Place the candle in a small bowl on a plate. Light both ends of the candle and let stand for 2 minutes, Blow out the candle and wait until the black smoke disappears and you can smell the aroma, then quickly put the candle still in the bowl on a plate into the pan of coconut milk syrup, cover with a lid, and let smoke for 10-15 minutes. This process can be repeated as many as 5-6 times for a more intense aroma. The candle can be used again if there is still some left after the dessert has been scented.
To serve, divide the different color mung bean noodles among serving bowls, pour the aromatic coconut milk over them, and add ice cubes.

recipes.subtitle: Central / South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 shallots, halved lengthwise and finely sliced
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain and rinse. Put the beans in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 25 minutes or until cooked. Pound the beans in a mortar with a pestle until fine, then transfer to a bowl and set aside.

For the crispy shallots, heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the shallots, and fry for 10-12 minutes or until golden brown. Set aside and reserve 2 tablespoons of the fried oil Preheat the oven to 400°F/200°C/Gas Mark 6. Grease a 30 cm round baking pan with butter or oil. Beat the eggs in a large bowl, then add the sugar, salt, and rice flour and mix well until the sugar has dissolved. Add the coconut milk, all but 1 tablespoon of the crispy shallots, and the reserved fried oil and mix well. Pour into the bowl containing the mung beans and mix well. Heat the mixture in a pan over low heat for about 5 minutes stirring continuously until smooth. Pour the mixture into the greased pan. Bake for 30 minutes or until the mixture has risen and turned golden brown on top. Let cool slightly, then remove from the pan and sprinkle with the reserved crispy shallots. Serve.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 120 g tapioca flour, plus extra for coating

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Sift the tapioca flour and rice flour into a bowl. Add about 120 ml tepid water and stir until a dough forms.
Let cool, knead, then pinch off small pieces and roll into balls. Press each ball on a krong krang or gnocchi press, or with a fork. Coat lightly in tapioca flour to prevent sticking.

Remove with a slotted spoon and place in a large bowl of cold water for 4-5 minutes. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

Add the tapioca balls and cook for 4-5 minutes.
Transfer to serving bowls, sprinkle with the sesame seeds, and serve.

steps: Soak the rice in a large bowl of cold water overnight or for at least 3 hours. Wash and drain. Wrap the rice in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 30 minutes, stirring the rice every 10 minutes, until cooked through, Dry the steamed rice and let cool.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the green rice balls, smash the pandan leaves in a mortar with a pestle, then pound to a paste. Add 250 ml water and instantly squeeze with your hands to get 3 tablespoons thick pand an juice. Mix the glutinous (sticky) rice flour and pandan juice together in a bowl to form a sticky dough, then knead. Gradually add 120 ml water to the dough until no longer sticky. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into balls Set aside.

For the yellow rice balls, steam the pumpkin in a steamer for 3 minutes or until soft, let cool, then pound in a mortar with a pestle. Mix the rice flour and pounded pumpkin together in a bowl, then knead. Gradually add 120 ml water to the dough until no longer sticky. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into balls. Set aside.

For the purple rice balls, steam the taro in a steamer for 3-4 minutes or until soft, let cool, then pound in a mortar with a pestle. Mix the rice flour and the pounded taro in a bowl, then knead. Gradually add 120 ml water to the dough until no longer sticky. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into balls. Set aside. Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat, add the rice balls, and cook for 4-5 minutes or until they float to the surface. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.

For the coconut milk, bring the coconut milk, sugars, salt, pandan leaves, and coconut meat to a boil in a pan. Reduce the heat and cook stirring continuously, for 3-4 minutes. Add the rice flour balls and return to a boil. Remove from the heat and stir in the coconut cream. Serve hot or cold.

recipes.searchText: Glutinous Rice Balls in Coconut Milk Central 10 pandan leaves, finely sliced 140 g glutinous (sticky) rice flour 120 g diced Thai pumpkin 140 g glutinous (sticky) rice ou 50 g diced taro 140 g glutinous (sticky) rice hour 750 ml coconut milk 150 g granulated sugar 50 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 1 teaspoon salt 2 Knotted pandan leaves meat from 2 coconuts 250 ml coconut cream To make the green rice balls, smash the pandan leaves in a mortar with a pestle, then pound to a paste. Add 250 ml water and instantly squeeze with your hands to get 3 tablespoons thick pand an juice. Mix the glutinous (sticky) rice flour and pandan juice together in a bowl to form a sticky dough, then knead. Gradually add 120 ml water to the dough until no longer sticky. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into balls Set aside. For the yellow rice balls, steam the pumpkin in a steamer for 3 minutes or until soft, let cool, then pound in a mortar with a pestle. Mix the rice flour and pounded pumpkin together in a bowl, then knead. Gradually add 120 ml water to the dough until no longer sticky. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into balls. Set aside. For the purple rice balls, steam the taro in a steamer for 3-4 minutes or until soft, let cool, then pound in a mortar with a pestle. Mix the rice flour and the pounded taro in a bowl, then knead. Gradually add 120 ml water to the dough until no longer sticky. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into balls. Set aside. Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat, add the rice balls, and cook for 4-5 minutes or until they float to the surface. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside. For the coconut milk, bring the coconut milk, sugars, salt, pandan leaves, and coconut meat to a boil in a pan. Reduce the heat and cook stirring continuously, for 3-4 minutes. Add the rice flour balls and return to a boil. Remove from the heat and stir in the coconut cream. Serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Ginkgo Nuts and Dates in Longan Syrup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 packed 225 g soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put 3 liters water, the dried longans, dried jujube, and ginkgo in a large pan and bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for about 15 minutes, adding more water if necessary. Add the sugar to taste, then transfer to a heatproof serving bowl and serve.

recipes.searchText: Ginkgo Nuts and Dates in Longan Syrup Central 200 g dried longans, rinsed 150 g dried jujube (Chinese dates), rinsed 175 g shelled ginkgo nuts 1 packed 225 g soft light brown sugar Put 3 liters water, the dried longans, dried jujube, and ginkgo in a large pan and bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for about 15 minutes, adding more water if necessary. Add the sugar to taste, then transfer to a heatproof serving bowl and serve.

recipes.title: Ginkgo Nuts, Taro, and Coconut Dessert
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g diced taro water and meat of 2 young coconuts

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 2 liters water and the sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the ginkgo nuts and taro, reduce the heat, and simmer for about 15 minutes, until softened. Add the coconut water and meat and continue to simmer for 5 minutes.
Dissolve the tapioca flour in 2 tablespoons water, then gradually pour into the pan, stirring continuously. Bring to a boil, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Bring the coconut cream to a boil in another pan, add the salt, stir, and return to a boil. Remove from the heat.
Put the ginkgo nuts and coconut meat in small serving bowls and pour the coconut cream over them. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Ginkgo Nuts, Taro, and Coconut Dessert Central 300 g granulated sugar 1 kg shelled ginkgo nuts 200 g diced taro water and meat of 2 young coconuts 2 tablespoons tapioca flour 250 ml coconut cream 1 teaspoon salt Bring 2 liters water and the sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the ginkgo nuts and taro, reduce the heat, and simmer for about 15 minutes, until softened. Add the coconut water and meat and continue to simmer for 5 minutes. Dissolve the tapioca flour in 2 tablespoons water, then gradually pour into the pan, stirring continuously. Bring to a boil, then remove from the heat and set aside. Bring the coconut cream to a boil in another pan, add the salt, stir, and return to a boil. Remove from the heat. Put the ginkgo nuts and coconut meat in small serving bowls and pour the coconut cream over them. Serve.

recipes.title: Glutinous Rice with Coconut and Black Sesame
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 5 banana leaves, cut into 5 x 15 cm strips

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice in a large bowl of water overnight or for at least 3 hours, then drain.
Lay a banana-leaf strip on a flat work surface. Place a little rice at one end, leaving a 1 cm border.
Fold the leaf and filling diagonally to form a triangle. Continue folding into triangles until the end of the leaf is reached, then secure with toothpicks. Repeat with the remaining rice.
Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan. Carefully add the packages, return to a boil, reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Remove the packages with a slotted spoon, drain, and let cool.
Combine the coconut, sesame seeds, and sugar in a small bowl.
Unwrap the rice packages and discard the leaves. Roll the rice in the coconut, sesame, and sugar mixture, then serve.

recipes.searchText: Glutinous Rice with Coconut and Black Sesame North 500 g glutinous (sticky) rice 5 banana leaves, cut into 5 x 15 cm strips 300 g dry unsweetened (desiccated) coconut 100 g black sesame seeds 200 g granulated sugar Soak the rice in a large bowl of water overnight or for at least 3 hours, then drain. Lay a banana-leaf strip on a flat work surface. Place a little rice at one end, leaving a 1 cm border. Fold the leaf and filling diagonally to form a triangle. Continue folding into triangles until the end of the leaf is reached, then secure with toothpicks. Repeat with the remaining rice. Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan. Carefully add the packages, return to a boil, reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour. Remove the packages with a slotted spoon, drain, and let cool. Combine the coconut, sesame seeds, and sugar in a small bowl. Unwrap the rice packages and discard the leaves. Roll the rice in the coconut, sesame, and sugar mixture, then serve.

recipes.title: Sesame and Sugar-Coated Peanuts
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Rinse the peanuts in plenty of cold water, then drain and set aside.

Put 120 ml water, the peanuts, and sugar in a wok over medium heat and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring continuously for about 20 minutes or until thickened. Be careful not to let the sugar boil and caramelize. Remove from the heat and continue stirring until the sugar cools, dries, and coats the peanuts. Sprinkle with the salt, and put the pan back over medium heat. Stir continuously for about 10 minutes until the sugar coating the peanuts starts to melt again. Add the sesame seeds and stir until the peanuts are well coated, then remove from the heat. Transfer to a large tray and use a spatula to separate the peanuts. Let cool, then serve.

recipes.searchText: Sesame and Sugar-Coated Peanuts Central 300 g raw peanuts 250 g granulated sugar 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 2 tablespoons white sesame seeds Rinse the peanuts in plenty of cold water, then drain and set aside. Put 120 ml water, the peanuts, and sugar in a wok over medium heat and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring continuously for about 20 minutes or until thickened. Be careful not to let the sugar boil and caramelize. Remove from the heat and continue stirring until the sugar cools, dries, and coats the peanuts. Sprinkle with the salt, and put the pan back over medium heat. Stir continuously for about 10 minutes until the sugar coating the peanuts starts to melt again. Add the sesame seeds and stir until the peanuts are well coated, then remove from the heat. Transfer to a large tray and use a spatula to separate the peanuts. Let cool, then serve.

recipes.title: Coconut Custard in Pumpkin
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 175 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Remove the top of the Thai pumpkin by cutting around the stem to create a "lid" 8 cm in diameter. Set the lid aside. Scoop out the seeds with a spoon. Set aside.

Whisk the eggs and coconut cream together in a bowl, add the sugar, salt, and pandan leaves. and mix well. Use your hand to squeeze the mixture until the pandan leaves are soft and aromatic and the sugar has dissolved. Strain through cheesecloth (muslin) or a fine strainer (sieve) and pour into the pumpkin. Fill to just under the top of the pumpkin.

Carefully place the pumpkin and its lid (on the side), into a large steamer, at least twice the size of the pumpkin. Steam over medium heat for 35-40 minutes or until the custard is firm and cooked and the pumpkin is soft Let cool slightly, then serve whole with the reserved lid on top.

recipes.searchText: Coconut Custard in Pumpkin Central 1 small pumpkin, 12 cm in diameter 4 duck eggs, beaten 150 ml coconut cream 175 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 2 pandan leaves Remove the top of the Thai pumpkin by cutting around the stem to create a "lid" 8 cm in diameter. Set the lid aside. Scoop out the seeds with a spoon. Set aside. Whisk the eggs and coconut cream together in a bowl, add the sugar, salt, and pandan leaves. and mix well. Use your hand to squeeze the mixture until the pandan leaves are soft and aromatic and the sugar has dissolved. Strain through cheesecloth (muslin) or a fine strainer (sieve) and pour into the pumpkin. Fill to just under the top of the pumpkin. Carefully place the pumpkin and its lid (on the side), into a large steamer, at least twice the size of the pumpkin. Steam over medium heat for 35-40 minutes or until the custard is firm and cooked and the pumpkin is soft Let cool slightly, then serve whole with the reserved lid on top.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Custard
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 450 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
350 g peeled, seeded, and sliced pumpkin batons (4 cm long and 1 cm wide)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Beat the eggs in a bowl until lightly foamy.

Mix the coconut milk and sugar together in another bowl until well blended, then pour into the beaten egg and mix well. Strain the mixture through a strainer (sieve) into a 20 cm square baking pan 5 cm deep. Sprinkle with the pumpkin batons and steam in a steamer over high heat for about 20 minutes or until firm. Let cool, then cut the custard into 16 squares and serve.

recipes.searchText: Pumpkin Custard Central 11 duck eggs 400 ml coconut milk 450 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 350 g peeled, seeded, and sliced pumpkin batons (4 cm long and 1 cm wide) Beat the eggs in a bowl until lightly foamy. Mix the coconut milk and sugar together in another bowl until well blended, then pour into the beaten egg and mix well. Strain the mixture through a strainer (sieve) into a 20 cm square baking pan 5 cm deep. Sprinkle with the pumpkin batons and steam in a steamer over high heat for about 20 minutes or until firm.
