recipes.title: Sweet Potato in Ginger Syrup
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3 sweet potatoes, cut into 4 cm cubes
90 g peeled and sliced fresh ginger (3 cm-thick pieces)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the sugar and salt and return to a boil for 1-2 minutes. Add the sweet potatoes and ginger and continue to boil for another 10-12 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool for 10 minutes. Serve hot or cold.

recipes.searchText: Sweet Potato in Ginger Syrup South 200 g granulated sugar 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 3 sweet potatoes, cut into 4 cm cubes 90 g peeled and sliced fresh ginger (3 cm-thick pieces) Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the sugar and salt and return to a boil for 1-2 minutes. Add the sweet potatoes and ginger and continue to boil for another 10-12 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool for 10 minutes. Serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Pumpkin in Syrup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1.5 kg pumpkin, peeled and cut into bite-size pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the pumpkin in the limewater for about 30 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Bring the coconut cream to a boil in a pan over low heat and add the salt. Add the rice flour and stir occasionally until the coconut milk has thickened.

Bring 350 ml water, the sugar, and lime juice to a boil in another pan over medium heal. Boil, stirring occasionally until the sugar has dissolved, then add the pumpkin. Cook for about 10 minutes until the pumpkin is glossy. Transfer to a serving bowl, pour the coconut milk over the top, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Pumpkin in Syrup Central 1.5 kg pumpkin, peeled and cut into bite-size pieces 2 liters limewater (see p. 509) 120 ml coconut cream 1⁄4 teaspoon salt 1 tablespoon rice flour 300 g granulated sugar 1⁄2 teaspoon lime juice Soak the pumpkin in the limewater for about 30 minutes, then rinse and drain. Bring the coconut cream to a boil in a pan over low heat and add the salt. Add the rice flour and stir occasionally until the coconut milk has thickened. Bring 350 ml water, the sugar, and lime juice to a boil in another pan over medium heal. Boil, stirring occasionally until the sugar has dissolved, then add the pumpkin. Cook for about 10 minutes until the pumpkin is glossy. Transfer to a serving bowl, pour the coconut milk over the top, and serve.

recipes.title: Wax Gourd Dessert
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 280 g peeled and grated wax gourd
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
90 g peeled and grated overripe coconut
1 teaspoon salt Banana leaves, cut into 20 cm-wide strips

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the grated wax gourd in cheesecloth and squeeze into a bowl to remove any excess liquid. Discard the liquid and put the damp wax gourd flesh in a bowl.
Sprinkle with the tapioca flour and mix well. Add the sugar, grated coconut, and salt and mix again. The mixture should be neither too thick nor too dry.

Lay a banana leaf on a work surface. Put 2 tablespoons of the wax gourd mixture in the center. Cover the filling with the sides of the leaf and fold over the ends to make a package. Secure with toothpicks and repeat with the remaining mixture.
Place the packages in a steamer and steam over high heat for 30 minutes, or until cooked. Let cool, then serve.

recipes.searchText: Wax Gourd Dessert South 280 g peeled and grated wax gourd 190 g tapioca flour 225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 90 g peeled and grated overripe coconut 1 teaspoon salt Banana leaves, cut into 20 cm-wide strips Put the grated wax gourd in cheesecloth and squeeze into a bowl to remove any excess liquid. Discard the liquid and put the damp wax gourd flesh in a bowl. Sprinkle with the tapioca flour and mix well. Add the sugar, grated coconut, and salt and mix again. The mixture should be neither too thick nor too dry. Lay a banana leaf on a work surface. Put 2 tablespoons of the wax gourd mixture in the center. Cover the filling with the sides of the leaf and fold over the ends to make a package. Secure with toothpicks and repeat with the remaining mixture. Place the packages in a steamer and steam over high heat for 30 minutes, or until cooked. Let cool, then serve.

recipes.title: Coconut Cakes with Herbs
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the batter, mix the rice flour with 475 ml tepid water in a bowl.

Mix the coconut milk, salt, sugar, cilantro (coriander), and scallions (spring onions) together in another bowl Coat the khanom krok pan or pancake puff pan with oil and place over medium heat. The pan is ready when a small drop of batter sizzles. Stir the batter and carefully pour a little into the molds until about two-thirds full, then carefully pour the coconut milk mixture on top to fill the molds. Cover with a lid and cook for about 5 minutes before removing the desserts from the molds with a spoon or fork. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Coconut Cakes with Herbs Central 500 g rice flour 2.5 liters coconut milk 1 tablespoon salt 300 g granulated sugar 120 ml vegetable oil, for costing 2 cilantro (coriander) sprigs, chopped 2 scallions (spring onions), chopped For the batter, mix the rice flour with 475 ml tepid water in a bowl. Mix the coconut milk, salt, sugar, cilantro (coriander), and scallions (spring onions) together in another bowl Coat the khanom krok pan or pancake puff pan with oil and place over medium heat. recipes.title: Coconut Milk Custard
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 250 ml unshaken can coconut milk, cream and mill separated
125 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Season the coconut cream with salt. Set aside.
Mix the coconut milk and the rice flour together in a large bowl, add the sugar, and stir well.
Pour the mixture into small talai cups or small heatproof cups or bowls about three-quarters full and steam in a steamer for 10 minutes until cooked.
Pour the coconut cream over the rice mixture and continue to steam for another 10 minutes until the coconut cream is cooked. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Coconut Milk Custard North 250 ml unshaken can coconut milk, cream and mill separated 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 250 g rice flour 125 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar Season the coconut cream with salt. Pour the mixture into small talai cups or small heatproof cups or bowls about three-quarters full and steam in a steamer for 10 minutes until cooked. Pour the coconut cream over the rice mixture and continue to steam for another 10 minutes until the coconut cream is cooked. Serve.

recipes.title: Gelatin in Young Coconut
recipes.subtitle: Central
recipes.prepTime: 35 minutes plus setting and chilling time

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Strain the water through cheesecloth (muslin) and bring to a boil in a pan. Add the gelatin powder, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes, Pour the coconut water mixture back into the coconuts and let set for 30 minutes. chill in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

recipes.searchText: Gelatin in Young Coconut Central 3 fresh young coconuts 85 g granulated sugar 11⁄2 tablespoons gelatin powder Strain the water through cheesecloth (muslin) and bring to a boil in a pan. Add the gelatin powder, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes, Pour the coconut water mixture back into the coconuts and let set for 30 minutes. chill in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

recipes.title: Fried Bananas
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 6-8 semi-ripe small bananas, peeled and sliced into 1 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the sugar, flours, coconut, coconut milk, sesame seeds, salt, and 60 ml water together in a large bowl until the sugar and flour have dissolved.
Dip the bananas into the batter and make sure they are well coated.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the bananas for 6-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Fried Bananas Central 1 tablespoon superfine (caster) sugar 120 g rice flour 30 g all-purpose (plain) flour 45 g dry unsweetened (desiccated) coconut 250 ml coconut milk 2 tablespoons white sesame seeds 1 teaspoon salt 6-8 semi-ripe small bananas, peeled and sliced into 1 cm lengths 1.2 liters vegetable oil, for deep-frying Mix the sugar, flours, coconut, coconut milk, sesame seeds, salt, and 60 ml water together in a large bowl until the sugar and flour have dissolved. Dip the bananas into the batter and make sure they are well coated. Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the bananas for 6-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve.

recipes.title: Tapioca and Young Coconut in Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil in a pan over medium-high heat. Put the tapioca pearls in a strainer (sieve) and dip in water, then shake once. Add to the pan of boiling water and cook for about 7 minutes, stirring occasionally until the tapioca pearls are cooked and translucent. Add the sugar and coconut meat and gently stir until the sugar has dissolved, then remove from the heat.
Heat the coconut milk and salt in another pan over low heat for about 5 minutes. Transfer the tapioca to small serving bowls with the coconut milk on the side.

recipes.searchText: Tapioca and Young Coconut in Coconut Milk Central 150 g small tapioca pearls 100 g superfine (caster) sugar 100 g shredded fresh coconut 1+300 ml coconut milk 1⁄2 teaspoon salt Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil in a pan over medium-high heat. Put the tapioca pearls in a strainer (sieve) and dip in water, then shake once. Add to the pan of boiling water and cook for about 7 minutes, stirring occasionally until the tapioca pearls are cooked and translucent. Add the sugar and coconut meat and gently stir until the sugar has dissolved, then remove from the heat. Heat the coconut milk and salt in another pan over low heat for about 5 minutes. Transfer the tapioca to small serving bowls with the coconut milk on the side.

recipes.title: Banana with Shredded Coconut and Sesame Seeds
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the shredded coconut and salt together in a small bowl and set aside.

Bring a medium pan of water to a boil, add the bananas, and cook for 20 minutes. Drain the bananas in a colander and cool under cold running water, then slice lengthwise. Put the banana slices into the coconut mixture and roll to coat. Place on a serving plate and sprinkle with sesame seeds and sugar. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Banana with Shredded Coconut and Sesame Seeds Central 80 g shredded coconut 1 teaspoon salt 10 semi-ripe small bananas, peeled 1 teaspoon sesame seeds, roasted 2 tablespoons granulated sugar Mix the shredded coconut and salt together in a small bowl and set aside. Bring a medium pan of water to a boil, add the bananas, and cook for 20 minutes. Drain the bananas in a colander and cool under cold running water, then slice lengthwise. Put the banana slices into the coconut mixture and roll to coat. Place on a serving plate and sprinkle with sesame seeds and sugar. Serve.

recipes.title: Bananas in Syrup
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring a medium pan of water to a boil, add the bananas, reduce the heat, and simmer for 10 minutes until tender. Remove with a slotted spoon and cut into 2.5 cm-thick slices. Set aside.

Bring the sugar and 350 ml water to a boil in another pan and boil for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved. Add the banana pieces, reduce the heat, and cook for 30 minutes or until the syrup thickens and the bananas turn red. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Bananas in Syrup Central 10 semi-ripe small bananas, peeled 500 g granulated sugar Bring a medium pan of water to a boil, add the bananas, reduce the heat, and simmer for 10 minutes until tender. Remove with a slotted spoon and cut into 2.5 cm-thick slices. Set aside. Bring the sugar and 350 ml water to a boil in another pan and boil for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved. Add the banana pieces, reduce the heat, and cook for 30 minutes or until the syrup thickens and the bananas turn red. Serve.

recipes.title: Glutinous Rice, Beans, and Banana in Palm Leaves
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 small ripe bananas, cut lengthwise into 3 slices Palm leaves, for wrapping

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice in water for about 1 hour, then drain and set aside.
Bring the coconut milk and salt to a boil in a wok or pan over medium heat.
Add the rice and cook, stirring constantly, for about 5 minutes, until dry.
Add the sugar and stir-fry for another 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, add the black beans, and stir. Let cool.
Lay a palm leaf on a work surface. Place 1 tablespoon rice mixture between 2 thin banana slices on the leaf.
Fold the leaf into a package and secure with toothpicks. Repeat until all the filling is used.
Steam the packages for about 40 minutes, until the rice is sticky, then serve.

recipes.searchText: Glutinous Rice, Beans, and Banana in Palm Leaves South 500 g glutinous (sticky) rice 400 ml coconut milk 1 teaspoon salt 200 g superfine (caster) sugar 100 g cooked black beans 10 small ripe bananas, cut lengthwise into 3 slices Palm leaves, for wrapping Soak the rice in water for about 1 hour, then drain and set aside. Bring the coconut milk and salt to a boil in a wok or pan over medium heat. Add the rice and cook, stirring constantly, for about 5 minutes, until dry. Add the sugar and stir-fry for another 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, add the black beans, and stir. Let cool. Lay a palm leaf on a work surface. Place 1 tablespoon rice mixture between 2 thin banana slices on the leaf. Fold the leaf into a package and secure with toothpicks. Repeat until all the filling is used. Steam the packages for about 40 minutes, until the rice is sticky, then serve.

recipes.title: Banana with Shredded Coconut
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Spread the shredded coconut in a shallow bowl or plate.
Steam the unpeeled bananas for about 10 minutes, or until soft and tender. Peel and cut into 2.5 cm pieces, then roll in the coconut until coated.
Mix the sugar and salt in a small bowl, sprinkle over the bananas, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Banana with Shredded Coconut Central 80 g shredded young coconut meat 10 ripe small bananas 2 tablespoons granulated sugar 1⁄2 teaspoon salt Spread the shredded coconut in a shallow bowl or plate. Steam the unpeeled bananas for about 10 minutes, or until soft and tender. Peel and cut into 2.5 cm pieces, then roll in the coconut until coated. Mix the sugar and salt in a small bowl, sprinkle over the bananas, and serve.

recipes.title: Caramelized Bananas
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 8 semi-ripe small bananas, peeled, or 4 ordinary bananas, halved crosswise
1 teaspoon all-purpose (plain) flour a pinch of salt

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the sugar, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the pandan leaves, return to a boil, and remove from the heat.

Strain the syrup into a pan and discard the pandan. Add the bananas and simmer over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes on each side, or until glossy and the syrup is absorbed. Sprinkle with lime juice, remove from the heat, and transfer to a serving plate.
Mix the coconut milk, flour, and salt in a small pan over medium-low heat for 2-3 minutes, or until thickened. Drizzle over the bananas and serve immediately.

recipes.searchText: Caramelized Bananas Central 300 g superfine (caster) sugar 2 pandan leaves, sliced 8 semi-ripe small bananas, peeled, or 4 ordinary bananas, halved crosswise 1 teaspoon lime juice 120 ml coconut milk 1 teaspoon all-purpose (plain) flour a pinch of salt Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the sugar, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the pandan leaves, return to a boil, and remove from the heat. Strain the syrup into a pan and discard the pandan. Add the bananas and simmer over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes on each side, or until glossy and the syrup is absorbed. Sprinkle with lime juice, remove from the heat, and transfer to a serving plate. Mix the coconut milk, flour, and salt in a small pan over medium-low heat for 2-3 minutes, or until thickened. Drizzle over the bananas and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Sweet Banana
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 ripe small bananas, peeled and mashed
200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the coconut and salt in a small bowl. Reserve half for the garnish.
Mix the bananas, rice flour, sugar, remaining coconut and salt, and coconut milk in a large bowl.
Pour into small heatproof cups or bowls, sprinkle with the reserved coconut, steam for 30 minutes, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Sweet Banana Central 100 g shredded fresh coconut 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 10 ripe small bananas, peeled and mashed 160 g rice flour 200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 250 ml coconut milk Mix the coconut and salt in a small bowl. Reserve half for the garnish. Mix the bananas, rice flour, sugar, remaining coconut and salt, and coconut milk in a large bowl. Pour into small heatproof cups or bowls, sprinkle with the reserved coconut, steam for 30 minutes, and serve.

recipes.title: Bananas in Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Dry-fry the mung beans in a wok over low heat for 5 minutes until roasted, shaking and stirring to prevent the beans from burning. Meanwhile, bring a small pan of water to a boil, then add the mung beans and cook for 5 minutes.

Bring another pan of water to a boil, add the bananas, and boil for 10 minutes. Drain and transfer to a bowl of cold water for 3-4 minutes. Drain, then cut the bananas in half lengthwise and then into 2.5 cm slices.
Bring the coconut milk to a simmer in a wok over low heat, add the mung beans, and cook for 10 minutes. Add the salt, sugar, and bananas and cook for another 5 minutes. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Bananas in Coconut Milk Central 1 tablespoon split mung beanss 10 small bananas, peeled 475 ml coconut milk 1 teaspoon salt 300 g granulated sugar Dry-fry the mung beans in a wok over low heat for 5 minutes until roasted, shaking and stirring to prevent the beans from burning. recipes.title: Jackfruit and Tapioca Threads in Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g tapioca flour, plus extra for sprinkling
250 g sliced jackfruit Ice cubes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the syrup, bring 175 ml water and the sugar to a boil over medium heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves and the mixture becomes syrupy.
Put the tapioca flour in a large bowl and gradually add 100 ml hot water, stirring quickly. Knead for 5 minutes, until a dough forms.
Divide the dough into 3 portions. Color one green and another red, leaving the third uncolored. Knead each portion separately on a lightly floured work surface.
Bring a pan of water to a boil and have a bowl of cold water ready. Roll each portion into a thin sheet, cut into thin threads, and dust with tapioca flour to prevent sticking.
Boil the threads for 3-4 minutes, until transparent. Remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to the cold water.
Bring the coconut milk and salt to a boil in another pan over medium heat, then remove from the heat.
Divide the tapioca threads and jackfruit among bowls. Pour over the coconut milk and sugar syrup, add a few ice cubes, and serve.

recipes.title: Rice Pudding with Longans and Butterfly Pea Flowers
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 small handful fresh butterfly pes flowers

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice in a bowl of water overnight The next day, drain and rinse under cold running water. Bring 750 ml water to a boil in a pan. Add the rice and butterfly pea flowers and cook for about 15 minutes or until the rice is softened. Add the sugar and longans, then remove the pan from the heat and set aside. Bring the coconut cream to a boil in another pan over low-medium heat, then stir in the salt.
Put the rice mixture into a serving bowl and pour the coconut cream over it. Serve.

recipes.title: Tapioca with Longan
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil in a pan over medium-high heat.

Put the tapioca pearls in a strainer (sieve) and dip in water, then shake once. Add to the pan of boiling water and cook for about 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tapioca pearls are cooked and translucent. Remove from the heat and drain. Return to the pan, add the sugar, and longans, and gently stir until the sugar has dissolved. Heat the coconut milk and salt in another pan over low heat for about 5 minutes. Transfer the tapioca and longan mixture to a serving bowl and pour the coconut milk over it. Serve.

Transfer the tapioca and longan mixture to a serving bowl and pour the coconut milk over it. Serve.

recipes.title: Glutinous Rice with Mango
recipes.subtitle: Central
recipes.prepTime: 10 minutes, plus soaking and standing time

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 ripe mangoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm-wide slices

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice in a bowl of water for at least 3 hours, or preferably overnight, then rinse and drain.
Soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 1 hour. Drain and pat dry with paper towels.
Wrap the rice in cheesecloth and steam for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes. The rice will look transparent when cooked.
Put the coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a small pan over low-medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat and set aside, reserving about 75 ml for the topping.
Toast the mung beans in a dry skillet over low-medium heat, stirring frequently, for 5 minutes, or until dark yellow and completely dry.
Transfer the cooked rice to a bowl and add the sweet coconut milk. Mix well, cover, and let stand for 10-15 minutes.
Top the sweet rice with the toasted mung beans and serve with the mango slices and reserved coconut milk.

recipes.title: Mangosteen in Syrup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g mangosteen, peeled and seeded crushed ice, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the sugar and salt and return to a boil for 1-2 minutes or until the sugar has dissolved. Add the mangosteen and continue to boil over low heat until softened. Remove from the heat and let cool. Transfer to a bowl, cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm), and let marinate in the refrigerator for 24 hours.
Remove the mangosteen from the refrigerator, add crushed ice, and serve cold.

recipes.title: Pandan Leaf Noodles in Coconut Milk Syrup
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 250 ml limewater (see p. 509) or club soda (soda water)
1 tablespoon mung bean flour ice cubes, to serve

ingredientGroups.heading: For the coconut milk syrup
lines: 225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blend the pandan leaves with 750 ml water until thoroughly combined. Strain through a very fine sieve or cheesecloth and reserve the extract.
Mix the flours together, then gradually stir in the limewater or club soda until a dough forms. Knead for 4-5 minutes, then add the pandan extract and mix until smooth.

Prepare a large bowl of ice-cold water. Cook the flour mixture in a nonstick pan or wok over medium heat for 6-7 minutes, stirring until it begins to thicken. Reduce the heat and stir for another 4-5 minutes, until thick, dark green, glossy, and syrupy. Adjust with a little water if necessary.
Transfer the mixture to a potato ricer and press the strands into the ice water. Leave for 5-7 minutes, or until firm, then transfer to a clean bowl with a slotted spoon.
For the syrup, heat the coconut milk, sugar, and salt over low heat for about 5 minutes, or until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat and cool.
Divide the pandan noodles among bowls, pour over the cooled coconut milk syrup, top with ice cubes, and serve.

recipes.title: Candied Sugar Palm Fruit
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Rinse the sugar palm fruit and scrub its skin with the shredded banana leaf to remove its grease, then rinse again under cold running water.
Mix the ground alum and 1 liter water together in a large bowl. Soak the sugar palm fruit in the alum water for 30 minutes, then remove and rinse under cold running water.
Bring a pan of water to a boil, add the sugar palm fruit, and boil for 5 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.

To prepare the sugar syrup, mix 5 liters water and 600 g of the sugar together in a pan and bring to a boil. Add the sugar palm fruit, reduce the heat, and simmer over medium heat for 1-2 hours. Add more water if necessary. Gradually add the remaining sugar until the fruit has absorbed the sugar and become shiny. Let cool, then serve the candied fruit on the whole banana leaf.

recipes.searchText: Candied Sugar Palm Fruit Central 25 mature sugar palm fruit 1 shredded banana leaf 10 g ground alum 1 kg granulated sugar 1 banana leaf Rinse the sugar palm fruit and scrub its skin with the shredded banana leaf to remove its grease, then rinse again under cold running water. recipes.title: Muskmelon in Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 muskmelon or cantaloupe, peeled, seeded, and cut into bite-size pieces crushed ice cubes, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the coconut milk in a pan over low heat. Add the sugar and salt and stir continuously until it reaches a gentle boil. Remove from the heat and let cool.
Put about I cubes of muskmelon or cantaloupe into a serving bowl. Add the coconut milk syrup and some crushed ice cubes and serve.

recipes.searchText: Muskmelon in Coconut Milk Central 200 ml coconut milk 225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 1 teaspoon salt 1 muskmelon or cantaloupe, peeled, seeded, and cut into bite-size pieces crushed ice cubes, to serve Heat the coconut milk in a pan over low heat. Add the sugar and salt and stir continuously until it reaches a gentle boil. Remove from the heat and let cool. Put about I cubes of muskmelon or cantaloupe into a serving bowl. recipes.title: Pandan Pudding
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 250 ml limewater (see p. 508) or club soda
75 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Grease a baking sheet with oil and set aside.
Put the pandan leaves and 250 ml water in a food processor and blend until smooth.
Mix the flours together in a wok or pan, then gradually add the limewater or club soda, stirring constantly.
Add the pandan juice and stir until smooth. Add both sugars and stir until thoroughly combined.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture begins to cook. Reduce the heat slightly and continue stirring for 7-8 minutes in total, until shiny, solid, and dark green.
Pour onto the prepared baking sheet and spread evenly with a spatula. Let cool.
Cut into 6 cm squares, remove from the tray, sprinkle with the grated coconut, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Pandan Pudding Central Vegetable oil, for greasing 10 pandan leaves 80 g rice flour 1 tablespoon mung bean flour 1⁄2 tablespoon tapioca flour 250 ml limewater (see p. 508) or club soda 11⁄2 tablespoons granulated sugar 75 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 80 g grated fresh coconut Grease a baking sheet with oil and set aside. Add the pandan juice and stir until smooth. Add both sugars and stir until thoroughly combined. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture begins to cook. Cut into 6 cm squares, remove from the tray, sprinkle with the grated coconut, and serve.

recipes.title: Pandan and Coconut Milk Gelatin
recipes.subtitle: Central
recipes.prepTime: 8 minutes, plus setting and chilling time

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the coconut gelatin (jelly), heat the coconut milk in a pan to 104-122°F/40-50°C, then add the gelatin powder. Stir until the gelatin melts, then add the salt. Stir and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, add the sugar, and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Fill a shallow tray halfway with the mixture and let cool at room temperature for about 25 minutes. To make the pandan gelatin, heat 750 ml water in a pan to 104-122°F/ 40-50°C and add the gelatin powder. Stir until the gelatin melts, then bring to a boil over low heat and continue to stir. Reduce the heat, add the sugar, and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Pour in the pandan juice and stir to combine When the coconut gelatin starts to set, pour the pandan gelatin on top, and set aside at room temperature for about 25 minutes or until set, then chill in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes or until firm. To serve, cut the gelatin into squares with a serrated knife and transfer to serving plates.

recipes.title: Crispy Fried Whole Fish with Roasted Chile and Garlic Sauce

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 35 g long red chile, finely chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the snapper for 7 minutes, until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and place on a serving plate.
Heat the sunflower oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the shallots and stir-fry for 5 minutes, until fragrant and reduced by about half. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 3-5 minutes, until soft.

Add the chile and stir for 1 minute, then add the broth, cherry tomatoes, tamarind puree, fish sauce, and sugar. Stir briefly and pour over the fish. Garnish with the chiles and kaffir lime leaves and serve.

recipes.searchText: Crispy Fried Whole Fish with Roasted Chile and Garlic Sauce 1 liter vegetable oil, for deep-frying 700 g whole red snapper 4 tablespoons sunflower oil 200 g finely diced shallots 35 g garlic, finely chopped 35 g long red chile, finely chopped 175 ml chicken broth (stock) 4 cherry tomatoes, halved 31⁄2 tablespoons Tamarind Puree 60 ml fish sauce 31⁄2 tablespoons superfine (caster) sugar 2 long red chiles, finely sliced 4 kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. recipes.title: Green Papaya Salad

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 tablespoons grated jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Shred the green papaya and immediately soak it in iced water for 5 minutes. Drain and refrigerate until ready to use.
Pound the sugar, garlic, and chiles in a mortar until almost paste-like, using a large spoon to scoop and toss the mixture.
Add the green beans, peanuts, and dried shrimp and pound until lightly flattened and crushed.
Add the tomatoes and gently crush them so the juices release without completely breaking them down.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice and pound and toss until the sugar dissolves.
Add the shredded papaya, toss until well mixed, and serve.

Drain and refrigerate until ready to use. Pound the sugar, garlic, and chiles in a mortar until almost paste-like, using a large spoon to scoop and toss the mixture. Add the fish sauce and lime juice and pound and toss until the sugar dissolves. Add the shredded papaya, toss until well mixed, and serve.

recipes.title: Beef Satay

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, sugar, and spices in a blender and process until smooth. Transfer to a bowl, add the coconut milk, and mix well.
Add the beef to the marinade and turn until well coated. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Preheat the broiler (grill). Thread the marinated beef onto skewers and broil for 5 minutes on each side, until cooked. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Beef Satay 3 lemongrass stalks 18 cm piece galangal, peeled 4-6 kaffir lime leaves 1 teaspoon granulated sugar 2 teaspoons curry powder 2 teaspoons ground coriander 4-5 cilantro (coriander) roots 1 teaspoon turmeric 1 teaspoon ground caraway 1⁄2 teaspoon salt 60 ml coconut milk 400 g beef, very thinly sliced Put the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, sugar, and spices in a blender and process until smooth. Transfer to a bowl, add the coconut milk, and mix well. Add the beef to the marinade and turn until well coated. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours. Preheat the broiler (grill). recipes.title: Spaghetti with Pork, Chile, and Basil

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 25 g holy or sweet basil leaves

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the chiles and garlic in a mortar and crush with a pestle.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and chile and stir-fry for 1 minute, or until golden brown.
Add the pork and stir-fry for about 5 minutes, until cooked. Season with the fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar, then toss to mix well.
Add the cooked spaghetti, basil, and kaffir lime leaves and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spaghetti with Pork, Chile, and Basil 3 tablespoons hot chiles 3 cloves garlic 3 tablespoons vegetable oil 500 g ground (minced) pork 11⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce 1 tablespoon soy sauce 1 teaspoon granulated sugar 400 g spaghetti, cooked 25 g holy or sweet basil leaves 3 kaffir lime leaves, chopped Put the chiles and garlic in a mortar and crush with a pestle. Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and chile and stir-fry for 1 minute, or until golden brown. Add the pork and stir-fry for about 5 minutes, until cooked. recipes.title: Stir-Fried Rice Noodles with Northern Thailand Chili Paste

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10 dried chiles, or fewer for a milder dish
To garnish Chopped cilantro (coriander) Chopped scallion (spring onion)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in water for about 10 minutes, or according to the package directions, until soft. Drain and set aside.
Blend the dried chiles, shallots, and garlic until smooth.
Heat the oil in a skillet over high heat for 10 seconds. Add the chile mixture and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until cooked through.

Add the cherry tomatoes, shrimp paste, sugar, and fish sauce and stir to combine. Pat the noodles with paper towels to remove excess moisture, add them to the pan, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, until soft.
Garnish with the cilantro and scallion and serve.

Pat the noodles with paper towels to remove excess moisture, add them to the pan, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, until soft. Garnish with the cilantro and scallion and serve.

recipes.title: Thai Calamari

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 tablespoon egg yolk Pinch of salt
200 g squid, cut into small strips Vegetable oil, for deep-frying

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish
lines: 1 teaspoon chopped green and red bell pepper

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blend the lemongrass and cilantro roots until combined, then transfer to a bowl.
Mix the cornstarch, egg yolk, and salt in another bowl to make a batter. Add the squid to the lemongrass mixture and stir until coated.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C. Dip the coated squid into the batter, then deep-fry in batches for 2-3 minutes, until crisp and golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

For the garnish, heat 1 teaspoon oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the bell pepper, onion, chiles, lemongrass, and lime leaves and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Place the squid on a serving plate, garnish with the stir-fried vegetables, and serve.

recipes.searchText: Thai Calamari 3-4 cilantro (coriander) roots 1 lemongrass stalk 1 tablespoon cornstarch (cornflour) 1 tablespoon egg yolk Pinch of salt 200 g squid, cut into small strips Vegetable oil, for deep-frying 1 teaspoon vegetable oil 1 teaspoon chopped green and red bell pepper 1 teaspoon chopped white onion 2-3 red chiles, sliced 1 lemongrass stalk, finely sliced 1 teaspoon torn lime leaves Blend the lemongrass and cilantro roots until combined, then transfer to a bowl. Mix the cornstarch, egg yolk, and salt in another bowl to make a batter. Add the squid to the lemongrass mixture and stir until coated. Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C. Dip the coated squid into the batter, then deep-fry in batches for 2-3 minutes, until crisp and golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. For the garnish, heat 1 teaspoon oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the bell pepper, onion, chiles, lemongrass, and lime leaves and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Place the squid on a serving plate, garnish with the stir-fried vegetables, and serve.

recipes.title: Charcoal Grilled Blowfish Tails with Seafood Nam Prik

ingredientGroups.heading: For the seafood dipping sauce
lines: 1 tablespoon chopped cilantro (coriander) leaves and stems
21⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar, softened in a microwave
1 heaping teaspoon olive oil Zest of 1 lime Pinch of salt

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blend all the marinade ingredients until smooth. Pour into a bowl, add the blowfish tails, cover, and marinate for at least 45 minutes.
For the dipping sauce, mix the garlic, cilantro, chiles, and softened sugar in a bowl. Add the lime juice, vinegar, fish sauce, olive oil, lime zest, and salt and whisk until thoroughly combined.

Heat a charcoal grill until the coals are glowing white, or preheat a gas grill to 190°C. Grill the fish over medium-high heat for about 4 minutes on each side, until lightly charred and cooked through. Serve with the seafood dipping sauce.

recipes.searchText: Charcoal Grilled Blowfish Tails with Seafood Nam Prik 450 g blowfish tails, cleaned 240 ml coconut milk 1⁄2 lemongrass stalk, sliced 20 g sliced cilantro (coriander) stems 10 g kaffir lime leaves 1 small clove garlic, chopped 1 tablespoon chopped cilantro (coriander) leaves and stems 2 green bird's-eye chiles, sliced 21⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar, softened in a microwave 80 ml lime juice 2 tablespoons white vinegar 2 tablespoons fish sauce 1 heaping teaspoon olive oil Zest of 1 lime Pinch of salt Blend all the marinade ingredients until smooth. Pour into a bowl, add the blowfish tails, cover, and marinate for at least 45 minutes. For the dipping sauce, mix the garlic, cilantro, chiles, and softened sugar in a bowl. Add the lime juice, vinegar, fish sauce, olive oil, lime zest, and salt and whisk until thoroughly combined. Heat a charcoal grill until the coals are glowing white, or preheat a gas grill to 190°C. Grill the fish over medium-high heat for about 4 minutes on each side, until lightly charred and cooked through. Serve with the seafood dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Coconut Sundae with Palm Sugar Whipped Cream and Sweet and Salty Peanuts

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 tablespoons freshly grated coconut meat, toasted

ingredientGroups.heading: For the palm sugar whipped cream
lines: 85 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
For the candied peanuts Canola (rapeseed) oil, for deep-frying

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the whipped cream, briefly microwave the palm sugar in a heatproof bowl to melt it. Gently warm the cream over low heat, then whisk in the melted sugar. Remove from the heat, cool quickly, and whip to soft peaks.
For the candied peanuts, bring 950 ml water and 800 g of the sugar to a boil over medium heat. Add the peanuts and boil for 4 minutes. Drain, then toss in the remaining sugar.

Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C. Shake the excess sugar from the peanuts and deep-fry for 2 minutes, or until golden. Remove with a slotted spoon, spread in a single layer on a baking sheet, and season with flaky sea salt.
To assemble, place a scoop of coconut ice cream in each dish. Top with the whipped cream, toasted coconut, and candied peanuts. Decorate with a wafer and serve.

recipes.searchText: Coconut Sundae with Palm Sugar Whipped Cream and Sweet and Salty Peanuts 4 large scoops coconut ice cream 4 tablespoons freshly grated coconut meat, toasted 4 coconut butter cookie wafers 85 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 475 ml heavy (double) cream For the candied peanuts Canola (rapeseed) oil, for deep-frying 1 kg granulated sugar 300 g peanuts Flaky sea salt For the whipped cream, briefly microwave the palm sugar in a heatproof bowl to melt it. Top with the whipped cream, toasted coconut, and candied peanuts. Decorate with a wafer and serve.

recipes.title: Broiled Beef Salad with Mangosteen and Chili Mint Dressing

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dressing
lines: 11⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 teaspoon unrefined superfine (caster) sugar Fish sauce, to taste
2-3 tablespoons coconut cream Fresh fruits and vegetables, such as cabbage, mint sprigs, green beans, and small purple apple eggplants, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the dressing, pound the garlic, mint, chiles, and shrimp paste to a very fine paste. Add both sugars and fish sauce to taste, followed by the lime juice and coconut cream. The dressing should be hot, sour, salty, pleasantly sweet, and strongly fragrant with mint.
Preheat the broiler (grill) to high. Broil the beef for 3-5 minutes on both sides, or until medium-rare. Let rest, then slice.

Put the mint, cilantro, shallots, lemongrass, and mangosteen in a bowl. Add a generous amount of dressing and toss lightly. Add the beef, drizzle over a little more dressing, and finish with the kaffir lime leaves. Serve with the fruits, vegetables, and a sprig of mint.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Pork with Santol

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 11⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar Fish sauce, to taste
4 red and green chiles, seeded and sliced lengthwise A squeeze of lime juice

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the paste, pound the cilantro roots, chiles, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste to a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-low heat. Add the paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pork, increase the heat slightly, and cook for 1-2 minutes, until almost cooked. Season with the sugar and a little fish sauce, then add enough broth to loosen the mixture.

Add the santol, kaffir lime leaves, and chiles and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat. Finish with lime juice. It should taste hot, sour, and equally sweet and salty; adjust the seasoning and serve.

recipes.searchText: Stir-Fried Pork with Santol 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 200 g pork neck, sliced 11⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar Fish sauce, to taste 50-100 ml light chicken broth (stock) 150 g santol 4 kaffir lime leaves, torn 4 red and green chiles, seeded and sliced lengthwise A squeeze of lime juice 2 cilantro (coriander) roots 5-10 red bird's-eye chiles 5 Thai shallots 5 garlic bulbs 1⁄2-1 tablespoon shrimp paste For the paste, pound the cilantro roots, chiles, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste to a coarse paste. Heat the oil in a wok over medium-low heat. Add the paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant. Add the pork, increase the heat slightly, and cook for 1-2 minutes, until almost cooked. Season with the sugar and a little fish sauce, then add enough broth to loosen the mixture. Add the santol, kaffir lime leaves, and chiles and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat. Finish with lime juice. It should taste hot, sour, and equally sweet and salty; adjust the seasoning and serve.

recipes.title: "Yam" Meringue with Beef Tartare and Herbs
recipes.subtitle: Henrik Yde-Andersen, Sra Bua by Kiin Kiin

ingredientGroups.heading: For the meringue
lines: 200 g confectioners' (icing) sugar fish sauce, to taste lime juice, to taste

ingredientGroups.heading: For the tartare fish sauce, to taste
lines: 200 g very fresh beef tenderloin or mignon fillet, finely chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Beat the egg whites in a large bowl, slowly adding the confectioners' sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice until the mixture has balanced sweet-and-sour flavor and forms stiff peaks.
Process the chile in a small food processor or spice grinder until smooth, then fold it into the meringue. Set aside.
For the tartare, combine the fish sauce and beef in a bowl. Cover and marinate for 5 minutes.
Arrange the meringue in a bowl, add the beef to one side, sprinkle with the shallot and herbs, and serve.

recipes.searchText: "Yam" Meringue with Beef Tartare and Herbs Henrik Yde-Andersen, Sra Bua by Kiin Kiin 2 egg whites 200 g confectioners' (icing) sugar fish sauce, to taste lime juice, to taste 2 large green chiles, seeded 200 g very fresh beef tenderloin or mignon fillet, finely chopped 2 shallots, finely chopped 8 cilantro (coriander) stems 8 Thai cilantro (coriander) stems 8 mint leaves Beat the egg whites in a large bowl, slowly adding the confectioners' sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice until the mixture has balanced sweet-and-sour flavor and forms stiff peaks. Process the chile in a small food processor or spice grinder until smooth, then fold it into the meringue. Set aside. For the tartare, combine the fish sauce and beef in a bowl. Cover and marinate for 5 minutes. Arrange the meringue in a bowl, add the beef to one side, sprinkle with the shallot and herbs, and serve.
